# Common Practice foundation review

This is a local design review of TaxKit at
`f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`, Common Practice at
`54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7`, and the published Commonplace
development-workflows scaffold `0.6.11`. Application changes and dependency
upgrades require final agreement after this review.

```text
Website server/browser -> API transports -> calculation service -> rules/core
Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP ----> API transports -> calculation service -> rules/core
Local SDK --------------------------------> calculation service -> rules/core
Alchemy ----------------> matching Website/API for each stage
```

Reuse order: preserve tax and package contracts; reuse app and host composition;
improve checked shared clients; qualify versions and patches; consolidate
tooling; then propose operational logging and metrics without enabling them.

## Scope and authority

Investigation and local review documents only. No application implementation,
dependency upgrade, provider change, secret change, deployment, publication,
billing change or analytics collection is authorised. Common Practice stays
read-only. GitHub Actions is out of credits; all checks for this review run
locally. Local results do not prove deployed behaviour or tax correctness beyond
the checked cases.

The [earlier clean-slate plan](../exec-plans/active/clean-slate-foundation.md)
remains active. The integrated 81 pull-request heads and
[merge receipt](../documentation-audit/clean-slate-foundation/2026-10-08-merge-all.json)
do not close its remaining tasks. This review is a candidate successor for
agreed design corrections, not permission to reopen completed tasks or rewrite
historical proof.

## Interview record

| Question | State | Answer and consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1 Website HTTP or RPC | Open | Cooper asked to decide after the full comparison. Preserve current RPC behaviour while investigating. |
| Q2 Supported hosts | Settled | Keep Bun and Cloudflare; shared packages remain independent of either host. Thoroughly check upstream Effect and Alchemy support. [Decision](../adr/0003-support-independent-api-hosts.md). |
| Q3 Operational fields | Settled | Safe operational fields only; no salaries, facts, results or calculation traces. [Decision](../adr/0004-limit-operational-observations.md). |

No proposed correction is accepted for implementation yet. The structured
[scope](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/audit-scope.json),
[findings](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/audit-findings.json)
and [empty implementation crosswalk](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/accepted-findings.json)
are the audit owners. The dated inventories account for 795 documentation and
README paths: 737 readable files and 58 retained binary evidence files. Current,
affected and contradictory owners receive deeper reading; inventory counts
alone do not establish semantic correctness.

## Intended base and justified differences

| Area | Reuse from Common Practice and scaffold | TaxKit difference to keep |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apps | Separate Website and API; one frontend server runner; one React-mounted Atom graph; typed private server calls and checked public browser address | Support both Bun and Cloudflare hosts. Preserve the no-JavaScript tax form and its checked submission data. |
| Domain | One owner for Schemas, operations, errors and live/test service implementations; transports depend inward | Core, calculators and Australian rule packages are real separate capabilities. Do not replace them with a single generic domain package. |
| Package layout | Explicit exports and ownership-based files | Keep nested `packages/api/*`, `packages/rules/au/*` and `packages/sdk/typescript` unless a separately evidenced move simplifies ownership. A folder rename alone gives no benefit. |
| Distribution | Source, declaration, default and actual packed-export checks | TaxKit compiles packages and prepares a dist-only SDK. Common Practice's source-only private packages do not establish distributable-package compatibility. All current TaxKit manifests remain private; no publication is established. |
| Clients | Native generated clients stay private behind named checked operations | Local calculator/SDK errors must not be widened with network failures. Preserve the existing checked RPC contract; add a checked HTTP contract alongside legacy public helpers. |
| Requests | Native Worker request execution and request-owned cleanup; no backend Promise runner | Preserve ten-second full RPC reply limit, 2 MiB response cap, five-second calculation work limit, eight calculation places per composed isolate and trusted private rate identity. A timer cannot pre-empt synchronous calculation work. |
| Tools | Shared command contract, strict lint, format, types, tests, build and unused-code checks | Keep release orchestration, the fixed ten-artifact release train, source/declaration/default export modes, staged packing and clean downstream consumers. Common Practice's smaller app-only command graph is insufficient. |
| Skills | Refreshed published plugin and local profiles | TaxKit's `docs/skills.md` forbids copied shared instructions. Do not reinstall the scaffold's copied-skill trees. First move any required executable lint asset to a code owner with provenance, then retire duplicate instructions. |
| Deployment | Native Alchemy stack, same-stage pair, own origin from Worker.URL and other host address from a resource Output | Preserve stable resource/state identities, exact Website Origin admission, stage-specific rate counters, stricter secrets policy and separately reviewed provider operations. Newer Alchemy does not contain every TaxKit fix. |

Common Practice source references: `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts`,
`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts`,
`apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts`, `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts`
and package manifests. Scaffold references: `repo-structure/references/tanstack-effect.md`,
`repository-contract.md`, `tooling-and-docs.md`, and sibling package contracts.
These are reference implementations, not current TaxKit runtime proof.

## Important corrections and optional simplification

This view follows the structured register. Stable finding IDs remain unchanged
when Cooper accepts, rejects or defers a correction.

| ID | Consequence and earliest owner | Proposed correction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FINDING-001 | An upgrade can restore swallowed provider errors or break the reciprocal Website/API origin graph. Root versions, patches and native graph own this. | Keep the locked baseline; reject an unpatched drop-in upgrade; qualify each patch and candidate against the actual graph. |
| FINDING-002 | RPC owns a Cloudflare-specific address trust rule. API/Website host ingress should own it. | Move edge-header interpretation to the Cloudflare adapter and supply checked keys to shared admission contracts. Keep the trusted private channel. |
| FINDING-003 | The HTTP client exposes its generated client and a generic callback helper. `packages/api/http/src/client` owns the correction. | Add named operations, safe errors, a checked address and whole-reply limits. Keep old exports as compatibility adapters. |
| FINDING-004 | Current summaries still describe the old docs app, starter Website or pre-merge handoff. The documentation routing/lifecycle owner comes first. | Link to current owners, refresh affected summaries and retain dated history. Do not mark remaining clean-slate tasks complete. |
| FINDING-005 | Copied shared instructions conflict with latest-plugin routing; lint uses an asset from a retained copy. `docs/skills.md` and `tools/oxlint` own this. | Separate qualified executable rule assets from shared instructions, retain provenance and remove copies only after consumers move. |
| FINDING-006 | Existing workspace checking covers crossings between `src` trees rather than every public-export boundary. `tools/oxlint/package-rules.ts` owns this. | Adapt the scaffold's manifest-aware checks for nested workspaces and prove root/config/app/package cases through the actual lint command. |
| FINDING-007, optional | Handwritten private Website transports add lifetime and conversion code. Website binding and API host adapters own this. | Prefer native Alchemy Bridge where equivalent trust, cancellation and response consumption are proved. HTTP/RPC choice remains open. |

Declared non-defects: exported telemetry and PostHog are intentionally deferred;
the placeholder UI package need not become a runtime package; a Bun host need
not have Cloudflare-specific services; compiled packages and tax-specific limits
are justified differences. No new generic helpers, duplicate docs renderer or
second permanent audit system is proposed.

## Complete call paths

**Browser calculation.** The page container mounts the existing Atom command.
The checked public address supplies a scoped native RPC client. It encodes
revision-four inputs, reads and decodes the complete bounded reply and releases
the receive loop. The API RPC handler calls `PublicCalculatorService`; the
catalogue checks facts and supplies the selected Australian rule/scenario layers
to Core. Core returns a report and calculation diagnostics. The reply reaches
the same Atom state, and the leaf renders readonly values. Editing/unmounting
interrupts pending browser work. Owners: `apps/web/src/lib/calculator-page.container.tsx`,
`calculator.atoms.ts`, `packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts`,
`packages/calculators/src/catalog.ts` and `packages/core/src/engine/live.layer.ts`.

**Server form.** Website `src/server.ts` bounds and checks the POST and calls its
server service. The private binding-only `calculatorRequest` sends the checked
original connection identity separately from JSON. The API buffers the reply
before its native method scope ends. Website encodes checked success/failure as
plain submission data for the page. This supports the no-JavaScript form without
a second engine. Current private `toRpcAsync` cannot carry an AbortSignal:
cancellation stops waiting locally, while remote work remains bounded. Do not
claim immediate remote cancellation. Owners: Website `lib/live.server.layer.ts`
and API `worker.application.ts`.

**HTTP machine caller.** HTTP API declarations decode the URL, query and body
with calculator-owned Schemas. The handler calls the same service and preserves
the current HTTP status/error envelope. Streamed ingress is capped at 64 KiB
within five seconds. The generated client shares those declarations, but its
existing public helper has no owned complete-read deadline or response-byte
policy. That is FINDING-003, not a reason to change tax calculations. Owners:
`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts`, `handlers/calculators.ts`,
`request-boundary.ts` and `client/*`.

**Local SDK.** This is an in-process library, not an HTTP SDK. The caller chooses
a typed calculator descriptor, the SDK constructs checked request values and
calls the same service. Effect callers own their provided services and lifetime.
The plain Promise-facing SDK privately owns independent client runtimes, waits
for cleanup on close and scopes one-shot calls. This runtime is justified by its
public library contract; it is not another API runner. Owners:
`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts`, `live.layer.ts` and `client.runtime.ts`.

**Remote MCP.** API-owned tool definitions reuse calculator/content Schemas;
`taxkit_calculate` calls the same captured service and returns fixed safe failure
guidance. Modern requests preserve request/key/signal ownership instead of
retaining the first caller's context. Legacy MCP sessions use a Cloudflare
Durable Object with bounded scope, concurrency and alarm expiry. Replies are
fully consumed within request scope and reply limits. In-process interruption
does not prove immediate real-network cancellation: the documented modern
pre-response path can rely on the five-second work budget. Owners:
`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts`, `mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts`,
`mcp-response.boundary.ts`, `mcp-session.layer.ts` and `worker.application.ts`.

## Website HTTP and RPC choice

| Choice | Benefit | Cost or limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep Website RPC | Retains checked errors, reply budgets and existing form/browser proof; smallest compatibility change | Keeps native RPC receive-loop and private binding conversion code; private calculator method cannot carry a signal remotely |
| Use HTTP clients over native Bridge | Matches Common Practice's Website and the scaffold; native conversion reduces handwritten transport work | First needs named checked HTTP operations, complete-reply limits, all docs discovery operations and an equally trusted private caller key. Plain forwarded headers are not sufficient |

Both choices keep HTTP/OpenAPI, public RPC and MCP contracts for their existing
callers, and leave the local SDK unchanged. Common Practice's Website uses typed
HTTP services; its RPC client is not its chosen Website transport. Its content
image timeout and permissive browser CORS are unsuitable defaults for anonymous
tax calculations. TaxKit's per-operation RPC acquisition is deliberate: copying
a once-acquired receive loop can retain the earlier Worker request lifetime.

Recommendation: retain Website RPC while adopting the shared app ownership and
checked-client base. Consider HTTP later only after an equivalent private
identity/cancellation path passes. This avoids coupling structural reuse to a
transport rewrite; the same checked HTTP correction is needed either way.

## Two hosts without host-specific packages

Shared tax, HTTP and RPC source currently imports no Alchemy, Cloudflare runtime,
Bun/Node providers or Effect runners. Host-specific header interpretation in
FINDING-002 is still a policy ownership issue even without a provider import.

Reuse a host-neutral application route/service composition within `apps/api`.
Bun provides its server and configuration; Cloudflare provides its native
request, binding, rate and session services. Keep the single Bun top-level runner
and the native Worker incoming Effect execution. Shared packages define checked
operations and handlers, never start a runtime or construct another managed
runner. Exact upstream support and limitations are recorded in the version and
infrastructure readout before adoption.

Bun currently serves HTTP; Cloudflare additionally serves RPC and MCP. Q2 does
not silently promise equal protocol coverage or a Bun replacement for Durable
Objects. The next interview round must decide supported surfaces before a
common composition is specified. MCP tool definitions should move to a package
only if there is a real shared consumer; the page's browser tools coordinate
form state and are not identical to a remote calculation tool.

## Compatibility constraints

Additive named clients and compatibility re-exports are the default. Removing
existing package names, public subpaths, constructor aliases or the callback
client helper is a breaking change and requires explicit separate approval.
Changing HTTP status/envelopes, RPC revisions, MCP protocol/session support,
schema encodings or public error unions is also breaking. A physical move must
keep the export and import contract stable. No such change is accepted here.

Keep TaxKit's staged-manifest packing: `publishConfig.exports` alone does not
prove npm or Bun rewrites the tarball. Keep the fixed release train and Changeset
rules. This design-only slice changes no package-facing contract, so it needs
no Changeset; each accepted implementation slice must assess one.

rules. This design-only slice changes no package-facing contract, so it needs

# TaxKit documentation

This is the sole router for maintainer-document type, lifecycle, truth layers,
and semantic ownership. Root `README.md` is the public repository entry point;
`AGENTS.md` is the short task map; `docs/architecture/README.md` is the current
architecture route. Public documentation content is a separate product surface
owned by the replacement `apps/web`, backend content contracts and docs
packages. The old `apps/docs` workspace is retired. Its tombstone routes to the verified
source bundle and dated provider recovery records; no provider operation is
authorised by that retained history.

## Truth layers

Use the strongest applicable owner and link rather than copy:

1. External systems own their current external state at readback time.
2. Code, configuration, Schemas, package exports, workflows, and generated
   sources own desired/executable state.
3. Architecture and standards own durable boundaries and enforceable policy.
4. Dated proof/evidence owns one artifact/environment/authority observation and
   its limitations.
5. Active SPEC/tasks and execution plans own current implementation intent.

Provider/registry output cannot grant authority. Completed plans are history.
Local release checks do not prove npm publication or external consumers.

## Metadata and lifecycle

New or materially revised maintainer docs separate `document_type`,
`lifecycle`, `authority`, and `owner`. Current durable docs also record
`last_reviewed` and `review_trigger`; superseded/tombstone docs record a
successor and reason.

Lifecycle values are `proposed`, `current`, `implemented`, `superseded`,
`historical`, `evidence`, `reference`, `failed`, `inconclusive`, `tombstone`,
and `archived`. Authority values are `canonical`, `supporting`, `generated`,
and `external`. Legacy `status: canonical` is an authority marker, not a
lifecycle; migrate it only when its owner is materially revised.

## Routes

| Need | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Architecture | [`architecture/README.md`](architecture/README.md) | Current architecture route. `architecture.md` is a tombstone only. |
| Standards | [`standards/README.md`](standards/README.md) | Current durable engineering/documentation rules. |
| Current intent | [`product-specs/index.md`](product-specs/index.md) and [`exec-plans/active/README.md`](exec-plans/active/README.md) | Only genuinely active work; implemented/history stays inventory. |
| Completed history | [`exec-plans/completed/README.md`](exec-plans/completed/README.md) | Historical provenance, never default policy. |
| Public docs product | [`../apps/web/README.md`](../apps/web/README.md), [`../packages/docs-content/README.md`](../packages/docs-content/README.md), and [`../packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md`](../packages/docs-fumadocs/README.md) | Consumer-facing content/runtime, not maintainer lifecycle policy. |
| Repeatable release/deployment/recovery operations | [`runbooks/README.md`](runbooks/README.md) and [`operations/authority-model.md`](operations/authority-model.md) | Exactly five target-owned procedures; stop consequential operations when principal, candidate, target or receipt is unknown. |
| CI controls and recurring automation | [`standards/controls.md`](standards/controls.md) and [`operations/automation-register.md`](operations/automation-register.md) | Quality workflow admission, release-graph controls, and report-only candidate boundaries; neither route grants external authority. |
| Verification/critical journeys/proof | [`architecture/testing-and-quality.md`](architecture/testing-and-quality.md), [`verification/critical-journeys.json`](verification/critical-journeys.json), [`evidence/releases/HGI-203-critical-journeys.json`](evidence/releases/HGI-203-critical-journeys.json), [`evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json`](evidence/releases/HGI-203-local.json), and [`documentation-audit/HGI-203-validation.json`](documentation-audit/HGI-203-validation.json) | The current inventory owns evolving journeys. Accepted HGI-203 retains the exact historical five-journey snapshot and bounded local proof that its immutable packet observed; HGI-204 validates both epochs without attributing current changes to the old attempt. Raw logs and secrets are never durable proof. |
| Harness foundation and requalification | [`verification/repository-harness-profile.json`](verification/repository-harness-profile.json), [`documentation-audit/harness-foundation/accepted-findings.json`](documentation-audit/harness-foundation/accepted-findings.json), [`verification/harness-epochs.md`](verification/harness-epochs.md), and [`verification/effectiveness.md`](verification/effectiveness.md) | The TaxKit profile, accepted HE crosswalk, content-addressed skill receipt and focused gate own the implemented baseline. Last accepted epoch `HFI-004-2026-07-24` qualifies saved candidate `7c8a96e`; HGI-206 remains previous history. The active clean-slate plan owns pending qualification of today's graph. Neither saved epoch establishes current-checkout or external state. |
| References | [`references/README.md`](references/README.md) | Revalidate mutable external guidance. |
| Audit/accounting | [`documentation-audit/README.md`](documentation-audit/README.md) | Dated evidence, not policy. |

Failed/inconclusive work retains provenance, last successful step, observed
state, escalation, resume trigger, recovery, and non-claims outside default
current routes. Do not delete or move historical/public/binary evidence without
an approved retention manifest.

## Maintenance

Every material slice decides `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A` for docs,
READMEs, architecture, standards, public/generated references, runbooks,
proof/evidence, skills, lint/config/CI, and active SPEC/tasks. Update the
earliest durable owner and necessary pointers in the same slice. Counts prove
accounting only; semantic and consumer claims need owner review and
boundary-matched proof.

Use the plugin `development-workflows:docs-maintainer` skill for this impact decision on
both PRD and ordinary changes. `$docs-writer` is limited to public-copy wording
after the maintenance route has selected the owner; it cannot close lifecycle,
generated-content, package, proof, or validation work. Background freshness
scans produce report-only candidates and cannot publish policy or documentation
without separately attached implementation authority, review and publication
identity.

`bun run check:docs` enforces the mechanical owner contract in
[`../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`](../tools/documentation/owner-policy.json).
It checks maintainer metadata, links, documented commands, workspace README
coverage, public/maintainer separation, accepted public-status representation,
and generated-source edges with bounded diagnostics and a JSON detail receipt.
The command accepts `--json`; failed checks return a nonzero exit after the
report is saved. Effect CLI owns option parsing.
`draft` means authored, locally renderable, visibly labelled candidate content;
`published` means explicitly accepted current public documentation. Neither
status proves runtime or external availability.

Acceptance-record Schemas live in `@taxkit/content`. The docs tool explicitly
selects source exports so it can run in a fresh checkout before package builds.
Version-two records include the reviewed source hash, which this check verifies;
version-one records retain their historical contract. The local accepted
catalogue builder, `bun run docs:catalogue`, requires version two, checks source
bytes before and after compilation, and writes generated output only when
accepted pages and matching navigation exist. It does not accept pages or
establish publication by running. See
[`../packages/docs-content/README.md`](../packages/docs-content/README.md).

`bun run check:runbooks` Schema-decodes the canonical runbook contract, the
current journey inventory and the exact historical HGI-203 journey snapshot,
then reconciles the immutable packet digest, four Markdown owners, commands,
evidence paths, stop operations, index rows and authority rows. It writes only
the ignored bounded receipt `tmp/runbook-validation-report.json`, executes none
of the documented procedures and establishes no consequential state.

Shared development workflows: [latest plugin and repository profiles](skills.md).

## Native cleanup and rollback limits

Common Practice's dated native-cleanup evidence was gathered on beta.79/Effect rc.117. It reports explicitly approved removal of two retired direct uploader bindings, worker readback, native destinations enabled, a no-op plan and bounded Axiom queries. It is historical hosted proof, not current beta.81/4.0.2 hosted proof: `/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/docs/evidence/observability/2026-10-06-native-cleanup.md:8`, `:60`, `:81`. Counts were 119 Website/514 API logs and 120 Website/332 API root spans in its chosen query window; a limit-1000 query is not an exhaustive export or proof of every parent relationship. No uploader secret in code is not proof an old token was revoked.

The older ADR `docs/adr/0001-production-owned-observability.md:3` says the design avoids a third deployment stack, while current source has separate Axiom and export stacks. Follow current source plus the dated evidence, not that stale sentence.

Alchemy `retain` prevents a provider delete while dropping the managed state row. Exact source: `/private/tmp/taxkit-review-alchemy-beta81/packages/alchemy/src/RemovalPolicy.ts:5`. It does not preserve a rollback snapshot. CP Production Worker retention therefore differs from TaxKit's current Worker deletion policy and cannot be adopted by assumption.

TaxKit retains Production zone/DNS ownership but Preview has no zone/domain declaration: `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts:109`. Its old Docs entrypoint is a retirement marker and retained resource history; do not point it at a new stack name and assume authority/state follows. Restore reviewed source, lockfile and patches locally; any later hosted rollback needs the exact approved artifact/source, old resource identities and provider readback. Existing authority and rollback owners are `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md:200`, `:242` and `docs/operations/authority-model.md`.

## Ready decisions and next proof

1. Keep both hosts, already agreed. Let each host supply services; keep provider names/types outside shared contracts.
2. Keep the current dependency baseline for this review. Later choose one exact aligned candidate and retain/adapt both Alchemy fixes, plus decide the Atom peer mismatch treatment. No upgrade is authorised now.
3. Preserve TaxKit's safe logging. The safe operational field decision already agreed by the user must have checked schemas and explicit host composition. Choose TaxKit-owned Preview/Production monitoring separation and sampling/persistence before any collection is enabled.
4. Keep hosted Doppler custody and isolated local composition. Optional local-only `.env` override is a separate small choice; do not inherit Common Practice's hosted override.
5. Move the accepted current stage schema away from the old Docs deployment file without changing stage values, physical names or stored identities.
6. Keep cleanup as a named separate operation. Confirm actual native removal support, classify the exact plan and read back old bindings/resources/tokens before claiming retirement. Retained resources and historical evidence remain explicit owners.

Later implementation proof should run in order: source/version/patch review; pure package and packed-consumer tests; mocked create/no-op/update graph plus forbidden-read no-PUT fixtures; Bun and Worker HTTP/error/cancellation/stream checks; emitted Worker and browser checks; exact approved Preview plan/apply/readback and observed safe records; then separately approved Production work with exact rollback identity. Passing local checks is not a deployment receipt.

## Paths read

TaxKit: `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `docs/README.md`, `docs/skills.md`, `docs/architecture/README.md`, `docs/architecture/effect-services.md`, `docs/architecture/deployment.md`, `docs/operations/authority-model.md`, `docs/runbooks/docs-deployment.md`, package infrastructure README, selected skill profiles, `alchemy.apps.local.run.ts`, `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, `apps-secrets.boundary.ts`, `native-domains-provider.boundary.test.ts`, `cloudflare/website.ts`, patches listed above, `packages/api/rpc/src/host-telemetry.ts`, `packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts`, calculator admission, API index/server/worker/worker.application/worker-admission files, Website runtime.server, and matching installed Effect/Alchemy/Atom/package type/source files. Shared domain/package searches verified no Cloudflare/Alchemy imports in core, calculators, rules and shared HTTP source (excluding explanatory comments).

Common Practice: `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `alchemy.run.ts`, `alchemy.axiom.run.ts`, `alchemy.trace.run.ts`, `packages/infrastructure/src/secrets.ts`, `axiom/resources.ts`, `axiom/dashboards/{types,index,queries}.ts`, `cloudflare/{traces,zone}.ts`, `stacks/{addresses,trace-export,telemetry}.ts`, `runtime/request-observation.ts` and its focused owners, API deployment Worker, Website build/runtime/telemetry owners, `docs/runbooks/deployment.md`, ADR0001 and dated cleanup evidence, installed Effect/Alchemy/package source/types, Effect4.0.2 and PostHog patch sections.

# Reuse the three shared Axiom datasets

Cooper selected the existing shared logs, traces and metrics datasets because
the account is limited to three. TaxKit will reference Site's existing resources
and own its own scoped ingestion token, destinations, dashboards and identity
filters. Site keeps ownership and retention policy for the datasets.

Sharing preserves capacity for every project but makes exact project, app and
stage filters essential. Resource references and safe fields must be checked;
shared storage is not access isolation or proof that events were delivered.
PostHog remains the owner of minimal product traffic/calculator counts; Axiom
owns operational observations without tax inputs or results.

The detailed contract and qualification work are in
[the proposed rebuild SPEC](../product-specs/clean-slate-foundation.md).
Implementation awaits final shared understanding; provider changes require a
reviewed exact-resource plan and its separate authority.

# TaxKit documentation profile

Read this profile after `AGENTS.md` and `docs/README.md`. Paths and commands
below are repository-local; resolve the checkout with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.

## Owner map

| Change class                                        | Earliest owner and required pointers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Maintainer lifecycle, truth layers, archive routing | `docs/README.md`; architecture, standards, audit and active intent only when affected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Calculator rules, facts and schemas                 | owning `packages/calculators` or `packages/rules/**` source/README; relevant `docs/architecture/**`, SDK/API/public docs only when consumers change                                                                                                                                                                             |
| SDK exports and examples                            | `packages/sdk/typescript` source/export map and README; packed-consumer/downstream proof; `docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| HTTP/OpenAPI                                        | `packages/api/http/src/**` schemas and `src/openapi.ts`; generated snapshot `packages/api/http/__snapshots__/openapi.json` through `test:openapi`; `packages/api/http/README.md`, `apps/api/README.md`, and API/SDK architecture only when their contracts change                                                               |
| Public MDX/navigation/lifecycle                     | `packages/docs-content/content/**`, `packages/docs-content/navigation.json`, and `tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`; `published` requires one exact `public.statusDecision.acceptanceRecords` binding to a strict addressable record, with the durable lifecycle decision routed from `docs/documentation-audit/hgi-207/public-mdx-lifecycle.json` |
| Public docs runtime/generated Fumadocs              | `apps/web/README.md` and its accepted catalogue/private API presentation; `apps/docs/README.md` is a retirement tombstone routing verified original source and separately approved historical recovery; `packages/docs-content/source.config.ts`, `packages/docs-content/.source`, and `packages/docs-fumadocs`; regenerate/check through the owning commands and never hand-edit generated output                                                                                                               |
| Package/app roots                                   | owning package/app README, package ownership architecture, root routes only when discoverability changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Commands, CI, versioning and release readiness      | `package.json`, workflow/command owner, `docs/standards/versioning.md`, `docs/runbooks/README.md`, testing-quality architecture and proof owner                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Runbooks, authority, proof and history              | exactly five target-owned procedures routed by `docs/runbooks/README.md`; `docs/operations/authority-model.md`; `tools/documentation/runbook-contract.json`; sanitized `docs/evidence/releases/**`, `docs/evidence/deployments/**`, or dated `docs/documentation-audit/**`; preserve provenance and non-claims                             |
| PRD and implementation                              | target SPEC, sibling tasks and active plan; local `prd-writer`, `prd-review`, `prd-implementer` invoke this skill                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Public `published` needs an exact accepted record and one-to-one binding in
`tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`; its `targetPath` must equal the public
path. Navigation remains independently draft unless it receives its own exact
record and binding.
Generated source is authoritative over checked output. Repository evidence is
not provider, registry, deployment, public-site or consumer proof.

## Commands and boundaries

- Baseline documentation/path/skill checks: `bun run
check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks`, `bun run check:repository-paths`.
- Harness foundation checks: `bun run check:harness-governance:types`, `bun run
  test:harness-governance`, and `bun run check:harness-governance`. The runtime
  gate reads only repository-local profile, audit, receipt, skill, link, and
  critical-journey owners.
- Full local closeout: `bun run verification` and `git diff --check`.
- Current accepted content/runtime: `bun run docs:catalogue`, `bun run
  docs:validate`, and `bun run web:test:native-pair`. The latter freshly builds
  the native API/Website and owns the release `docs-browser` check. The old
  docs workspace/build/test selection and writer workflows are retired;
  `bun run check:docs-deployment` verifies original-source addressability and
  historical receipts without provider access.
- SDK package boundary: `bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk check-packed-artifact`
  and `bun run --filter=@taxkit/sdk validate:downstream` when applicable.
- Release evidence: `bun run release:check` is local proof only; versioning,
  publication and deployment remain separately authorized operations.
- Runbook contract: `bun run check:runbooks` is inspect-only and writes the
  bounded ignored `tmp/runbook-validation-report.json`; it never runs a
  documented procedure or establishes external state.

For each check, state its observable postcondition and what it does not prove.
Keep background freshness reports as candidates until an attached implementation
authority, responsible reviewer and separately named publisher accept them.

## Clean-slate compatibility and implementation

The local root manifest and lockfile select stable Effect 4.0.0 and TypeScript
7.0.2. Canonical skill templates may retain their upstream rc.117 qualification;
that reference snapshot does not downgrade TaxKit or prove an app/provider
migration. Check installed exports and the active clean-slate plan before use.

Shared workflow skills are selected through `docs/skills.md` from the latest
installed plugin. The removed local collection and its 0.6.1 receipt remain
historical evidence; they do not select today's plugin or qualify TaxKit's
stable dependency graph. Repository validators stay independent of a user's
plugin installation. Use the retained task receipts and direct source checks
for the implementation's current acceptance and limits. Use its task receipts for current acceptance; the
upstream skill receipt alone does not prove runtime behaviour.

# Reuse the three shared Axiom datasets

Cooper selected the existing shared logs, traces and metrics datasets because
the account is limited to three. TaxKit will reference Site's existing resources
and own its own scoped ingestion token, destinations, dashboards and identity
filters. Site keeps ownership and retention policy for the datasets.

stage filters essential. Resource references and safe fields must be checked;
shared storage is not access isolation or proof that events were delivered.

owns operational observations without tax inputs or results.

-## Compatibility constraints
+## Exact versions and retained fixes
+
+The [infrastructure research](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/infrastructure-readout.md)
+records receiving source, installed types, matching upstream clones and primary
+release information. This is a source and local-test comparison, not an upgrade.
+
+| Exact combination | Result for TaxKit |
+| --- | --- |
+| Effect family 4.0.0 + Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80 + committed patches | Locked baseline. Existing three mocked redirect-rule tests pass. Full local verification remains incomplete because emulator tests time out. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81 | Rejected as a drop-in upgrade. The same fixture passes two tests but fails the forbidden-read case: it reports success and performs a mocked replacement write. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + beta.81 with equivalent TaxKit fixes | Possible candidate only. Peer ranges permit it; the whole candidate is unqualified. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + patched beta.80 | Unqualified alternative; peer compatibility alone is insufficient. |
+| Effect 4.0.0-rc.118 + unchanged beta.80 or beta.81 | Stable `^4.0.0` peers do not admit this prerelease as a drop-in combination. |
+
+Two Alchemy fixes still matter. TaxKit catches only a checked absent redirect
+ruleset; upstream beta.81 catches every read failure. TaxKit also defers fresh
+and cyclic resource properties; upstream still resolves properties earlier.
+The latter matters because TaxKit's Website and API refer to each other's
+outputs. Common Practice's simpler graph cannot establish this behaviour.
+
+The Atom patch widens scheduler peer metadata only. Both Atom 4.0.0 and 4.0.2
+declare a scheduler range below React 19.3.0's resolved 0.28.0. A later version
+change needs its own exact patch or recorded exception and browser lifetime
+checks. Align Effect companion versions and the explicit node-shared override
+when qualifying a candidate; do not copy another project's MCP patch blindly.
+
+Upstream references were cloned at Effect `effect@4.0.2`, commit
+`269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691`, and Alchemy `v2.0.0-beta.81`, commit
+`e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e`. Effect's HTTP API builder captures
+shared services while its router supplies each current request scope. Bun
+supplies the abstract server. Alchemy's Worker bridge supplies the native
+request context and hands streamed-response cleanup to the consumer. It pins
+application construction once and resets failed cold starts. Worker isolate
+shutdown has no guaranteed cleanup hook: request cleanup must not depend on it.
+
+## Safe observations, stages and secrets
+
+Q3 permits checked operational fields only: project, app, checked stage, fixed
+route category, event, duration and safe failure category. Exclude tax inputs,
+facts, results, calculation traces, raw errors, arbitrary messages, query
+strings, caller addresses and request bodies. Fixed field names are not enough
+if their values can contain user data. Native platform records also need their
+own privacy review, including request URLs, before any export is enabled.
+
+Common Practice demonstrates native Cloudflare destinations for logs and
+traces, a scoped Axiom token, and dashboards. Its metrics token permission is
+idle: no custom request-latency metric writer is active. Cloudflare's
+[export documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/opentelemetry-export/)
+supports logs and traces but excludes infrastructure and custom metrics from
+this export path. An Alchemy metrics destination type does not prove provider
+support. Native request/error/CPU/wall-time metrics can remain in Cloudflare;
+wall time includes background work and is not exact visitor latency.
+
+Retain [the earlier three-dataset choice](../adr/0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
+unless Cooper revisits it. That choice references Site-owned physical datasets
+because of an account limit, with TaxKit-owned scoped token, destinations and
+dashboards. Do not replace those references with Common Practice's production
+stack names or silently assume new dataset capacity. Project/app/stage filters
+separate reports, not access. Current capacity, permissions, retention and
+sampling are unverified; this review enables nothing. PostHog stays postponed.
+
+Keep one checked current stage owner and preserve `prod`, `pr-N` and
+`dev_identity`, stable resource names and stored stack identities. Move its
+contract away from the retained Docs deployment owner when implementation is
+accepted. Both hosted apps use their matching stage's resource outputs and
+bindings. Local execution retains its separate stack/state and rate namespace.
+Shared monitoring destinations do not imply that Preview may call Production.
+
+Preserve TaxKit's Doppler project/configuration selection and disabled ambient
+application values. Common Practice allows `.env` overrides for hosted stages;
+TaxKit's current no-DotEnv policy is a justified stricter choice. Provider
+authentication remains separate. Resource retention is not a rollback snapshot:
+Alchemy can retain the provider object while dropping its managed state row.
+Any later cleanup or deployment needs exact resources, separate authority and
+readback through the existing runbook owners.
+
+## Proposed migration order and local proof
+
+The [active design plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
+names the owners, compatibility checks and rollback for each candidate slice.
+First agree transport and host coverage, then accept finding IDs. Refresh
+current documentation owners; qualify versions and preserved patches; improve
+shared checked clients and host composition; consolidate copied tooling assets;
+then qualify any proposed operational resources. This sequence preserves tax
+rules, public encodings, compiled exports and the local SDK throughout.
+
+The [validation receipt](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/validation.json)
+records bounded local results and failures. Tax checks passed 162 cases; SDK
+packing checked actual entry points. The native pair builds on retry, but five
+tests across four files time out, including the fixture waiting for API startup.
+These results leave native runtime qualification open. No timeout was widened,
+no application fix was made, and no current deployed-revision claim is made.
+
+Documentation impact is owned by the structured findings' surface maps and
+the [slice ledger](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/documentation-impact.json).
+Current summaries flagged by FINDING-004 remain candidate corrections until
+accepted. Historical evidence is preserved and is not rewritten as current proof.
+
+## Compatibility constraints

+| Accepted correction requirements/tasks | Pending | No finding accepted for implementation. Map stable IDs only after shared understanding. |
+
+## Candidate implementation sequence
+
+This table makes the next work reviewable; it grants no implementation or
+external authority. Keep each slice small enough to reverse independently.
+
+| Order | Owners and change | Required proof | Rollback |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | Resolve open choices in the proposal; accept/reject/defer FINDING IDs; record meaningful decisions and affected tasks | Fresh independent review; no contradictions between glossary, decisions, SPEC and structured findings | Restore exact design documents; keep dated evidence |
+| 2 | FINDING-004: current architecture/product/audit summaries and routes; preserve earlier clean-slate plan and historical receipts | Documentation impact route, `check:docs`, `check:runbooks`, addressable retained history | Restore affected summaries and pointers |
+| 3 | FINDING-001: root manifest/lock and patches, only if an exact candidate is separately accepted | Frozen install, matching installed source/types, forbidden-read no-write fixture, absent/existing fixtures, create/update/no-op reciprocal graph, browser lifetime, package and packed/downstream checks | Restore exact manifest, lock and patch bytes; reinstall frozen baseline |
+| 4 | FINDING-003: `packages/api/http/src/client`; named checked operations alongside old exports | Decode/error/deadline/byte-cap/cancellation checks; preserved HTTP statuses/envelopes and OpenAPI; source/declaration/default and packed consumers; Changeset assessment | Restore added client contract and compatibility adapters without removing legacy exports |
+| 5 | FINDING-002 and agreed host coverage: `apps/api` composition and ingress; calculator-owned admission contract; current stage contract | Bun and Worker serve the agreed operations through one service; trusted key cannot be forged; per-request cleanup/error/stream checks; no-JavaScript form and Atom cancellation; same-stage pair and isolated local checks | Restore host composition and stage imports while keeping resource/state identities |
+| 6 | FINDING-005/006: qualified executable lint assets under `tools/oxlint`; nested-manifest-aware public-export checking; copied instruction retirement | Actual lint command proves valid imports and rejects root/config/app/package crossings; strict policy parity, types, format, unused-code and path checks | Restore previous code asset/import and instruction routing; preserve provenance |
+| 7 | Optional FINDING-007: native private binding conversion after transport agreement | Equivalent trusted caller identity, whole-reply consumption, interruption and safe errors in emitted native pair; no extra runner | Restore current binding adapter and checked RPC service |
+| 8 | Separately accepted safe operations: infrastructure declarations and host composition; earlier shared-dataset decision retained unless revisited | Checked safe-field fixtures; platform URL/error privacy review; exact destination/token/stage permissions, sampling and retention design; logs/traces versus native metrics distinction | Leave collection off; restore declarations; later provider rollback uses its separately approved receipt |
+
+Every code slice needs focused checks and `bun run verification`; public
+package changes assess a Changeset. The current unresolved emulator failures
+must be diagnosed before a later slice claims native runtime qualification.
+Do not alter time limits merely to make those checks pass.
+
+Only after local agreement and qualification may a separate named operation
+request Preview plan/apply/readback. Production, tokens, dataset permissions,
+cleanup and publication each retain their existing authority requirements.
+This review runs none of those operations and creates no CI run.
*** End Patch"));

+The [infrastructure research](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/infrastructure-readout.md)
+records receiving source, installed types, matching upstream clones and primary
+release information. This is a source and local-test comparison, not an upgrade.
+
+| Exact combination | Result for TaxKit |
+| --- | --- |
+| Effect family 4.0.0 + Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80 + committed patches | Locked baseline. Existing three mocked redirect-rule tests pass. Full local verification remains incomplete because emulator tests time out. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81 | Rejected as a drop-in upgrade. The same fixture passes two tests but fails the forbidden-read case: it reports success and performs a mocked replacement write. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + beta.81 with equivalent TaxKit fixes | Possible candidate only. Peer ranges permit it; the whole candidate is unqualified. |
+| Effect family 4.0.2 + patched beta.80 | Unqualified alternative; peer compatibility alone is insufficient. |
+| Effect 4.0.0-rc.118 + unchanged beta.80 or beta.81 | Stable `^4.0.0` peers do not admit this prerelease as a drop-in combination. |
+
+Two Alchemy fixes still matter. TaxKit catches only a checked absent redirect
+ruleset; upstream beta.81 catches every read failure. TaxKit also defers fresh
+and cyclic resource properties; upstream still resolves properties earlier.
+The latter matters because TaxKit's Website and API refer to each other's
+outputs. Common Practice's simpler graph cannot establish this behaviour.
+
+The Atom patch widens scheduler peer metadata only. Both Atom 4.0.0 and 4.0.2
+declare a scheduler range below React 19.3.0's resolved 0.28.0. A later version
+change needs its own exact patch or recorded exception and browser lifetime
+checks. Align Effect companion versions and the explicit node-shared override
+when qualifying a candidate; do not copy another project's MCP patch blindly.
+
+Upstream references were cloned at Effect `effect@4.0.2`, commit
+`269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691`, and Alchemy `v2.0.0-beta.81`, commit
+`e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e`. Effect's HTTP API builder captures
+shared services while its router supplies each current request scope. Bun
+supplies the abstract server. Alchemy's Worker bridge supplies the native
+request context and hands streamed-response cleanup to the consumer. It pins
+application construction once and resets failed cold starts. Worker isolate
+shutdown has no guaranteed cleanup hook: request cleanup must not depend on it.
+
+## Safe observations, stages and secrets
+
+Q3 permits checked operational fields only: project, app, checked stage, fixed
+route category, event, duration and safe failure category. Exclude tax inputs,
+facts, results, calculation traces, raw errors, arbitrary messages, query
+strings, caller addresses and request bodies. Fixed field names are not enough
+if their values can contain user data. Native platform records also need their
+own privacy review, including request URLs, before any export is enabled.
+
+Common Practice demonstrates native Cloudflare destinations for logs and
+traces, a scoped Axiom token, and dashboards. Its metrics token permission is
+idle: no custom request-latency metric writer is active. Cloudflare's
+[export documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/observability/opentelemetry-export/)
+supports logs and traces but excludes infrastructure and custom metrics from
+this export path. An Alchemy metrics destination type does not prove provider
+support. Native request/error/CPU/wall-time metrics can remain in Cloudflare;
+wall time includes background work and is not exact visitor latency.
+
+Retain [the earlier three-dataset choice](../adr/0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
+unless Cooper revisits it. That choice references Site-owned physical datasets
+because of an account limit, with TaxKit-owned scoped token, destinations and
+dashboards. Do not replace those references with Common Practice's production
+stack names or silently assume new dataset capacity. Project/app/stage filters
+separate reports, not access. Current capacity, permissions, retention and
+sampling are unverified; this review enables nothing. PostHog stays postponed.
+
+Keep one checked current stage owner and preserve `prod`, `pr-N` and
+`dev_identity`, stable resource names and stored stack identities. Move its
+contract away from the retained Docs deployment owner when implementation is
+accepted. Both hosted apps use their matching stage's resource outputs and
+bindings. Local execution retains its separate stack/state and rate namespace.
+Shared monitoring destinations do not imply that Preview may call Production.
+
+Preserve TaxKit's Doppler project/configuration selection and disabled ambient
+application values. Common Practice allows `.env` overrides for hosted stages;
+TaxKit's current no-DotEnv policy is a justified stricter choice. Provider
+authentication remains separate. Resource retention is not a rollback snapshot:
+Alchemy can retain the provider object while dropping its managed state row.
+Any later cleanup or deployment needs exact resources, separate authority and
+readback through the existing runbook owners.
+
+## Proposed migration order and local proof
+
+The [active design plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
+names the owners, compatibility checks and rollback for each candidate slice.
+First agree transport and host coverage, then accept finding IDs. Refresh
+current documentation owners; qualify versions and preserved patches; improve
+shared checked clients and host composition; consolidate copied tooling assets;
+then qualify any proposed operational resources. This sequence preserves tax
+rules, public encodings, compiled exports and the local SDK throughout.
+
+The [validation receipt](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/validation.json)
+records bounded local results and failures. Tax checks passed 162 cases; SDK
+packing checked actual entry points. The native pair builds on retry, but five
+tests across four files time out, including the fixture waiting for API startup.
+These results leave native runtime qualification open. No timeout was widened,
+no application fix was made, and no current deployed-revision claim is made.
+
+Documentation impact is owned by the structured findings' surface maps and
+the [slice ledger](../documentation-audit/common-practice-foundation/documentation-impact.json).
+Current summaries flagged by FINDING-004 remain candidate corrections until
+accepted. Historical evidence is preserved and is not rewritten as current proof.
+

1:# Application call comparison — read-only evidence
5:## Shape and recommended reuse order
8:Website HTML / React forms      machine HTTP / RPC / MCP
23:Reuse the Common Practice native Website/API connection and single server runner as the app base; reuse its named client operations and closed errors; retain TaxKit's calculator/core/rules/SDK owners; preserve wire routes and exports with compatibility adapters; then qualify any replacement of the private calculation connection before retiring its current code. HTTP versus RPC for the Website is a design decision after this comparison, not an already settled correction.
25:## Concrete Website HTTP versus RPC comparison
27:| Concern | Common Practice / scaffold | Current TaxKit | Recommendation and consequence |
28:|---|---|---|---|
29:| Website server reads | Common Practice `ApiClientsLive` builds typed HTTP Content and Training clients over the native private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts:70-90`). Scaffold uses `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` then named domain client Layer (`repo-structure/assets/repository/apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts.tmpl:29-51`). | `WebsiteServerLive` builds calculator and docs RPC clients over matching private binding (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:33-208`). | HTTP can be the shared default base. Keeping RPC is also valid if the richer contracts and current proof justify it. Neither choice requires changing a tax rule. |
30:| Browser calls | Common Practice's browser WebMCP calls typed HTTP Content/Training services through checked API settings (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts:88-124`). Normal page loading uses TanStack server functions (`apps/web/src/lib/seo/page.functions.ts:13-29`). | React Atom owns calculator RPC calls to public POST `/rpc` (`apps/web/src/lib/calculator.atoms.ts:37-89`). Root checks and seeds configuration (`apps/web/src/routes/__root.tsx:49-91`). Docs use server functions instead of an independent browser backend. | Prefer one closed Website client contract independent of transport; either private HTTP/public HTTP or private RPC/public RPC may implement it. Keep direct public API calculation and same page-owned command state. |
31:| Private rate identity | Common Practice has content reads, no equivalent anonymous-tax calculation allowance in the inspected path. | TaxKit refuses forwarded Worker IP headers and sends the checked original connection identity through a private Worker method, separate from JSON (`packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts:11-20`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). | Necessary preservation. Plain binding fetch must not replace this method until it has an equally trusted identity path. A new checked HTTP client alone does not solve this. |
32:| Private cancellation | Native binding HTTP can carry an operation signal. Common Practice server entry forwards the request signal (`apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts:93-101`). | Calculator private `toRpcAsync` call explicitly cannot carry AbortSignal; local cancellation stops waiting, while server work remains bounded (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:60-73`). Docs byte-body binding fetch supplies a signal (`:174-180`). | HTTP has a simpler cancellable transport, but trusted identity and actual remote abort must both be proved. Keep the present limit stated until replacement proof exists. |
33:| Client service | Common Practice HTTP and RPC Layers implement the same Content service; generated native client is private (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:25-64`; `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:28-56`). | RPC has a checked named transport client (`packages/api/rpc/src/service.ts:22-54`). HTTP exposes the generated client and callback wrapper (`packages/api/http/src/client/index.ts:12-24`; `client/service.ts:5-17`). | Important correction: add named checked HTTP operations and keep old entrypoints as compatibility adapters. Do not simply widen the local SDK's error contract to transport errors. |
34:| Errors | Common Practice maps unavailable/invalid replies to Content-owned errors, retaining semantic failures (`packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:15-60`). | RPC projects private request failures to `CalculatorRpcRejected`, retains canonical capacity/rate/time errors, and adds transport errors (`handlers.ts:15-65`; `errors.ts:16-100`). HTTP generated client exposes HTTP/Schema errors and HTTP envelopes. | A checked Website-facing service should share safe named failures regardless of transport, while HTTP status/error bytes and RPC revision 4 stay unchanged. |
35:| Whole reply limits | Common Practice HTTP timeout wraps the complete native client operation (40 seconds due image rendering; `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts:31-59`, `content/src/service.ts:15-16`). | RPC is ten seconds including reply decode and cleanup, 2 MiB body cap, no automatic retry (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:55-85`; `response-budget.boundary.ts:12-53`; `schemas.ts:60-61`). HTTP helper has no owning complete-read deadline or byte budget (`client/index.ts:12-16`). | Important correction: supply full-read deadline, byte cap, invalid-reply failure and earlier caller cancellation for the new HTTP client. Keep TaxKit's ten-second budget; Common Practice's 40-second image budget does not fit tax calculation. |
36:| RPC receive loop lifetime | Common Practice RPC client is acquired once (`packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts:27-31`); it is not the Website's chosen transport. | TaxKit creates/releases each native RPC client in the named operation; retaining an earlier Worker request's receive loop can stall later requests (`packages/api/rpc/src/live.layer.ts:87-107`). | Preserve TaxKit's scope while RPC remains. Copying Common Practice's once-acquired RPC client into this Website would undo a deliberate request-lifetime fix. |
37:| Documentation reach | Common Practice HTTP Content has selected data/Markdown/SEO/image variants. | TaxKit RPC also has named discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown operations. Public HTTP currently has four content routes; discovery uses the private RPC operation (`packages/api/http/README.md:43-46`; `apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:145-150`). | HTTP-only Website needs a checked replacement for discovery too. Do not invent a second documentation renderer or source loader in Website. |
38:| SDK | Common Practice packages are private source-only. | TaxKit SDK is in-process, not a network client (`packages/sdk/typescript/package.json:4-5`; `src/effect.ts:91-117`; `live.layer.ts:1-9`). | Keep SDK contract, caller-owned lifetime, engine calculation and dist-only exports regardless of Website transport. A Website change has no reason to turn this into a remote SDK. |
40:Recommendation for the later transport round: use typed HTTP as the default app-base path once the named safe HTTP client and trusted private rate identity are qualified; retain public RPC for existing machine consumers. The alternative is to keep RPC for the Website, preserving its already explicit timeout/byte/cancellation/error policy, while still fixing the weaker HTTP client. This is optional simplification, not evidence that RPC calculations are wrong.
42:## Representative traces with exact owners
48:3. Remote HTTP calculation: native route group decodes URL/body/query with calculator-owned Schemas and preserves existing HTTP error/status envelopes (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:62-104`; handlers `:83-120`). The handler calls the same service; SDK is not in the server dependency path. Request body owner admits streamed 64 KiB within five seconds (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-83`). Private adapter sends native `/rpc` Request plus original checked identity to API binding-only `calculatorRequest` (`apps/web/src/lib/live.server.layer.ts:53-92`; `apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:213-239`). API buffers/bounds the JSON reply before the native method's event scope closes (`:241-275`). Website Schema-encodes success/failure into plain TanStack submission data (`server.ts:234-251`), root restores checked result, the page keeps no independent backend. Only plain report/form values enter request context. Changing this custom entry needs no-JavaScript, safe failure and response-consumption proof; it should not be removed just because Common Practice has no tax form.

3. Remote HTTP calculation: native route group decodes URL/body/query with calculator-owned Schemas and preserves existing HTTP error/status envelopes (`packages/api/http/src/groups/calculators.ts:62-104`; handlers `:83-120`). The handler calls the same service; SDK is not in the server dependency path. Request body owner admits streamed 64 KiB within five seconds (`packages/api/http/src/request-boundary.ts:33-83`). API composition shares the calculation service instance across HTTP and RPC. HTTP client generation uses the same API declarations, but its public helper currently leaves timeout and transport-failure ownership to each consumer.

4. Local SDK: caller-selected descriptor supplies calculator identity and input/report types; canonical context/query constructors precede calculator service call and selected report validation (`packages/sdk/typescript/src/effect.ts:71-117`). Default Layer supplies the same calculator service + Core engine (`live.layer.ts:1-9`). Plain clients have independent lazily started ManagedRuntime, stop pending work when closed, await cleanup; one-shot helpers own temporary Scope (`client.runtime.ts:66-75,95-173,177-225`). Effect callers keep their own service provision and lifetime. This is justified machinery for a Promise SDK, not a duplicate server runner.

5. Remote MCP: six app-owned toolkit definitions reuse canonical calculator/content inputs and replies (`apps/api/src/mcp.tools.layer.ts:24-90`). `taxkit_calculate` calls the captured calculator service and projects failures to fixed tool guidance (`:92-148`). The tool has explicit request cancellation that removes its AbortSignal listener and waits for losing work cleanup (`mcp-cancellation.boundary.ts:6-39`). Native API instance composes modern `2026-07-28` once; registration removes first caller's request/key/signal from retained context (`worker.application.ts:121-157`). Legacy `2025-11-25` sessions have a stage-owned Durable Object, ten-minute Scope with 32 initialisations/32 concurrent requests, native alarm expiry (`mcp-session.layer.ts:51-147`; `mcp.schemas.ts:4-8`). Reply JSON/SSE is fully read under request Scope, 2 MiB/ten seconds, no subscriptions/resumption (`mcp-response.boundary.ts:11-49`). Current documented modern real-network pre-response cancellation relies on the five-second work budget; do not describe in-process early interruption as remote cleanup proof (`docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md:720-727`).

content.text:
Q1 — After the full comparison, should the website keep RPC (typed remote function calls) during this refactor, or move to HTTP? I recommend keeping RPC for now: its reply checks, time/size limits and trusted caller identity are already explicit. HTTP needs equivalent protections and documentation discovery before it can replace that path. Both choices preserve the public HTTP/RPC APIs and local SDK.
- Keep website RPC for now (recommended)
- Move website calls to HTTP after equivalent protections pass

Q4 — What should the retained Bun API support? It currently serves HTTP; Cloudflare also serves RPC and MCP (the tool interface used by AI clients). I recommend preserving that coverage for this refactor while sharing the calculation service and host-independent code. Adding RPC/MCP to Bun needs its own session, rate-limit and cancellation checks.
- Keep Bun HTTP and current Cloudflare coverage (recommended)
- Add RPC and modern MCP to Bun as part of the design

---

# Keep Bun and Cloudflare as independent API hosts

Cooper agreed on 10 October 2026 that both the standalone Bun API and the
Cloudflare API remain supported. Shared calculation and transport packages must
work without knowing which host runs them. Each app host supplies its server,
configuration and platform services to the same checked operations.

Keeping two hosts costs additional host-specific checks, but allows callers to
run TaxKit outside Cloudflare without a second implementation of tax rules.
The [foundation review](../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
must check this against both upstream Effect and Alchemy sources and the
installed package types. This is an agreed design constraint, not proof that
both hosts currently expose identical features or that a deployment passed.
---
document_type: architecture-decision
lifecycle: current
authority: supporting
owner: taxkit-architecture-owner
last_reviewed: 2026-10-10
review_trigger: operational signal fields, collection destination or privacy policy changes
---

# Keep operational observations separate from calculation values

Cooper agreed on 10 October 2026 to allow only safe operational details in the
Axiom and Cloudflare logging and metrics design: fixed fields such as stage,
route, duration and safe error name. Salaries, calculation facts, results and
calculation traces are excluded. This makes operational diagnosis less detailed
but keeps financial circumstances out of the signal store.

The policy applies to platform-generated records as well as application logs.
URLs, request headers and raw errors need separate field-level review before
export because they can contain financial or identifying values. The
[foundation review](../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
will propose the exact field and destination contracts. It does not authorise
collection, provider configuration, secrets, billing or deployment. PostHog
remains postponed. The earlier [shared-dataset proposal](0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
retains its history; its destination and collection choices are not approved by
this decision.

# Fresh independent design review

Reviewed 10 October 2026, TaxKit branch codex/common-practice-foundation-review at f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442, with authorised document changes. This is a read-only independent review; no application, dependency, provider or test change was made.

## Important observation

The original proposal missed a concrete Bun lifetime difference. Bun serves TaxKitServerLayer (apps/api/src/server.ts:20-23; packages/api/http/src/server.ts:1-4), which exports ApiRoutesLive. That Layer uses HttpRouter.provideRequest for PublicCalculatorServiceBounded (packages/api/http/src/server/live.layer.ts:41-49). Installed Effect describes these as request dependencies and builds the Layer inside request middleware (node_modules/effect/src/http/HttpRouter.ts:1298-1319). The bounded service allocates Semaphore.make(8) during its construction (packages/calculators/src/work.layer.ts:38-49), so separate Bun requests receive separate pools. Cloudflare acquires and captures its bounded service once (apps/api/src/worker.ts:37-50; apps/api/src/worker.application.ts:87-116). Both use the five-second operation budget, while Bun lacks Cloudflare rate admission and uses permissive CORS. These policy differences must stay separate from the open choice about adding RPC/MCP to Bun.

The parent incorporated this as FINDING-008 in the structured register and proposal, with an overlapping-request proof in plan step 5. No runtime fix was made or accepted by this review.

## Small document corrections

The application readout's former APP-008 reference should be FINDING-002. The actual-slice impact ledger must classify the two new current ADRs and CONTEXT.md change as Change required, while preserving implementation architecture. Temporary log basenames and a locator make hashes useful provenance; the bounded receipt should retain the failed test names and reasons. Raw logs do not establish durable acceptance and need not be copied as repository proof.

## Reviewed conclusions

The ten-row Website HTTP/RPC comparison now distinguishes trust, cancellation, reply bounds, discovery, errors and current caller lifetime. Keeping Website RPC while adding a checked HTTP client independently is a reasonable proposal; Q1 remains a user decision. The documents preserve both hosts, tax rules, SDK lifetime and exports, existing encodings, the earlier three shared datasets and PostHog deferral. The accepted implementation crosswalk stays empty.

Matching Effect 4.0.2 and Alchemy beta.81 clone identities and cited source confirm the captured shared services/current request scope, native response lifetime, failed cold-start reset, broad redirect error catch, and early resource-property resolution. These source conclusions do not qualify an upgrade. The newer unpatched provider candidate remains rejected by the recorded mocked forbidden-read case.

No further material design defect was found within this review's focused scope. No new package, duplicate runtime, generic helper collection or permanent comparative evaluation system is needed.

## Proof limits

This review inspected source, draft documents, inventories and receipts. It did not repeat the parent's checks, run provider commands, broaden testing, inspect all 795 inventoried documents, or prove hosted behaviour. Corpus counts establish accounting only. The parent's tax/SDK results remain bounded recorded local evidence. Full verification and native runtime qualification remain incomplete due failed build/startup tests; the documents correctly avoid success claims. Final mechanical document checks and final candidate identity remain parent-owned closeout work.
