## Initial JavaScript and fonts

Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.

Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.

For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.

Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.

## React lifecycle

For subscriptions/streams:

- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
- scope to mount/route lifetime;
- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
- encode backpressure/sampling;
- update view state through a controlled adapter.

Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.

When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
An optional registration/subscription pattern is
`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
not required for purely synchronous local UI state.

Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
state or cleanup has a real owner.

at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.

Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.

# Cloudflare

## Contents

- [Ownership decisions](#ownership-decisions)
- [File ownership](#file-ownership)
- [Worker and asset semantics](#worker-and-asset-semantics)
- [Routes zones and domains](#routes-zones-and-domains)
- [Bindings and storage](#bindings-and-storage)
- [Website origin rules](#website-origin-rules)
- [Secrets](#secrets)
- [Observability](#observability)
- [State](#state)
- [Readback checklist](#readback-checklist)

## Ownership decisions

Declare which system owns each Cloudflare lifecycle:

- Worker or static-asset deployment;
- routes and custom domains;
- DNS/zone configuration;
- R2, D1, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, or Secrets Store;
- environment secrets and bindings;
- logs, metrics, traces, and observability destinations;
- remote state infrastructure.

Do not assume Alchemy owns all Cloudflare resources because it owns one Worker.

## File ownership

For a small graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts
```

For a substantial graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare/
  stack.ts
  website.ts
  worker.ts
  storage.ts
  routes.ts
  secrets.ts
  observability.ts
```

Keep stage/config Schemas outside provider declarations when other providers share them.

## Worker and asset semantics

Make asset routing policy explicit. In particular, distinguish asset-first and Worker-first behaviour and test the intended choice. A deployed Worker and green CI do not prove that static assets return the correct content type or bypass the Worker.

Test:

- root document;
- hashed CSS and JavaScript assets;
- missing assets;
- API paths;
- redirects;
- cache headers;
- content types;
- route precedence.

Record compatibility date, compatibility flags, runtime limits, module format, and bundler inputs in a stable typed owner. Keep application and deployment configuration aligned through one contract or an invariant test.

## Routes, zones, and domains

Treat a zone or domain as foreign unless this repository creates and owns it.

- Read the target zone before applying routes.
- Adopt only under explicit authority.
- Default adopted zones and routes to retain.
- Restrict Production route adoption to the Production stage.
- Reject a route whose account/zone does not match the authority record.
- Read back the route pattern and bound Worker after apply.
- Prove the public host independently.

Do not infer route correctness from a Worker URL.

## Bindings and storage

Model each binding as typed desired state:

- binding name;
- resource kind;
- physical resource identity;
- stage/environment;
- creation/adoption policy;
- removal policy.

Assert that application code and deployment configuration use the same binding names. For Durable Objects, include class name, migration/tag policy, and deployment sequencing. For R2/D1/KV, make data retention explicit and default destructive deletion to forbidden until authorised.

## Website origin rules

An origin is the protocol and host, with an optional port, such as
`http://127.0.0.1:3210`. The deployed host owns that address. Applications must
never hard-code it or build it from a stage, Worker name, account subdomain,
custom domain or development port.

For Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81`, use the native self URL binding on the host that
needs its own address:

```typescript
const website =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Website", {
    rootDir: "apps/web",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });

// The same binding works in a native Worker declaration.
const api =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Worker("Api", {
    main: "./src/worker.ts",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });
```

Alchemy resolves this binding to the local development proxy during local
development, the deployed `workers.dev` address, or the configured custom
domain. Do not add separate local/cloud address formulas or a copied-address
fallback. For Vite browser code, a `VITE_`-prefixed self URL binding uses the
same native resolution before the client bundle is built.

It is valid to declare a chosen custom domain as infrastructure input, for
example `domain: "app.example.com"`. Keep the application's own
`PUBLIC_ORIGIN` bound to `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`; do not repeat that domain in
its environment or build `"https://" + domain` there. Aliases and incoming
request origins are separate from the host's configured canonical address.

The native Effect Worker host supplies a ConfigProvider from its resolved
bindings. Application Layers consume the address with
`yield* Config.schema(OwnedOrigin, "PUBLIC_ORIGIN")` during runtime startup.
Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure route Layers, or read it while constructing an
existing service with `Layer.effect`. Reuse the host provider, owning Schema
and [general configuration pattern](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
instead of adding an address-only Context service. For a Website whose framework
does not supply that provider, use its existing narrow host adapter to check
owned bindings and pass only public settings to the browser.

Beta.79 also supports `yield* Cloudflare.Worker.URL` in native Worker
initialisation. That yield attaches the binding and returns a deferred Effect,
not the address string. Running the returned Effect requires the native
`RuntimeContext`, where the binding is populated. Check the phase and lifetime
before using this accessor; the explicit env binding plus checked Config is the
startup path above. Do not read runtime bindings during graph planning or add a
new runtime to obtain them.

For a different host, use that resource's native Output, such as `api.url`.
Pass the Output to the receiving resource; check its resolved value with the
owning Schema when application code reads the binding. If the native address
can be absent, preserve that absence as `null` for an env binding and reject it
with the Schema. Do not replace an absent Output with a guessed address.

Keep expected validation failures typed. Beta.79's `Output.mapEffect` callback
accepts no expected errors, so do not force Schema decoding into it with
`Effect.orDie`. `Output.map` may select a checked resource attribute or represent
absence; it must not reconstruct the hostname. Resolve and decode Outputs
separately before writing workflow or receipt values.

Check the selected Alchemy version's self URL, Vite, native Worker and local
provider APIs before copying this example. See the
[matching primary sources](../sources.md#cloudflare-website-origins).
Local source/type checks do not prove live domain routing.

## Separate Website and native API Workers

Use standard Website.Vite for the frontend and a native Effect Worker for the
API. The root stack deploys both with exact same-stage service/public bindings.
Preview has its own API; a Website preview parent does not authorise using the
Production API. Do not wrap TanStack in a backend Worker or recreate an API
runtime around the native incoming request fibre.

Check the installed Alchemy build/runtime mechanism before reading deployment
services in a Worker declaration. The qualified beta.81 runtime build guard
removes stack-only requirements from the uploaded entry. Test the real native
entry without those services, return from startup, then request and release
resources. A typecheck or successful upload alone does not prove startup.

Test browser CORS with the native client's actual headers and an actual browser
call. Tracing headers b3 and traceparent are part of the qualified client's
request; disabling tracing to avoid preflight is not a correction. Separate
remote MCP Origin validation from matching-origin Website WebMCP registration.

## Preview environments without provider patches

Check the installed ordinary Worker and Worker Preview providers separately.
A declared observability type or an existing Preview retaining earlier settings
does not prove that a newly created Preview receives those settings. Check both
create and update paths and read back a new deployment.

When required Preview settings lack native support, consider an ordinary
stage-owned Website Worker alongside its stage-owned API before patching the
provider. Keep exact stage names, self URL bindings and native log/trace
destinations. This changes the Preview URL and teardown owner; confirm that
tradeoff. For a mode change, use a distinct native resource identity, such as
`Namespace.push`, and inspect the create/delete plan so the former parent cannot
be overwritten. Preserve production identities and shared state.

Ordinary workers.dev Websites need their own indexing policy. Cloudflare's
[`_headers` file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/)
covers static assets; it does not cover Worker-generated replies. Apply the
checked stage policy through the existing framework response adapter, test
pages, errors, machine replies and assets, and keep production indexable.
Update CI addresses, Preview comments and trace queries for distinct Worker
names while preserving historical Preview records.

## Secrets

Prefer provider-managed secret references or Secrets Store bindings over plaintext workflow values.

- Acquire credentials through redacted Config.
- Validate secret binding names and stage.
- Never emit values in plans, logs, outputs, or receipts.
- Separate credential issuance from resource apply.
- Read back metadata or binding presence, never the secret.
- Revoke disposable credentials after lifecycle proof.

Removing a secret declaration may leave the old binding on the deployed Worker.
Check the active version's binding names and types; a no-change plan does not
prove removal. Prefer a supported native Alchemy deletion operation. If the
installed provider has none, record the residue and request an exact one-off
ownership exception before a provider write. Do not introduce a dependency
patch, custom resource or placeholder secret to conceal the gap. Keep shared
token revocation separate from binding removal. See the
[hosted telemetry cutover](../effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Observability

Cloudflare platform observability and application telemetry are separate sources.

For Cloudflare-native logs or destinations:

- identify Worker/service/environment/stage;
- define retention and sampling;
- read back the destination/binding;
- query the downstream provider.

For Effect OTLP export:

- keep endpoint/token in a redacted binding;
- decode the binding at application ingress;
- attach one exporter Layer to the runtime;
- preserve `waitUntil` or the host completion mechanism;
- test transport wiring;
- query Axiom independently before claiming ingestion.

## State

If Cloudflare backs Alchemy state, document bootstrap and recovery. Do not create a circular dependency between the state backend and the graph it stores. Use a separate bootstrap stack or a tested provider-supported mechanism where necessary.

Start with the installed native `Cloudflare.state()` setup and maintenance
behaviour. In the qualified beta.80 source, `--yes` permits automatic creation
and upgrades; pending setup can also be recovered. An existing-only rule is a
separate project choice. Check it before building a custom state client. Native
Website `domain.redirects` likewise has shared-list and failure semantics that
must be understood before promising stronger preservation. See
[native migrations](../operations/native-migrations.md#start-with-the-standard-behaviour)
and its pinned sources.

## Readback checklist

After apply, query the Cloudflare API for:

- account and zone identity;
- Worker/script/service name;
- deployment/version identifier where available;
- routes/domains;
- bindings and safe resource IDs;
- compatibility settings;
- observability configuration;
- storage resource presence.

Then run the public route/asset journey. Report any unavailable readback as a non-claim.

- [Website origin rules](#website-origin-rules)
- [Secrets](#secrets)
- [Observability](#observability)
- [State](#state)
- [Readback checklist](#readback-checklist)

## Ownership decisions

Declare which system owns each Cloudflare lifecycle:

- Worker or static-asset deployment;
- routes and custom domains;
- DNS/zone configuration;
- R2, D1, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, or Secrets Store;
- environment secrets and bindings;
- logs, metrics, traces, and observability destinations;
- remote state infrastructure.

Do not assume Alchemy owns all Cloudflare resources because it owns one Worker.

## File ownership

For a small graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts
```

For a substantial graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare/
  stack.ts
  website.ts
  worker.ts
  storage.ts
  routes.ts
  secrets.ts
  observability.ts
```

Keep stage/config Schemas outside provider declarations when other providers share them.

## Worker and asset semantics

Make asset routing policy explicit. In particular, distinguish asset-first and Worker-first behaviour and test the intended choice. A deployed Worker and green CI do not prove that static assets return the correct content type or bypass the Worker.

Test:

- root document;
- hashed CSS and JavaScript assets;
- missing assets;
- API paths;
- redirects;
- cache headers;
- content types;
- route precedence.

Record compatibility date, compatibility flags, runtime limits, module format, and bundler inputs in a stable typed owner. Keep application and deployment configuration aligned through one contract or an invariant test.

## Routes, zones, and domains

Treat a zone or domain as foreign unless this repository creates and owns it.

- Read the target zone before applying routes.
- Adopt only under explicit authority.
- Default adopted zones and routes to retain.
- Restrict Production route adoption to the Production stage.
- Reject a route whose account/zone does not match the authority record.
- Read back the route pattern and bound Worker after apply.
- Prove the public host independently.

Do not infer route correctness from a Worker URL.

## Bindings and storage

Model each binding as typed desired state:

- binding name;
- resource kind;
- physical resource identity;
- stage/environment;
- creation/adoption policy;
- removal policy.

Assert that application code and deployment configuration use the same binding names. For Durable Objects, include class name, migration/tag policy, and deployment sequencing. For R2/D1/KV, make data retention explicit and default destructive deletion to forbidden until authorised.

## Website origin rules

An origin is the protocol and host, with an optional port, such as
`http://127.0.0.1:3210`. The deployed host owns that address. Applications must
never hard-code it or build it from a stage, Worker name, account subdomain,
custom domain or development port.

For Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81`, use the native self URL binding on the host that
needs its own address:

```typescript
const website =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Website", {
    rootDir: "apps/web",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });

// The same binding works in a native Worker declaration.
const api =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Worker("Api", {
    main: "./src/worker.ts",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });
```

development, the deployed `workers.dev` address, or the configured custom
domain. Do not add separate local/cloud address formulas or a copied-address
fallback. For Vite browser code, a `VITE_`-prefixed self URL binding uses the
same native resolution before the client bundle is built.

example `domain: "app.example.com"`. Keep the application's own
`PUBLIC_ORIGIN` bound to `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`; do not repeat that domain in
its environment or build `"https://" + domain` there. Aliases and incoming
request origins are separate from the host's configured canonical address.

The native Effect Worker host supplies a ConfigProvider from its resolved
bindings. Application Layers consume the address with
`yield* Config.schema(OwnedOrigin, "PUBLIC_ORIGIN")` during runtime startup.
Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure route Layers, or read it while constructing an
existing service with `Layer.effect`. Reuse the host provider, owning Schema
and [general configuration pattern](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
instead of adding an address-only Context service. For a Website whose framework
does not supply that provider, use its existing narrow host adapter to check
owned bindings and pass only public settings to the browser.

Beta.79 also supports `yield* Cloudflare.Worker.URL` in native Worker
initialisation. That yield attaches the binding and returns a deferred Effect,
not the address string. Running the returned Effect requires the native
`RuntimeContext`, where the binding is populated. Check the phase and lifetime
before using this accessor; the explicit env binding plus checked Config is the
startup path above. Do not read runtime bindings during graph planning or add a
new runtime to obtain them.

For a different host, use that resource's native Output, such as `api.url`.
Pass the Output to the receiving resource; check its resolved value with the
owning Schema when application code reads the binding. If the native address
can be absent, preserve that absence as `null` for an env binding and reject it
with the Schema. Do not replace an absent Output with a guessed address.

Keep expected validation failures typed. Beta.79's `Output.mapEffect` callback
accepts no expected errors, so do not force Schema decoding into it with
`Effect.orDie`. `Output.map` may select a checked resource attribute or represent
absence; it must not reconstruct the hostname. Resolve and decode Outputs
separately before writing workflow or receipt values.

Check the selected Alchemy version's self URL, Vite, native Worker and local
provider APIs before copying this example. See the
[matching primary sources](../sources.md#cloudflare-website-origins).
Local source/type checks do not prove live domain routing.

## Separate Website and native API Workers

Use standard Website.Vite for the frontend and a native Effect Worker for the
API. The root stack deploys both with exact same-stage service/public bindings.
Preview has its own API; a Website preview parent does not authorise using the
Production API. Do not wrap TanStack in a backend Worker or recreate an API
runtime around the native incoming request fibre.

Check the installed Alchemy build/runtime mechanism before reading deployment
services in a Worker declaration. The qualified beta.81 runtime build guard
removes stack-only requirements from the uploaded entry. Test the real native
entry without those services, return from startup, then request and release
resources. A typecheck or successful upload alone does not prove startup.

Test browser CORS with the native client's actual headers and an actual browser
call. Tracing headers b3 and traceparent are part of the qualified client's
request; disabling tracing to avoid preflight is not a correction. Separate
remote MCP Origin validation from matching-origin Website WebMCP registration.

## Preview environments without provider patches

Check the installed ordinary Worker and Worker Preview providers separately.
A declared observability type or an existing Preview retaining earlier settings
does not prove that a newly created Preview receives those settings. Check both
create and update paths and read back a new deployment.

When required Preview settings lack native support, consider an ordinary
stage-owned Website Worker alongside its stage-owned API before patching the
provider. Keep exact stage names, self URL bindings and native log/trace
destinations. This changes the Preview URL and teardown owner; confirm that
tradeoff. For a mode change, use a distinct native resource identity, such as
`Namespace.push`, and inspect the create/delete plan so the former parent cannot
be overwritten. Preserve production identities and shared state.

Ordinary workers.dev Websites need their own indexing policy. Cloudflare's
[`_headers` file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/)
covers static assets; it does not cover Worker-generated replies. Apply the
checked stage policy through the existing framework response adapter, test
pages, errors, machine replies and assets, and keep production indexable.
Update CI addresses, Preview comments and trace queries for distinct Worker
names while preserving historical Preview records.

## Secrets

Prefer provider-managed secret references or Secrets Store bindings over plaintext workflow values.

- Acquire credentials through redacted Config.
- Validate secret binding names and stage.
- Never emit values in plans, logs, outputs, or receipts.
- Separate credential issuance from resource apply.
- Read back metadata or binding presence, never the secret.
- Revoke disposable credentials after lifecycle proof.

Removing a secret declaration may leave the old binding on the deployed Worker.
Check the active version's binding names and types; a no-change plan does not
prove removal. Prefer a supported native Alchemy deletion operation. If the
installed provider has none, record the residue and request an exact one-off
ownership exception before a provider write. Do not introduce a dependency
patch, custom resource or placeholder secret to conceal the gap. Keep shared
token revocation separate from binding removal. See the
[hosted telemetry cutover](../effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Observability

Cloudflare platform observability and application telemetry are separate sources.

For Cloudflare-native logs or destinations:

- identify Worker/service/environment/stage;
- define retention and sampling;
- read back the destination/binding;
- query the downstream provider.

For Effect OTLP export:

- keep endpoint/token in a redacted binding;
- decode the binding at application ingress;
- attach one exporter Layer to the runtime;
- preserve `waitUntil` or the host completion mechanism;
- test transport wiring;
- query Axiom independently before claiming ingestion.

## State

If Cloudflare backs Alchemy state, document bootstrap and recovery. Do not create a circular dependency between the state backend and the graph it stores. Use a separate bootstrap stack or a tested provider-supported mechanism where necessary.

behaviour. In the qualified beta.80 source, `--yes` permits automatic creation
and upgrades; pending setup can also be recovered. An existing-only rule is a
separate project choice. Check it before building a custom state client. Native

must be understood before promising stronger preservation. See
[native migrations](../operations/native-migrations.md#start-with-the-standard-behaviour)
and its pinned sources.

## Readback checklist

After apply, query the Cloudflare API for:

- account and zone identity;
- Worker/script/service name;
- deployment/version identifier where available;
- routes/domains;
- bindings and safe resource IDs;
- compatibility settings;
- observability configuration;
- storage resource presence.

Then run the public route/asset journey. Report any unavailable readback as a non-claim.

name: package-structure
description: Scaffold, audit, migrate, or validate TypeScript packages with strict Effect v4 boundaries, explicit live-types exports, deterministic test Layers, and repository-local source conditions. Use for Effect service, RPC, or HTTP API packages; package export maps; live.layer.ts/test.layer.ts separation; package ownership; helper-sprawl prevention; or replacing stale package scaffolds. Do not use for repository-root or TanStack application scaffolding.
---

# Package Structure

Build the narrowest package that owns a real semantic boundary. Follow the
repository contract before the generic templates.

## Resolve the repository contract

1. Read the applicable `AGENTS.md`, root/package `README*`, architecture docs,
   manifests, TypeScript/lint/test config, and current package exemplars.
2. If invoked through a repository-local same-name skill, read its
   `references/repository-profile.md` first. That profile owns package manager,
   namespace, source condition, package exceptions, forbidden paths, and
   package commands.
3. Load the sibling [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) and its
   repository-local profile when present. That profile—not the package
   profile—owns documentation, runbook, proof, lifecycle, and archive routes.
4. Inspect the worktree before writes. Preserve unrelated changes and do not
   scaffold into a package until ownership is decided.
5. Load [package contract](references/package-contract.md), then only the
   relevant variant section in [variants](references/variants.md).

## Select the variant

- `effect-service`: domain/provider capability with Schemas, expected failures,
  a contract-only service, production Layer, and deterministic test Layer.
- `rpc`: RPC transport over an existing domain service. It owns RPC contracts,
  handlers, clients, and transport—not domain policy.
- `http-api`: HTTP transport over an existing domain service. It owns API
  groups, status mapping, handlers, browser and host-supplied clients, and routes.
- A transport client Layer can implement the existing domain Context.Service.
  Keep generated native clients private and avoid a duplicate public contract.
- Source-only or publishable packages are export/build policies applied after
  choosing the semantic variant; they are not extra module trees.

Do not create a package for one-use code, a pass-through wrapper, a generic
`utils` bucket, or a boundary already owned by another package.

## Render or audit

For a new package, use the canonical renderer. It refuses existing targets and
has no overwrite mode. It renders the compiled-internal policy only; source-only
and publishable packages require a repository-specific audit/migration because
their bundler and actual publisher own the proof:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_package.py \
  --kind effect-service \
  --target /absolute/new/package \
  --package-name @scope/catalog \
  --source-condition @scope/source \
  --versions /absolute/version-snapshot.json
```

RPC and HTTP API also require `--domain-package @scope/catalog`. Read
[renderer and safety](references/renderer-and-safety.md) before invoking it.

For an existing package, run inspection first and make the smallest patch that
brings it to the owning repository contract:

```bash
python3 scripts/inspect_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
```

## Enforce the Effect boundary

- `schemas.ts` owns Schemas, brands, and schema-derived types.
- `errors.ts` owns expected failures. Serializable boundaries use the installed
  Schema error factory (`Schema.TaggedError` in the qualified RC); internal-only
  failures may use `Data.TaggedError`. Templates target the same qualified RC.
- `service.ts` owns only `Context.Service` contracts—never a Layer or SDK.
- `live.layer.ts` keeps host/SDK construction private and owns production
  configuration/resources.
- `test.layer.ts` creates deterministic substitution at the same contract and
  may return `{ layer, observations }` scoped to one test.
- Public methods use named `Effect.fn`; dependent private generators use
  `Effect.fnUntraced`, while short private pipelines stay plain functions.
  Use `Service.of` to check implementations and the
  two-argument `Layer.effect` for effectful construction. Read the sibling
  [service and Layer recipes](../strict-effect-ts/references/services/services-and-layers.md).
- Decode unknown provider input/output once at ingress. Encode only at outward
  HTTP/RPC/provider/persistence/report boundaries.
- Keep operations lazy, flat, and sequential. Keep one-use mapping, decoding,
  and error handling beside the operation. Extract only demonstrated reuse,
  independently testable policy, real I/O, or resource lifetime.
- Reject generic SDK callbacks, raw client access, unbranded semantic strings,
  primitive semantic config, runtime type-class branching, unchecked output,
  scattered Effect execution, and speculative helpers.
- When a public schema/service/transport changes, update the repository's
  architecture owner and affected proof/critical journeys in the same slice.
  Operational packages route to a repository runbook; pure packages state why
  no runbook applies.

Read [Effect service rules](references/effect-service.md) before changing an
external client or live Layer.

## Validate and hand off

Run the repository's real format, lint, typecheck, focused tests, integration
tests, build, packed-artifact, and downstream commands that apply. Also run:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_ecosystem.py /absolute/skill-or-repository-root
```

For publishable packages, inspect the tarball produced by the repository's
actual publisher; `publishConfig.exports` alone is not proof that npm or Bun
removed the development source condition.

For new or changed skill folders, run the global skill validator separately.
Run the local docs-maintainer checks and attach the applicable impact rows and
non-claims. Report the selected variant, ownership decision, exports,
documentation/proof impact, tests, commands, and any repository-specific exception. Render receipts
retain official sources, qualified compatibility decisions, config digests,
limitations, and non-claims. Read [maintenance](references/maintenance.md)
when updating templates, validators, or Effect APIs.

## Strict data ownership in every package

Declare owned live and test Layers as static values. Put caller-supplied checked
inputs in named Context requirements and supply them with native `Layer.succeed`
and `Layer.provide`. Tests use `Layer.mock` or replacement Layers; native
composition callbacks remain valid. The HTTP and RPC templates follow this rule.

Use one Schema owner for each identity, constrained value and data record; infer
its public types and reuse its fields and record-level checks in HTTP/RPC/provider
and persistence codecs. Typed internal inputs/replies are already checked. Decode
unknown data once at its real boundary, construct newly constrained values with
the owning fallible constructor, and encode only outward contracts. Meaningful
IDs, URLs, dates, offsets and bounded text use owning brands rather than parallel
primitive definitions.

Domain absence uses Option, including recursive source fields. Preserve old
formats, missing/null distinctions, literal values and source hashes in codecs
and compatibility tests. Use Effect Array/Record functions, immutable HashMap/
HashSet and exhaustive Match throughout source, tests, tools and configuration.
No loops, native array traversal, reassignment or mutable/transient collection
mode is justified by a readonly return type. Genuine shared state belongs in an
owned Ref/transaction with a pure immutable update. Use readonly structured keys
for Effect caches and qualify sharing, full identity and cleanup on cancellation.

See the sibling strict-effect-ts Schema, collection and cache owners. The generated
package runs under its repository's actual strict lint configuration; the offline
Python shape check is not proof of TypeScript policy, execution or cloud behaviour.

```bash
  --source-condition @scope/source \
  --versions /absolute/version-snapshot.json
```

RPC and HTTP API also require `--domain-package @scope/catalog`. Read
[renderer and safety](references/renderer-and-safety.md) before invoking it.

For an existing package, run inspection first and make the smallest patch that
brings it to the owning repository contract:

```bash
python3 scripts/inspect_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
```

## Enforce the Effect boundary

- `schemas.ts` owns Schemas, brands, and schema-derived types.
- `errors.ts` owns expected failures. Serializable boundaries use the installed
  Schema error factory (`Schema.TaggedError` in the qualified RC); internal-only
  failures may use `Data.TaggedError`. Templates target the same qualified RC.
- `service.ts` owns only `Context.Service` contracts—never a Layer or SDK.
- `live.layer.ts` keeps host/SDK construction private and owns production
  configuration/resources.
- `test.layer.ts` creates deterministic substitution at the same contract and
  may return `{ layer, observations }` scoped to one test.
- Public methods use named `Effect.fn`; dependent private generators use
  `Effect.fnUntraced`, while short private pipelines stay plain functions.
  Use `Service.of` to check implementations and the
  two-argument `Layer.effect` for effectful construction. Read the sibling
  [service and Layer recipes](../strict-effect-ts/references/services/services-and-layers.md).
- Decode unknown provider input/output once at ingress. Encode only at outward
  HTTP/RPC/provider/persistence/report boundaries.
- Keep operations lazy, flat, and sequential. Keep one-use mapping, decoding,
  and error handling beside the operation. Extract only demonstrated reuse,
  independently testable policy, real I/O, or resource lifetime.
- Reject generic SDK callbacks, raw client access, unbranded semantic strings,
  primitive semantic config, runtime type-class branching, unchecked output,
  scattered Effect execution, and speculative helpers.
- When a public schema/service/transport changes, update the repository's
  architecture owner and affected proof/critical journeys in the same slice.
  Operational packages route to a repository runbook; pure packages state why
  no runbook applies.

Read [Effect service rules](references/effect-service.md) before changing an
external client or live Layer.

## Validate and hand off

Run the repository's real format, lint, typecheck, focused tests, integration
tests, build, packed-artifact, and downstream commands that apply. Also run:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_ecosystem.py /absolute/skill-or-repository-root
```

For publishable packages, inspect the tarball produced by the repository's
actual publisher; `publishConfig.exports` alone is not proof that npm or Bun
removed the development source condition.

For new or changed skill folders, run the global skill validator separately.
Run the local docs-maintainer checks and attach the applicable impact rows and
non-claims. Report the selected variant, ownership decision, exports,
documentation/proof impact, tests, commands, and any repository-specific exception. Render receipts
retain official sources, qualified compatibility decisions, config digests,
limitations, and non-claims. Read [maintenance](references/maintenance.md)
when updating templates, validators, or Effect APIs.

## Strict data ownership in every package

Declare owned live and test Layers as static values. Put caller-supplied checked
inputs in named Context requirements and supply them with native `Layer.succeed`
and `Layer.provide`. Tests use `Layer.mock` or replacement Layers; native
composition callbacks remain valid. The HTTP and RPC templates follow this rule.

Use one Schema owner for each identity, constrained value and data record; infer
its public types and reuse its fields and record-level checks in HTTP/RPC/provider
and persistence codecs. Typed internal inputs/replies are already checked. Decode
unknown data once at its real boundary, construct newly constrained values with
the owning fallible constructor, and encode only outward contracts. Meaningful
IDs, URLs, dates, offsets and bounded text use owning brands rather than parallel
primitive definitions.

Domain absence uses Option, including recursive source fields. Preserve old
formats, missing/null distinctions, literal values and source hashes in codecs
and compatibility tests. Use Effect Array/Record functions, immutable HashMap/
HashSet and exhaustive Match throughout source, tests, tools and configuration.
No loops, native array traversal, reassignment or mutable/transient collection
mode is justified by a readonly return type. Genuine shared state belongs in an
owned Ref/transaction with a pure immutable update. Use readonly structured keys
for Effect caches and qualify sharing, full identity and cleanup on cancellation.

See the sibling strict-effect-ts Schema, collection and cache owners. The generated
package runs under its repository's actual strict lint configuration; the offline
Python shape check is not proof of TypeScript policy, execution or cloud behaviour.

name: package-structure
description: Scaffold, audit, migrate, or validate TypeScript packages with strict Effect v4 boundaries, explicit live-types exports, deterministic test Layers, and repository-local source conditions. Use for Effect service, RPC, or HTTP API packages; package export maps; live.layer.ts/test.layer.ts separation; package ownership; helper-sprawl prevention; or replacing stale package scaffolds. Do not use for repository-root or TanStack application scaffolding.
---

# Package Structure

Build the narrowest package that owns a real semantic boundary. Follow the
repository contract before the generic templates.

## Resolve the repository contract

1. Read the applicable `AGENTS.md`, root/package `README*`, architecture docs,
   manifests, TypeScript/lint/test config, and current package exemplars.
2. If invoked through a repository-local same-name skill, read its
   `references/repository-profile.md` first. That profile owns package manager,
   namespace, source condition, package exceptions, forbidden paths, and
   package commands.
3. Load the sibling [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) and its
   repository-local profile when present. That profile—not the package
   profile—owns documentation, runbook, proof, lifecycle, and archive routes.
4. Inspect the worktree before writes. Preserve unrelated changes and do not
   scaffold into a package until ownership is decided.
5. Load [package contract](references/package-contract.md), then only the
   relevant variant section in [variants](references/variants.md).

## Select the variant

- `effect-service`: domain/provider capability with Schemas, expected failures,
  a contract-only service, production Layer, and deterministic test Layer.
- `rpc`: RPC transport over an existing domain service. It owns RPC contracts,
  handlers, clients, and transport—not domain policy.
- `http-api`: HTTP transport over an existing domain service. It owns API
  groups, status mapping, handlers, browser and host-supplied clients, and routes.
- A transport client Layer can implement the existing domain Context.Service.
  Keep generated native clients private and avoid a duplicate public contract.
- Source-only or publishable packages are export/build policies applied after
  choosing the semantic variant; they are not extra module trees.

Do not create a package for one-use code, a pass-through wrapper, a generic
`utils` bucket, or a boundary already owned by another package.

## Render or audit

For a new package, use the canonical renderer. It refuses existing targets and
has no overwrite mode. It renders the compiled-internal policy only; source-only
and publishable packages require a repository-specific audit/migration because
their bundler and actual publisher own the proof:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_package.py \
  --kind effect-service \
  --target /absolute/new/package \
  --package-name @scope/catalog \
  --source-condition @scope/source \
  --versions /absolute/version-snapshot.json
```

RPC and HTTP API also require `--domain-package @scope/catalog`. Read
[renderer and safety](references/renderer-and-safety.md) before invoking it.

For an existing package, run inspection first and make the smallest patch that
brings it to the owning repository contract:

```bash
python3 scripts/inspect_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
```

## Enforce the Effect boundary

- `schemas.ts` owns Schemas, brands, and schema-derived types.
- `errors.ts` owns expected failures. Serializable boundaries use the installed
  Schema error factory (`Schema.TaggedError` in the qualified RC); internal-only
  failures may use `Data.TaggedError`. Templates target the same qualified RC.
- `service.ts` owns only `Context.Service` contracts—never a Layer or SDK.
- `live.layer.ts` keeps host/SDK construction private and owns production
  configuration/resources.
- `test.layer.ts` creates deterministic substitution at the same contract and
  may return `{ layer, observations }` scoped to one test.
- Public methods use named `Effect.fn`; dependent private generators use
  `Effect.fnUntraced`, while short private pipelines stay plain functions.
  Use `Service.of` to check implementations and the
  two-argument `Layer.effect` for effectful construction. Read the sibling
  [service and Layer recipes](../strict-effect-ts/references/services/services-and-layers.md).
- Decode unknown provider input/output once at ingress. Encode only at outward
  HTTP/RPC/provider/persistence/report boundaries.
- Keep operations lazy, flat, and sequential. Keep one-use mapping, decoding,
  and error handling beside the operation. Extract only demonstrated reuse,
  independently testable policy, real I/O, or resource lifetime.
- Reject generic SDK callbacks, raw client access, unbranded semantic strings,
  primitive semantic config, runtime type-class branching, unchecked output,
  scattered Effect execution, and speculative helpers.
- When a public schema/service/transport changes, update the repository's
  architecture owner and affected proof/critical journeys in the same slice.
  Operational packages route to a repository runbook; pure packages state why
  no runbook applies.

Read [Effect service rules](references/effect-service.md) before changing an
external client or live Layer.

## Validate and hand off

Run the repository's real format, lint, typecheck, focused tests, integration
tests, build, packed-artifact, and downstream commands that apply. Also run:

```bash
python3 scripts/validate_package.py /absolute/package
python3 scripts/validate_ecosystem.py /absolute/skill-or-repository-root
```

For publishable packages, inspect the tarball produced by the repository's
actual publisher; `publishConfig.exports` alone is not proof that npm or Bun
removed the development source condition.

For new or changed skill folders, run the global skill validator separately.
Run the local docs-maintainer checks and attach the applicable impact rows and
non-claims. Report the selected variant, ownership decision, exports,
documentation/proof impact, tests, commands, and any repository-specific exception. Render receipts
retain official sources, qualified compatibility decisions, config digests,
limitations, and non-claims. Read [maintenance](references/maintenance.md)
when updating templates, validators, or Effect APIs.

## Strict data ownership in every package

Declare owned live and test Layers as static values. Put caller-supplied checked
inputs in named Context requirements and supply them with native `Layer.succeed`
and `Layer.provide`. Tests use `Layer.mock` or replacement Layers; native
composition callbacks remain valid. The HTTP and RPC templates follow this rule.

Use one Schema owner for each identity, constrained value and data record; infer
its public types and reuse its fields and record-level checks in HTTP/RPC/provider
and persistence codecs. Typed internal inputs/replies are already checked. Decode
unknown data once at its real boundary, construct newly constrained values with
the owning fallible constructor, and encode only outward contracts. Meaningful
IDs, URLs, dates, offsets and bounded text use owning brands rather than parallel
primitive definitions.

Domain absence uses Option, including recursive source fields. Preserve old
formats, missing/null distinctions, literal values and source hashes in codecs
and compatibility tests. Use Effect Array/Record functions, immutable HashMap/
HashSet and exhaustive Match throughout source, tests, tools and configuration.
No loops, native array traversal, reassignment or mutable/transient collection
mode is justified by a readonly return type. Genuine shared state belongs in an
owned Ref/transaction with a pure immutable update. Use readonly structured keys
for Effect caches and qualify sharing, full identity and cleanup on cancellation.

See the sibling strict-effect-ts Schema, collection and cache owners. The generated
package runs under its repository's actual strict lint configuration; the offline
Python shape check is not proof of TypeScript policy, execution or cloud behaviour.

Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/operations_simplification
Payload:
Use plugin 0.6.11’s portable Effect rules as the main owner, then retain a small set of TaxKit rules that cover genuine gaps. Copying Common Practice’s entire lint collection would preserve overlapping checks and several obsolete assumptions.

The source comparison found:

- Plugin 0.6.11’s `effect-policy.ts` has 13 rules, including new `static-layers` and `module-ownership` rules.
- TaxKit loads an older 11-rule copy from `.agents`. Common Practice vendors almost the same older copy; its only difference is allowing native Alchemy `Namespace.push`.
- Common Practice separately implements static Layers, private Promise adapters, SDK privacy and browser-runtime ownership in its own rule file.
- Several anti-slop files are identical between the repos. Common Practice’s retained TaxKit rules are older than TaxKit’s current implementation.
- Tool versions differ: TaxKit uses Oxlint/plugins **1.86.0**, Ultracite **7.12.2**, Effect tooling **0.48.0**; Common Practice uses **1.85.0**, **7.12.0**, **0.45.0**. Reusing rules does not require downgrading TaxKit.

| Area | Recommended source-to-target change |
|---|---|
| Portable Effect rules | Vendor the current plugin’s single `effect-policy.ts` under `tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect`. Enable all relevant rules across owned apps, packages, tools, configuration and tests. Remove the executable `.agents` copy and duplicate rules once equivalent behaviour is demonstrated. |
| Static Layers | Enable `strict-effect/static-layers`. Replace internal factories with static Layers whose named requirements carry checked caller settings. Native inline composition callbacks remain allowed. The rule recognises aliases, return types and common Layer-preserving operations. |
| Host/SDK ownership | Configure `strict-effect/module-ownership` for Alchemy, Cloudflare bindings, private SDKs and authored/generated content imports. It checks imports, re-exports, import types and known dynamic import addresses. TaxKit’s current host-contract rule does **not** cover Alchemy or `cloudflare:workers`. |
| Promise adapters | Use current `strict-effect/no-promise-workflow` with exact host/SDK files. Keep TaxKit’s `effect/no-bare-effect-try-promise` to require a checked error mapping. No allowance for every `*.layer.ts` or every test. Use `promiseOnlyFiles` where a host test needs only `Effect.promise`. |
| Runtime ownership | Keep one server runtime and one browser Atom runtime. Port Common Practice’s browser `Atom.runtime`/`RegistryProvider` ownership check using TaxKit’s real paths. Keep the SDK’s necessary private Promise runtime as an exact library adapter. |
| External decoding | Retain TaxKit’s `no-decoding-outside-boundaries` and `no-route-transport-restore-outside-consumers`: their lexical alias tracking and actual CLI fixtures cover useful behaviour beyond the portable rules. Keep encoding at the owning outward boundary. |
| Mutable state | Keep current portable collection rules **and** TaxKit’s lexical `no-native-collections`/`no-object-writes`. The latter follows constructor aliases and Object/Reflect writes which the portable rule does not fully cover. State belongs in Effect Ref/collections; pure folds do not need Ref. |
| Raw HTTP work | Extend raw-fetch restrictions across owned source. TaxKit currently bans bare `fetch` only in selected analytics files. Native HttpClient or an exact unavoidable host adapter should own it. |
| Package boundaries | Adapt the plugin’s manifest-derived export check to TaxKit’s actual nested workspaces. Preserve SDK packed/export/downstream checks. The current cross-package rule checks `/src` paths and `@scope/package/src`, but does not validate all exported subpaths or imports starting outside `/src`. |
| Effect diagnostics | Replace the one-file compatibility probe with strict diagnostics over actual apps, packages, tools and Alchemy roots. Preserve normal TypeScript checks. Common Practice already runs strict diagnostics on its root and packages. |

Useful source references: [current portable rules](/Users/cooper/.codex/plugins/cache/commonplace/development-workflows/0.6.11/skills/strict-effect-ts/assets/oxlint/effect-policy.ts:1538), [static Layers](/Users/cooper/.codex/plugins/cache/commonplace/development-workflows/0.6.11/skills/strict-effect-ts/SKILL.md:114), [Common Practice ownership rules](/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/tools/oxlint/common-practice-rules.ts:1180), [TaxKit host-import check](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tools/oxlint/effect-rules.ts:523), [TaxKit package rule](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tools/oxlint/package-rules.ts:35).

Several checks need careful adaptation:

- **Named operations:** public service methods should use named `Effect.fn`; private dependent generators can use `fnUntraced`, and short pipelines can remain plain functions. Common Practice’s apparent instrumentation rule hard-codes old services such as `Distribution` and `ManifestSync`, and recognises the literal identifier `Effect`. It does not enforce Content or TaxKit service methods. Do not copy it and claim complete coverage. [Implementation](/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/tools/oxlint/vendor/commonplace/effect-rules.js:287).
- **Configuration:** use the owning Schema through `Config.schema` for constrained settings. TaxKit’s API and Website already do this; the old HTTP config uses `Config.URL` followed by a synchronous `.make`. The scaffold’s primitive-config regex matches obsolete lowercase names and scans only one-level `package/src` folders. It misses TaxKit’s nested packages and current Config spellings. Native `Config.Boolean` remains appropriate for a plain flag; a blanket primitive ban would be wrong. [Template scan](/Users/cooper/.codex/plugins/cache/commonplace/development-workflows/0.6.11/skills/repo-structure/assets/repository/tools/oxlint/policy.test.ts.tmpl:159).
- **Absence:** portable `no-unsafe-option-unwrap` rejects `getOrThrow`, but not `getOrNull`/`getOrUndefined`. Add a focused domain rule if desired, while allowing real protocol/compiler adapters. Preserve TaxKit’s nested Option model that distinguishes a missing key from a present undefined key. Common Practice’s nullable rule merely catches `Schema.NullOr` and literal null properties; it cannot prove every domain type is non-nullable.
- **Schema-derived types:** existing unknown/type-assertion checks help, but none proves that every handwritten type reuses its owning Schema. Retain type-level checks and focused review; avoid claiming that a broad regex solves this.
- **False positives:** the current portable rule already allows functional `Output.map` and native `Namespace.push`. Do not add wide exceptions for those. `.at`, `.json` and runtime method names are matched syntactically, so unrelated methods can collide. Exceptions should name the actual file and operation.
- **Suppressions:** TaxKit’s two-pass directive check makes inline suppression of the two boundary rules fail. Keep that effective protection. It does not protect every other lint rule. A nearby `SAFETY:` comment does not permit a type assertion while the ordinary assertion ban is active.

TaxKit’s Effect diagnostic command currently examines only `tools/effect-language-service/compatibility.ts`, which contains a single `Effect.succeed` example. Its base config also excludes warnings/suggestions from compiler failure. That establishes tool compatibility, not application-wide Effect correctness. [Probe configuration](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tools/effect-language-service/tsconfig.json:9), [base settings](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/tsconfig.base.json:4), [Common Practice settings](/Users/cooper/Projects/common-practice/tsconfig.base.json:19).

Two genuine design choices remain:

1. **Existing public Layer factories:** HTTP exports include `createTaxKitApiClientLayer` and its deprecated alias. The new static-Layer rule permits no factory exceptions. Either retire those public helpers in a deliberate breaking package change, or explicitly allow their narrow compatibility adapter temporarily. Internal RPC, Content and Website factories can change without weakening the rule. [Public helpers](/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit/packages/api/http/src/client/live.layer.ts:12).
2. **Object-only Effect inputs:** Common Practice requires every reusable `fn`/`fnUntraced` operation to take one object. That would change established TaxKit SDK methods and valid branded-value helpers. I recommend keeping existing checked signatures and applying named-object inputs only where several inputs need a meaningful combined contract.

Do not copy Common Practice’s training identifiers, training/appearance dependency rules or product-specific paths. Reuse their ownership approach for TaxKit’s calculator identities, tax packages, content and host adapters. Retain a compact actual-CLI fixture suite proving rejection **and** acceptance, including aliases, neighbouring files and nested packages. No receipt, qualification ledger or governance register is needed.

No files changed and no tests or provider calls ran.

---
document_type: design-proposal
lifecycle: proposed
authority: supporting
owner: taxkit-architecture-owner
last_reviewed: 2026-10-10
review_trigger: agreed direction, Common Practice implementation, upstream support or migration scope changes
---

# Common Practice foundation review

Use Common Practice's application structure and ordinary development workflow.
Prioritise the Cloudflare Website and API, remove every Alchemy patch, and remove
TaxKit's separate receipt and approval machinery. Keep Bun as a supported,
secondary host over the same calculation packages.

```text
Website server/browser -> checked RPC operations -> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP -----------------------------> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Local SDK ----------------------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core

Checked stage settings -> API declaration -> Website declaration
                                      API address + private binding -> Website
Git commit/PR -> ordinary checks -> native Alchemy -> deployed Website/API
                               Doppler supplies stage-specific secrets
```

The comparison uses TaxKit commit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`,
Common Practice commit `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7`, and Commonplace
`development-workflows` 0.6.11, checked against its published release on
10 October 2026. This document and its [plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
replace the large, uncommitted audit packet created during this review.

This remains the agreed research and design stage. Application code, dependency
versions, hosted workflows, provider resources and credentials have not changed.
The latest instructions determine the proposed direction; they do not require a
new JSON acceptance record for each finding. Common Practice is read-only.

## Agreed direction

| Choice | Direction |
| --- | --- |
| Website calls | Keep the current typed RPC calls for this change; adopt Common Practice's checked client and application ownership. Improve the HTTP client separately. |
| Hosts | Cloudflare first. Keep Bun and Cloudflare, with shared packages independent of either. Preserve Bun's current HTTP coverage; adding RPC/MCP to Bun is outside this change. |
| Alchemy | Zero Alchemy patches, including replacement monkeypatches, copied planner code or a custom provider carrying the same fixes. Redesign the declarations that currently need them. |
| Development and operations | Ordinary commits, pull requests, checks, GitHub Actions, native Alchemy and native Doppler, following Common Practice. Remove receipt packets, duplicated approval records and checks whose only purpose is to verify that paperwork. |
| Operational information | Allow fixed safe details such as app, stage, route category, duration and safe failure category. Exclude salaries, facts, results, calculation traces, raw URLs, request bodies and raw errors. PostHog remains postponed. |

The host and privacy choices are also recorded in [ADR 0003](../adr/0003-support-independent-api-hosts.md)
and [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-limit-operational-observations.md). The earlier
[shared Axiom dataset choice](../adr/0002-reuse-shared-telemetry-datasets.md)
remains: reference the existing three physical datasets, with TaxKit-owned scoped
access and destinations. No collection is enabled by this review.

## What to copy from Common Practice

| Area | Common Practice source | TaxKit adoption |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server execution | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.server.ts` | One frontend server runtime, constructed in the application. Services and tax packages never start their own runtime. |
| Browser state | `apps/web/src/lib/runtime.client.ts` | One React-mounted Atom state graph. Keep TaxKit's existing form commands and cancellation. |
| Checked clients | `packages/http/src/client.layer.ts`, `packages/rpc/src/client.layer.ts`, `packages/content/src/service.ts` | Keep generated clients private; expose named operations through a checked service, with live and test implementations. |
| Private Cloudflare calls | `apps/web/src/lib/api/binding.adapter.layer.ts` | Put Cloudflare binding conversion in one Website-owned adapter. Use native Alchemy conversion where it preserves caller trust and complete reply handling. |
| Resource declarations | `alchemy.run.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts`, `apps/api/src/deployment/cloudflare/worker.ts` | Declare the API before the Website. Website uses the API's actual address and private binding. Keep deployment code at the app/infrastructure owners. |
| Secrets | `packages/infrastructure/src/secrets.ts` | One native source list: Doppler, ignored `.env` overrides, disabled shell-value fallback. Keep TaxKit's own project, configs and credentials. |
| Commands | Root `package.json` | Short commands calling native Alchemy directly. Keep one understandable verification command. |
| Automation | `.github/workflows/checks.yml`, `preview.yml`, `production.yml` | Checks on PR/main; PR previews and close-event cleanup; manual main-only Production. Native dry-run/deploy, small public smoke checks and native Production drift. |
| Everyday records | Git commits, PRs, workflow logs and Alchemy state | Use these ordinary records. No additional repository receipt files or approval-envelope system. |

These are paths within Common Practice, not personal checkout paths. Reuse the
approach and required code, not its project names, access tokens or provider IDs.

Common Practice still runs build, formatting, lint, types, Effect checks, tests,
unused-code and documentation checks. Its workflow does not support a claim that
all verification disappears. TaxKit should remove checks of ceremony while

a library that calculates inside the caller's program.

| Call | Current path and behaviour to preserve |
| --- | --- |
| Browser calculation | Page container -> Atom command -> checked public RPC address -> API handler -> `PublicCalculatorService` -> catalogue/fact checks -> Australian rules/Core -> checked report -> the same Atom state and rendering leaf. Editing or leaving the page cancels pending browser work. |
| Server HTML form | Website checks the 64 KiB POST -> server service -> private API method carrying the checked original caller identity separately from JSON -> the same calculation service -> checked submission data. Keep working without JavaScript. |
| Machine HTTP | HTTP declarations decode requests with the owning Schemas -> handler -> the same calculation service -> existing status/error envelope. The new client adds named checked operations around these declarations. |
| Machine RPC | Revision-four checked operations -> the same service. Keep the current encoded replies and safe named failures. |
| Remote MCP | API tool definitions reuse the owning Schemas and shared service. Keep current request/cancellation ownership and Cloudflare session support. |
| Local SDK | Checked in-process request -> the same calculation service. Effect callers own their services; the Promise-facing SDK privately owns its necessary runtime and closes it. It does not become a network SDK. |

| Comparison | Common Practice | TaxKit decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Website transport | Typed HTTP over a private binding; ordinary page reads use server functions. Its RPC client exists but is not the Website's chosen path. | Keep Website RPC because it already covers calculator and documentation operations. Copy client ownership rather than force an HTTP rewrite. |
| Named services | HTTP and RPC implement its Content service; raw generated clients are private. | RPC already has named checked operations. Add the equivalent HTTP approach, keeping existing exports as compatibility adapters. |
| Error ownership | Remote client errors become safe Content-owned errors. | A remote call can fail differently from a local calculation. Use one owning checked remote-operation contract, with existing RPC names retained; do not pretend transport errors are local engine errors or add another generic facade. |
| Original caller identity | Content reads do not have TaxKit's anonymous-calculation rate policy. | Preserve the private method's trusted caller key. Plain forwarded headers from a binding are insufficient. Interpret Cloudflare edge headers in the host, not the shared RPC package. |
| Cancellation | Native HTTP binding can carry an operation signal. | Browser RPC cancellation stays. The current private RPC method cannot send an AbortSignal remotely: it stops waiting locally; remote work has its five-second budget. Do not claim immediate remote cancellation. |
| Reply limits | Content uses a longer timeout for image rendering. | Keep TaxKit's ten-second complete-reply limit, 2 MiB response cap and no automatic retries. Give the new HTTP client equivalent full-read limits. |
| RPC lifetime | Common Practice acquires its RPC client once. | Keep TaxKit's per-operation client scope: a receive loop left on an earlier Cloudflare request can stall the next request. Copying the once-acquired loop would undo a deliberate fix. |
| Documentation | HTTP has selected content/Markdown/SEO/image operations. | TaxKit also needs discovery, navigation, page, search and Markdown. An HTTP-only Website would need equivalent checked coverage; do not add a second content renderer. |
| Package consumers | Common Practice's packages are private and source-oriented. | Keep TaxKit's compiled exports, actual packed SDK entry points and clean downstream consumer checks when those contracts change. |

This resolves the Website choice for the foundation change. A later HTTP switch
can be assessed on its own merit; it is not required to adopt Common Practice.

## Cloudflare first, with host-independent packages

Use Effect services and Layers to describe shared operations and supply their
implementations. Core, rule, calculator and transport packages must not import
Cloudflare, Alchemy or Bun server code, interpret trusted Cloudflare headers, or
run Effects themselves. The SDK's private Promise adapter is a justified public
library execution boundary.

The API app owns the host adapters. Cloudflare supplies native request context,
private bindings, rate services and sessions. Bun supplies its HTTP server and
configuration through one top-level runner. Both use the same tax operations.
Do not add a managed Promise runtime to the native API Worker.

Matching upstream Effect 4.0.2 supports this separation: `HttpApiBuilder` captures
shared services, `HttpRouter` supplies the current request scope, and
`BunHttpServer` supplies the abstract server. `HttpRouter.provideRequest` builds
its supplied Layer per request; it must not own an application-wide capacity
pool. Alchemy's Worker bridge builds the application once and supplies native
request context. Stream cleanup belongs to the current consumer; isolate
shutdown is not a guaranteed cleanup hook.

Cloudflare already captures one bounded calculation service. Keep its shared
eight-place pool, five-second work budget, exact Website Origin and checked
private identity. A timer cannot interrupt synchronous calculation code.

Bun currently builds the bounded service per request, creating a fresh pool for
each one. Fix that at Bun application composition after the Cloudflare work.
Keep its current HTTP coverage and explicitly owned CORS/admission differences;
no Cloudflare Durable Object substitute or new Bun protocol promise is needed.

## Patch-free Alchemy design

TaxKit currently locks Effect 4.0.0 and patched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.80. Common
Practice locks Effect 4.0.2 and unpatched Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81. The target is the
compatible, published, unpatched upstream package used by Common Practice,
checked against TaxKit's installed types and consumers during implementation.
An upstream comparison is not an installation or a completed upgrade.

Two declarations need to change before removing the current Alchemy patch:

1. **Remove the two-way output dependency.** In
   `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, Website uses API output/binding
   while API reads Website output. Replace API's reverse dependency with one
   checked, stage-owned exact Website address. The same settings own its domain
   or checked Worker name. For Preview, retain the actual existing Worker name
   and use the actual account subdomain through Alchemy's native setting; syntax
   checks alone do not confirm account ownership. Do not guess the
   generated hostname or add Preview DNS as an incidental change. API retains
   its own `Worker.URL`; Website consumes API output and retains its own
   `Worker.URL`. Declare API, then Website.
   Use fixed local ports and `strictPort: true`, following Common Practice,
   so an occupied port fails rather than silently changing the allowed origin.
   Check both native local addresses before implementation. Do not widen allowed Origins to `*` or infer an
   address from arbitrary request headers to solve this.
2. **Avoid the shared redirect write.** Remove `domain.redirects` from the
   Website declaration. Set the canonical `domain.name` to `taxkit.dev` and
   `aliases` to `["www.taxkit.dev"]`. At Website ingress, return the existing
   permanent redirect for `www` before routes or calculator forms. Select native
   `assets: { runWorkerFirst: true }` so static files cannot skip that host check;
   then serve canonical static files through the native `ASSETS` binding while
   preserving the normal page fallback. The current Website needs this asset
   delegation added. Preserve path/query semantics and the current redirect
   status. This bypasses the Worker
   provider's shared-zone redirect ruleset code without a custom provider.
   Common Practice itself uses `domain.redirects`; this field is a necessary
   TaxKit departure. Previously saved redirect declarations can invoke the
   same provider path during removal, so check the existing-state transition
   before calling the migration safe. No patched replacement is permitted.

Upstream beta.81 still treats every shared redirect-rules read failure as an
absent ruleset. The earlier mocked forbidden-read case produced a replacement
write. That shows a problem with blindly keeping this declaration while deleting
the patch; it does not require retaining the patch. A separate native Ruleset
resource owns an entire zone phase, so it is unsuitable unless TaxKit owns every
rule in that phase. Use the Website alias/redirect approach instead.

Remove the Alchemy entry from `patchedDependencies`, its patch file, and the
corresponding lockfile patch references together. Search build, install and
infrastructure code for every other Alchemy modification. Do not relocate a fix
into a wrapper, copied source or postinstall step. Preserve logical resource IDs,
stack/state identities and the existing unrelated DNS records.

The Atom scheduler peer-metadata patch is unrelated to Alchemy. Common Practice
also has non-Alchemy Effect/PostHog patches; those are not required by this
proposal and must not be copied without a TaxKit need. Align the Effect family
and explicit companion override if choosing 4.0.2. Any React/Atom compatibility
change needs ordinary type/build/browser checks, not a new exception receipt.

## Ordinary commits, deployments and Doppler

Copy Common Practice's workflow shape:

- Make normal coherent Git commits and PRs. Describe the change and meaningful
  test results in the PR. Do not require an approval JSON, finding crosswalk,
  source-digest receipt or separate commit acceptance ceremony.
- Run one ordinary check workflow. Use the same verification command locally
  and in Actions, rather than a second release-policy graph that rechecks every
  earlier document and receipt.
- On an internal PR, install the frozen lockfile, check the change, then run
  native Alchemy dry-run and deploy for that PR's stage. Check the Website/API.
  On close, use native destroy restricted to that PR stage. Keep fork secrets
  excluded, same-stage deployment/cleanup serialised, and the current PR-state
  check. These prevent real mistakes and are small enough to understand.
- Production runs manually from `main`: ordinary verification, native dry-run,
  native deploy, native drift, and a small public Website/API check. Use existing
  GitHub environment settings; do not add a second TaxKit approval system.
- Use native `Doppler.Secrets`, `.env` and disabled `ProcessEnv` fallback in one
  owner, following Common Practice. `.env` overrides also apply in hosted runs;
  Actions should write deployment metadata only. Retain TaxKit's actual Doppler
  project/config mapping and environment-scoped read-only Doppler credentials.
  Do not copy another project's values or duplicate Cloudflare keys in GitHub.
- Roll back by redeploying the previous working Git revision through the same
  native workflow. Alchemy resource retention is not a deployment snapshot.

The [proposal](../../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md) records
the source comparison and Cooper's direction: Common Practice's app/client and
ordinary operational approach, Cloudflare first, patch-free Alchemy, supported
Bun host, and safe operational details only. This remains design work; no runtime
or provider change has been made.

Completed research covers the full Website/HTTP/RPC/MCP/SDK call paths, current
Common Practice workflows and native secrets, upstream Effect/Alchemy support,
package/export differences, and the tools that enforce TaxKit's extra ceremony.
The new audit packet has been removed and its useful findings folded into the
proposal. No implementation acceptance crosswalk or new receipt is required.

## Implementation order

| Order | Work | Meaningful check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Replace receipt/approval/custody/epoch tooling and instructions with normal commits, checks, native Alchemy and Doppler. Wire current Cloudflare preview/production workflows. | Commands select the intended stage; forks receive no secrets; preview deploy/cleanup cannot overlap; ordinary checks run without old receipt files. |
| 2 | Declare API then Website; use checked exact Website stage settings; replace shared redirect rules with native domain aliases and Website redirect handling. Remove all Alchemy patch entries/files and align the chosen published dependency graph. | Frozen unpatched install; real native create/update/no-op planning, local dev address behaviour and Website/API requests; exact Origin/trusted key; redirect behaviour including static files, fixed local ports, and unchanged unrelated zone rules. |
| 3 | Adopt CP named checked clients and native binding adaptation, keeping Website RPC and its per-operation lifetime. Improve HTTP client additively. Move Cloudflare header interpretation to host ingress. | Safe errors, complete reply deadline/byte cap, cancellation/repeated requests, no-JavaScript form, current HTTP/RPC/MCP contracts and package exports. |
| 4 | Move executable lint assets to their code owner; remove copied shared instructions; make import rules aware of nested manifests. | Actual lint catches invalid root/app/package crossings and accepts public exports. |
| 5 | Fix Bun application-wide calculation pool using the same host-neutral services. Keep current HTTP coverage. | Overlapping requests share eight places; five-second work limit and existing HTTP behaviour remain. |
| Later | Introduce fixed safe operational fields through native Axiom/Cloudflare resources using the agreed existing datasets. | No salaries/facts/results/traces, raw URLs/bodies/errors or unsafe native channel exports. |

Keep each code change coherent and reversible with Git. Use focused tests for
its actual behaviour and one ordinary verification command. Public package
contract changes use normal Changesets and actual packed/downstream checks.
The previous native emulator timeout failures remain unresolved; do not declare
the new graph working until meaningful runtime checks pass.

Update current architecture, runbooks, root instructions, skill profiles and the
older clean-slate plan as their implementation changes. History stops being an
executable prerequisite. Do not create a replacement receipt system under a
new name. Redeploy a previous working revision for operational rollback through
the same native workflow.
