## Accepted design

Remove every Website `createServerFn` wrapper, including settings. TanStack owns
routes, rendering and navigation. Local isomorphic loader branches select the
existing server runner or browser Atom runtime. Website backend reads share
Effect RPC declarations and Content/Training Schemas and errors. Public HTTP,
RPC and MCP APIs remain available.

```text
first HTML -> server loader -> existing runner -> private BACKEND /rpc
navigation/preload -> client loader -> existing Atom registry/runtime
                   -> checked public API /rpc
root setup -> Website cookie + checked bindings -> encoded initial data
           -> retained browser settings + live appearance
```

Server rendering waits for page text and metadata. Encoded success/error
results preserve named failures and response statuses. Browser data consumers
restore checked values as needed. There is no Website RPC proxy or settings RPC.

The [Alchemy example](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/full-stack-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/)
uses a proxy and AtomRpc.Service. This project instead reuses its existing
browser runtime and direct public API, checked against Effect 4.0.2 and Alchemy
2.0.0-beta.81. Those examples do not require changing the site's first render.

## Runtime and cancellation

The router creates a local browser registry before loaders; React uses that same
registry and releases it on final unmount. Development mount replay cancels a
scheduled disposal through Atom React's native scheduler. SSR uses its own
isolated registry. No Effect Context or registry is serialised into loader data.

Hydrated configuration atoms stay alive until registry disposal. A shared
resource atom builds the native RPC services in its Scope. Per-request atoms
let a cancelled navigation stop its own request without closing shared clients.
The sole browser loader bridge waits with AtomRegistry.getResult. Server
loaders combine router and incoming request cancellation. Appearance, progress,
analytics and WebMCP retain their separate acquisition rules in one runtime.

## Contracts and enforcement

Native NDJSON is used on both ends. Semantic client Layers provide Content and
Training; their generated client remains private. The checked getPage operation
retains exact format results and the complete default data response. Total-read
deadlines cover headers and body. Invalid native reply decoding uses a private
marker so an unrelated SchemaError defect is not rewritten as an expected error.

Canonical Commonplace guidance, starter and portable Oxlint checks are updated
together. Common Practice retains the exact portable rule bytes and hashes.
Real negative fixtures cover renamed imports, re-exports, alternate HTTP data
clients, extra runtimes and unguarded runtime calls. Positive fixtures retain
matching environment calls and ordinary HttpClient work.

## Qualification and delivery

- Reference sync: Effect 4.0.2 and Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81 verified against the lock.
- Focused native RPC tests cover complete pages, all four formats, image bytes,
  courses, all six Content failures and all four Training failures.
- Browser registry tests cover retained settings, shared transport, interruption
  and final cleanup; analytics acquisition remains independent.
- A real React StrictMode probe mounted the actual BrowserRegistry component:
  replay mounted twice and cleaned up once while keeping one acquired client
  alive. Final unmount disposed the registry once and released the client once.
- The actual browser loader bridge received an AbortController signal while
  its native GetPage request was paused. Aborting rejected the wait with Effect
  interruption and Chrome reported `net::ERR_ABORTED`, `canceled: true` for
  that same request. Temporary interception and the probe registry were removed.
- Local browser navigation showed direct API `/rpc/` POSTs and successful CORS.
  Training and existing saved progress rendered; WebMCP tools registered at the
  matching Website origin.
  Calling WebMCP get_page for Home SEO returned the checked variant through
  the same public RPC client. Dark appearance survived reload; the prior Light
  choice was then restored and all existing course progress remained unchanged.
- Hovering About made one direct GetPage request; clicking and returning with
  forward navigation within the existing 60-second window reused that result.
  Returning again after 78 seconds made a new GetPage request and rendered it.
- The hosted public suite against local development passed seven of eight
  tests, covering page bodies/metadata, HTTP/RPC/MCP, discovery and errors. The
  remaining assertion expects Cloudflare's static `noindex` header on the
  favicon, which Vite does not supply. Hosted Preview passed that check.
- Full Common Practice verification passed: 230 tests across 50 files, plus all
  required build, formatting, lint, type, Effect, unused-code and docs checks.
- Native Alchemy deployed Preview, then production. Each public suite passed
  all eight tests. Independent provider readback and hosted browser checks are
  recorded in the delivery record above.

Canonical Commonplace source is committed locally at
`cf8269dc983f5fbb4683a019f92f8b3995f7ff36`, with a minor Changeset and no published
version claim. Frozen install, full tests, full verification and the adversarial
repository-validator cases passed. A fresh rendered starter used pinned Bun
1.4.2, installed dependencies, finalised its receipt and passed its complete
verification, including the actual Oxlint command, types, tests and builds.
Repeating the build with Turbo's force option rebuilt all five packages/apps
successfully, without reusing the prior build result.

GitHub Actions are unavailable for this delivery. Use the normal local commands
and native Alchemy plan/apply, Preview first, without changing infrastructure
scope or bypassing protected release rules. Keep local checks, provider readback,
public checks and browser checks separate. Plugin source preparation is not a
published plugin release.

---
name: repo-structure
description: Scaffold, audit, migrate, or validate a strict Bun and Turbo TypeScript monorepo with a TanStack Start app, Effect v4 domain/RPC/HTTP API packages, live-types export conditions, Oxlint/Oxfmt, Vitest, Knip, docs, CI, and repository-owned skills. Use for repository topology, root tooling, workspace contracts, current dependency snapshots, app/runtime composition, or a new repo using the separate Website/API architecture. Do not use for an isolated package inside an established repository.
---

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.

Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
satisfy the generated repository's local references.

## Split folders and files by durable ownership

Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file
capability should stay a file when a folder would add no meaning.

- Start with actual callers, exports, tests, untrusted ingress, runtime
  composition, and provider/authority edges before moving a file.
- Name folders after capabilities/domains (`observability`, `cloudflare`, or
  `metrics-token-qualification`) and files after owned roles (`schemas.ts`,
  `errors.ts`, `service.ts`, `plan.ts`, `authority.ts`, `website.ts`, or
  `manifest.main.ts`).
- Do not scaffold every conventional file. Add `service.ts`, `live.layer.ts`,
  `test.layer.ts`, or `config.ts` only when a real service, resource Layer,
  deterministic test Layer, or durable configuration boundary exists.
- Keep tests beside app-internal owners or in the package's contract/test
  location; keep reusable fixtures in the package-approved testing owner.
  Reject `common/`, `shared/`, `helpers/`, and `utils/` dumping grounds.
- After a split, update imports, tests, architecture/README pointers, exports,
  and lifecycle/proof owners in the same slice. Preserve one canonical Schema,
  error, service, plan, and configuration owner.

## Enforce the separate Website/API architecture

Read the [TanStack, Effect and Alchemy architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md)
before composing apps. The scaffold uses the separate frontend/backend design:

- The domain package owns Schemas, failures, operations, source validation and
  live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and optional MCP reuse that owner.
- apps/api composes the live domain and native handler Layers in Alchemy's
  instance Scope. Incoming work keeps the native request fibre and cleanup.
  It has no ManagedRuntime or extra Promise runner.
- apps/web remains a standard TanStack Website. Server loaders call shared Effect RPC
  through a private service binding; browser loaders call the checked public
  API `/rpc` directly. Local isomorphic branches create no Website endpoint.
  Remove `createServerFn` wrappers, including settings, and add no `/rpc` proxy. Do not bundle a backend fallback or machine routes into it.
- Keep one frontend server runner and one React-mounted browser Atom graph.
  No Effect Context, request-service merge or tracer-hook workaround goes
  through TanStack. Use matching server/client environment functions for imports.
- Native client Layers implement the domain contract, keep generated clients
  private, preserve checked named errors and enforce a whole-read deadline.
- One native Alchemy stack deploys both apps with a matching API per stage.
  Preview never connects to Production. Bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` for each
  host's own origin; use native resource Outputs for another host's address.
  Never hard-code or construct a deployed website address. Keep Schema checks
  where resolved bindings enter application code. A chosen custom domain is
  valid infrastructure input, not a second application origin setting. Follow
  the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md).
- Every cross-workspace import uses explicit exports, including infrastructure.
- Routes and feature owners load data and choose error/workflow behaviour.
  Presentation components receive readonly values and action callbacks.
- Decode external input and encode outward values with their owning Schemas.
  Extract only demonstrated reuse, substantial work or a resource lifetime.

Check actual Worker startup after initialisation returns, response consumption
and cancellation, native-client errors and deadlines, real browser CORS and
bundle contents. Run negative Oxlint fixtures under the moved package paths;
a green typecheck or server call alone does not prove those connections.

## Add product analytics when required

For browser and backend PostHog analytics, read the
[application ownership and relay guide](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md). It
routes to the Alchemy lifecycle and Effect browser adapter owners. Keep analytics
optional: the base scaffold does not provision projects or start collection.

## Verify and maintain

Run in this order:

```bash
bun install
bun run format:check
bun run lint
bun run test:lint-rules
bun run check-types
bun run test
bun run build
python3 scripts/validate_repository.py /absolute/repository
```

Inspect export consumers and generated docs in addition to command status. Read
[maintenance](references/maintenance.md) before changing versions, assets,
profiles, rules, or skill baselines. Report exact commands, exit codes, and any
blocked upstream incompatibility; do not waive a failing compatibility fixture.
Use the generated docs-maintainer owner map and lifecycle/skill checks for
documentation impact, and retain a bounded impact receipt with explicit
non-claims.

## Immutable Effect and Schema ownership

Apply the canonical strict-effect-ts policy to all owned TypeScript, including
tests, tools, configuration and infrastructure. Use immutable Effect Array,
Record, HashMap and HashSet operations and exhaustive Match. For pure work use
folds/unfolds; for effectful work use a bounded sequential traversal or owned
Stream. Ref belongs to real changing state with a pure immutable update.

Every meaningful identifier/value and data record has one owning Schema with
inferred types. Reuse fields, brands and whole-record checks across codecs;
decode actual external input/replies once, construct new constrained values
with checked constructors and named errors, and trust typed internal contracts.
Domain absence is Option. Preserve historical source formats, missing/null
distinctions and hashes when changing a codec. Internal caches use full readonly
address records, tested with installed equality/hash and cancellation rules.

Enable the portable no-imperative-collections rule alongside the existing
rules; prove it through actual negative and valid Oxlint fixtures in app,
package, tests, tools and config paths. Document precise host operation/property
allowances, never a whole-file or wildcard mutation waiver. Keep the native API
request execution and cleanup and the one exact TanStack server runner. Templates
are examples qualified at their snapshot; research a v4 clone and reconcile with
installed source/types before applying them to another Effect version.

# Website RPC delivery — 11 October 2026

The Website RPC change was deployed to Preview, checked, then deployed to
production using the native Alchemy CLI. GitHub Actions were not used.

## Checked source

- Common Practice: `29e88f4cc3cf2d45487238ebde775acea3d4f090` on
  `codex/website-effect-rpc`.
- Canonical Commonplace plugin preparation:
  `cf8269dc983f5fbb4683a019f92f8b3995f7ff36` on the same branch name in
  `commonplace-plugins`. Its minor Changeset is prepared locally. No plugin
  version, tag or release was published, and neither branch was pushed.
- Effect 4.0.2 and Alchemy 2.0.0-beta.81 reference clones matched the committed
  reference lock. No dependency upgrade was part of this change.
- The copied portable Oxlint rule matches the canonical source byte for byte;
  its source commit and hash are recorded in `docs/sources`.

The [implementation plan](../../exec-plans/website-rpc-data-loading.md),
[architecture](../../../ARCHITECTURE.md) and
[ADR 0002](../../adr/0002-api-owned-publishing.md) explain the design.

## Local checks

`bun run verification` passed on the Common Practice source above: build,
formatting, actual Oxlint checks, TypeScript, Effect checks, all 230 tests in
50 files, unused-code checks and documentation checks. Effect reported no
errors or warnings; its informational suggestions remained informational.

The native RPC tests cover complete default page data, all four response
formats, image bytes, courses and all declared Content and Training failures.
They distinguish malformed responses from connection failures, retain unrelated
defects, enforce complete-read deadlines and check cancellation.

The canonical plugin passed frozen installation, full tests, full verification
and the repository validator's negative cases. A fresh starter was rendered,
installed using its pinned Bun 1.4.2 and had its receipt finalised. Its complete
verification passed, including 15 policy tests and 25 application/package tests.
A forced repeat build rebuilt all five packages/apps successfully.

## Local browser checks

- Hovering About made one direct public API read. Clicking and forward
  navigation within 60 seconds reused it; returning after 78 seconds fetched
  it again. No Website server-function request was needed.
- The real BrowserRegistry component survived React development replay with
  one acquired client. Final unmount disposed the registry and released the
  client once each.
- Cancelling the real loader's AbortController interrupted its wait and the
  matching browser request ended with `net::ERR_ABORTED`, `canceled: true`.
  Temporary interception and test resources were removed afterwards.
- Dark appearance survived reload. The previous Light choice was restored;
  existing training progress remained unchanged.
- A real WebMCP get_page call returned Home SEO through the shared RPC client.

Running the hosted public suite against local Vite passed seven of eight tests.
The remaining assertion expected Cloudflare's static-file `noindex` header on
the favicon. It passed on hosted Preview. The local development server was
stopped after these checks.

## Native deployment and independent Cloudflare readback

Both stage plans contained exactly two Worker updates, with no creation,
deletion or adoption. Native apply reported two successful updates in each
stage. Production's existing domain and security resources were unchanged.

| Stage | Worker | Active version, serving 100% |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preview | `common-practice-preview` | `06fbd6de-4db1-4966-ad2a-294047f237f8` |
| Preview | `common-practice-preview-backend` | `47fde92b-16e4-4122-a5f2-9ff2b5279f24` |
| Production | `common-practice-production` | `d0facac9-d48e-448e-a76d-f1267ca73ba7` |
| Production | `common-practice-production-backend` | `867ea3e6-25c8-4039-a49f-6447ac08d800` |

Cloudflare recorded the Preview deployments at 03:31 UTC and production at
03:58 UTC on 11 October. Independent readback confirmed each Website's BACKEND
binding points to its own stage's API. Preview public addresses use the matching
workers.dev hosts; production uses `withcommonpractice.com` and
`api.withcommonpractice.com`. Existing Alchemy ownership tags remained present.

Both stages retained enabled logs and traces, sampling rate 1, persistence and
their existing Axiom destination names. This readback proves saved settings;
new stored Axiom or PostHog events were not queried during this delivery.

### Separate pre-existing Preview finding

Before and after deployment, the Preview API retained two old secret bindings:
`COMMON_PRACTICE_AXIOM_METRICS_TOKEN` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_HEADERS`.
Current source neither declares nor uses them. Native deployment retained them;
no direct provider write was used to remove them. This remains a separate
cleanup item, not a claim that Preview matches the no-exporter-binding rule.
Neither production Worker has these bindings. No secret values were read or

# Separate Website and API: TanStack, Effect and Alchemy

TanStack owns Website routing, HTML rendering and thin frontend loaders.
The native Effect API owns domain operations and HTTP, RPC and remote MCP.
Alchemy owns both Workers and their stage-specific connection.

```text
alchemy.run.ts
  -> apps/api: native Worker -> shared handlers -> domain live Layer
  -> apps/web: standard Website.Vite -> frontend runner -> semantic Effect RPC client
React root -> browser Effect Atom runtime -> public Effect RPC client
```

## Own the feature once

The domain package owns Schemas, brands, named errors, the service, source
validation and live/test Layers. Authored sources may have their own source-only
package; it owns files and inventory, not a second set of domain types.
HTTP, RPC and MCP packages reuse the domain exports. Their handlers call the
service and their client Layers implement that same checked service contract.
Packages never import an app or start a runtime.

The API supplies host adapters and builds the live domain and handler Layers
once in Alchemy's Worker-instance Scope. It does not add a ManagedRuntime or
Promise runner. Incoming HTTP work runs in the host's Effect fibre. Request
cancellation and response streams keep their request lifetime; never capture
HttpServerRequest, an event Scope or a request tracer in instance-wide services.
Keep native HttpEffect response mapping for routing errors, cancellation and
defects. A blanket catch returning 500 turns a missing route into a server
error. In beta.81, qualify `Http.safeHttpEffect` at the API boundary with a
safe reporter visible to that mapper's catch; a reporter inside only the route
still leaves the host's raw-Cause fallback active. Capture only the checked
reporter set and provide that service, preserving the incoming request Scope.
Keep its required synchronous callback fixed-field only, without another
runner, and prove safe logs as well as safe client responses.

Workerd has no guaranteed isolate shutdown callback. Beta.79 never closes its
instance Scope, so shared-resource finalisers cannot be relied on to run.
Keep resources needing guaranteed release in the request or response-stream
Scope. A synthetic instance-close test proves ownership, not hosted shutdown.

The Website supplies the semantic Effect RPC client with a private service-binding
transport to its own stage's API. Its one server runner serves every TanStack
entry point. It imports no domain live Layer, authored source loader, renderer,
HTTP/RPC server or remote MCP server. Use `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient`
from the published `alchemy/Cloudflare/Bridge` runtime entry for the private
binding. Keep host capability checks and named failures in the adapter; upstream
owns Promise and HTTP conversion. Import `cloudflare:workers` normally in a
separate live ingress, with checked env reads during operations. Node tests can
then exercise the adapter without mocking the host module. No custom transport,
dynamic import, package-export patch or second client stack is needed.

Browser calls use the public API address checked by the root loader and the
same native RPC group and NDJSON serialisation. React mounts one Effect Atom graph and releases
registrations and pending work on unmount. Import server and browser runtimes
inside TanStack's matching environment functions as well as using matching
filenames. Inspect the real browser build for server dependencies.

Keep optional browser services independently acquired inside that graph when
their dependencies or lifetime differ. Follow the strict Effect
[React lifecycle](../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md#react-lifecycle)
and [initial JavaScript and fonts](../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md#initial-javascript-and-fonts)
guidance before joining startup work, adding lazy imports or changing font
loading. The scaffold does not add analytics or browser tools by default.

## Keep the Website a frontend

Use standard Website.Vite. Do not add a custom Alchemy entry around TanStack,
Register.server.requestContext, Effect Context injection, request-service
merging, borrowed tracer hooks or backend machine routes to the Website.
Website data loaders use local `createIsomorphicFn` branches. Remove every
`createServerFn` page, training or settings wrapper: those create an unnecessary
remote Website API. Keep local cookie/configuration reads in the server branch.
The browser calls its checked public API `/rpc` directly; do not add a Website
`/rpc` proxy. Public HTTP APIs, downloads, publishing and analytics may still
use native HttpClient in their actual owners.
Use Cloudflare's automatic request/fetch traces for the standard Website and
`Cloudflare.Telemetry()` for the native API in its incoming request fibre.
Qualify the installed native paths before adding any custom tracing adapter.

Preserve tags and fields through TanStack using a Schema-checked success/error
result. Do not rely on thrown error prototypes surviving JSON serialisation.
Expected errors, invalid replies and unavailable transport have named types;
interruption and unexpected defects stay at their owning host boundary.

Native generated HTTP/RPC clients can return a union even when a request field
selects one response. A small domain-owned operation checks the requested
variant before promising its exact type. Optional input defaults must appear
in both decoding and tool descriptions. See the strict Effect
[format-selected example](../../strict-effect-ts/references/examples/format-selected-client.md).

The router starter preloads links on intent and reuses loaded/preloaded data
for one minute. These are `createRouter` settings, separate from Vite and HTTP
cache headers. Read the strict Effect [router freshness guidance](../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md#router-preloading-and-freshness)
before changing loader caching or investigating repeated navigation requests.

## Optional Website-owned analytics ingress

A fixed same-origin browser analytics relay may remain in the Website, using its
existing server runner and native Effect HTTP client. It is provider ingress for
the Website client, not a second domain API. Follow the
[PostHog ownership and relay guide](../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md) before adding this
narrow route; backend capture stays with the native API. The scaffold does not
add analytics or this route by default.

## Deploy each stage as a pair

One root native Alchemy stack deploys both apps. Every local, Preview and
Production Website has its own API address and private binding. Prefer ordinary
stage-owned Website Workers when native parent Previews cannot provide required
settings; do not patch the provider to reproduce that support. Its API Worker
is independent and must never point to Production. One stack coordinates updates; it does not make
their activation atomic. Admit public domains and production resources only
under the repository's explicit decisions and authority.

Keep shared deployment Schemas with their real package owner and consume public
exports. A host's own origin comes from `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` on that host's
`env`. Another host's address comes from its native resource Output. Do not
copy a custom domain or construct a `workers.dev` or local address for
application configuration. Keep Schema checks when the resolved values enter
application code. In beta.81, Output.mapEffect cannot carry expected decoding
errors; do not erase them with Effect.orDie. An Action is for a bounded
operation, not a pure address selection. After an authorised apply, a fresh
native plan should recognise unchanged bindings. See the
[website origin rules](../../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md#website-origin-rules).

## Check the running connections

Use the native Worker entry in a startup test. Return from initialisation,
then make multiple requests and consume or cancel a response. Prove shared
services survive request cleanup. In a controlled host, close the synthetic
instance Scope to prove ownership; do not claim workerd closes that Scope.
Deployment-only services must not be required by the uploaded Worker; use the
installed Alchemy build/runtime mechanism and recheck it on upgrades.

Test HTTP and RPC with their actual native clients. Check encoded errors,
invalid responses, requested variants, complete-read deadlines and interruption.
A deadline covers response headers and the decoded body, with one total budget.
Use TestClock for a late header followed by a stalled body and for earlier
caller cancellation. Do not add automatic retries accidentally.

Use the browser's actual outgoing headers to test CORS preflight, including
native tracing headers such as b3 and traceparent in the qualified version.
Then perform an actual browser read or tool call. Server-only public checks
cannot prove a browser can call the API. WebMCP registers only at the matching
Website origin; public remote MCP has its own checked Origin/CORS policy.

Run real negative Oxlint fixtures under moved package paths. Keep adapter
exceptions confined to exact files. Local checks, native apply, exact-stage
provider readback, public calls and browser calls remain separate evidence.
Follow the Alchemy [hosted telemetry guide](../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md)
for signal ownership and limits; the scaffold itself proves no hosted delivery.

# Cloudflare

## Contents

- [Ownership decisions](#ownership-decisions)
- [File ownership](#file-ownership)
- [Worker and asset semantics](#worker-and-asset-semantics)
- [Routes zones and domains](#routes-zones-and-domains)
- [Bindings and storage](#bindings-and-storage)
- [Website origin rules](#website-origin-rules)
- [Secrets](#secrets)
- [Observability](#observability)
- [State](#state)
- [Readback checklist](#readback-checklist)

## Ownership decisions

Declare which system owns each Cloudflare lifecycle:

- Worker or static-asset deployment;
- routes and custom domains;
- DNS/zone configuration;
- R2, D1, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, or Secrets Store;
- environment secrets and bindings;
- logs, metrics, traces, and observability destinations;
- remote state infrastructure.

Do not assume Alchemy owns all Cloudflare resources because it owns one Worker.

## File ownership

For a small graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare.ts
```

For a substantial graph:

```text
src/lib/build/cloudflare/
  stack.ts
  website.ts
  worker.ts
  storage.ts
  routes.ts
  secrets.ts
  observability.ts
```

Keep stage/config Schemas outside provider declarations when other providers share them.

## Worker and asset semantics

Make asset routing policy explicit. In particular, distinguish asset-first and Worker-first behaviour and test the intended choice. A deployed Worker and green CI do not prove that static assets return the correct content type or bypass the Worker.

Test:

- root document;
- hashed CSS and JavaScript assets;
- missing assets;
- API paths;
- redirects;
- cache headers;
- content types;
- route precedence.

Record compatibility date, compatibility flags, runtime limits, module format, and bundler inputs in a stable typed owner. Keep application and deployment configuration aligned through one contract or an invariant test.

## Routes, zones, and domains

Treat a zone or domain as foreign unless this repository creates and owns it.

- Read the target zone before applying routes.
- Adopt only under explicit authority.
- Default adopted zones and routes to retain.
- Restrict Production route adoption to the Production stage.
- Reject a route whose account/zone does not match the authority record.
- Read back the route pattern and bound Worker after apply.
- Prove the public host independently.

Do not infer route correctness from a Worker URL.

## Bindings and storage

Model each binding as typed desired state:

- binding name;
- resource kind;
- physical resource identity;
- stage/environment;
- creation/adoption policy;
- removal policy.

Assert that application code and deployment configuration use the same binding names. For Durable Objects, include class name, migration/tag policy, and deployment sequencing. For R2/D1/KV, make data retention explicit and default destructive deletion to forbidden until authorised.

## Website origin rules

An origin is the protocol and host, with an optional port, such as
`http://127.0.0.1:3210`. The deployed host owns that address. Applications must
never hard-code it or build it from a stage, Worker name, account subdomain,
custom domain or development port.

For Alchemy `2.0.0-beta.81`, use the native self URL binding on the host that
needs its own address:

```typescript
const website =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Website.Vite("Website", {
    rootDir: "apps/web",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });

// The same binding works in a native Worker declaration.
const api =
  yield *
  Cloudflare.Worker("Api", {
    main: "./src/worker.ts",
    env: { PUBLIC_ORIGIN: Cloudflare.Worker.URL },
  });
```

Alchemy resolves this binding to the local development proxy during local
development, the deployed `workers.dev` address, or the configured custom
domain. Do not add separate local/cloud address formulas or a copied-address
fallback. For Vite browser code, a `VITE_`-prefixed self URL binding uses the
same native resolution before the client bundle is built.

It is valid to declare a chosen custom domain as infrastructure input, for
example `domain: "app.example.com"`. Keep the application's own
`PUBLIC_ORIGIN` bound to `Cloudflare.Worker.URL`; do not repeat that domain in
its environment or build `"https://" + domain` there. Aliases and incoming
request origins are separate from the host's configured canonical address.

The native Effect Worker host supplies a ConfigProvider from its resolved
bindings. Application Layers consume the address with
`yield* Config.schema(OwnedOrigin, "PUBLIC_ORIGIN")` during runtime startup.
Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure route Layers, or read it while constructing an
existing service with `Layer.effect`. Reuse the host provider, owning Schema
and [general configuration pattern](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/services/config-and-secrets.md#read-settings-in-the-owning-layer)
instead of adding an address-only Context service. For a Website whose framework
does not supply that provider, use its existing narrow host adapter to check
owned bindings and pass only public settings to the browser.

Beta.79 also supports `yield* Cloudflare.Worker.URL` in native Worker
initialisation. That yield attaches the binding and returns a deferred Effect,
not the address string. Running the returned Effect requires the native
`RuntimeContext`, where the binding is populated. Check the phase and lifetime
before using this accessor; the explicit env binding plus checked Config is the
startup path above. Do not read runtime bindings during graph planning or add a
new runtime to obtain them.

For a different host, use that resource's native Output, such as `api.url`.
Pass the Output to the receiving resource; check its resolved value with the
owning Schema when application code reads the binding. If the native address
can be absent, preserve that absence as `null` for an env binding and reject it
with the Schema. Do not replace an absent Output with a guessed address.

Keep expected validation failures typed. Beta.79's `Output.mapEffect` callback
accepts no expected errors, so do not force Schema decoding into it with
`Effect.orDie`. `Output.map` may select a checked resource attribute or represent
absence; it must not reconstruct the hostname. Resolve and decode Outputs
separately before writing workflow or receipt values.

Check the selected Alchemy version's self URL, Vite, native Worker and local
provider APIs before copying this example. See the
[matching primary sources](../sources.md#cloudflare-website-origins).
Local source/type checks do not prove live domain routing.

## Separate Website and native API Workers

Use standard Website.Vite for the frontend and a native Effect Worker for the
API. The root stack deploys both with exact same-stage service/public bindings.
Preview has its own API; a Website preview parent does not authorise using the
Production API. Do not wrap TanStack in a backend Worker or recreate an API
runtime around the native incoming request fibre.

Check the installed Alchemy build/runtime mechanism before reading deployment
services in a Worker declaration. The qualified beta.81 runtime build guard
removes stack-only requirements from the uploaded entry. Test the real native
entry without those services, return from startup, then request and release
resources. A typecheck or successful upload alone does not prove startup.

Test browser CORS with the native client's actual headers and an actual browser
call. Tracing headers b3 and traceparent are part of the qualified client's
request; disabling tracing to avoid preflight is not a correction. Separate
remote MCP Origin validation from matching-origin Website WebMCP registration.

## Preview environments without provider patches

Check the installed ordinary Worker and Worker Preview providers separately.
A declared observability type or an existing Preview retaining earlier settings
does not prove that a newly created Preview receives those settings. Check both
create and update paths and read back a new deployment.

When required Preview settings lack native support, consider an ordinary
stage-owned Website Worker alongside its stage-owned API before patching the
provider. Keep exact stage names, self URL bindings and native log/trace
destinations. This changes the Preview URL and teardown owner; confirm that
tradeoff. For a mode change, use a distinct native resource identity, such as
`Namespace.push`, and inspect the create/delete plan so the former parent cannot
be overwritten. Preserve production identities and shared state.

Ordinary workers.dev Websites need their own indexing policy. Cloudflare's
[`_headers` file](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/headers/)
covers static assets; it does not cover Worker-generated replies. Apply the
checked stage policy through the existing framework response adapter, test
pages, errors, machine replies and assets, and keep production indexable.
Update CI addresses, Preview comments and trace queries for distinct Worker
names while preserving historical Preview records.

## Secrets

Prefer provider-managed secret references or Secrets Store bindings over plaintext workflow values.

- Acquire credentials through redacted Config.
- Validate secret binding names and stage.
- Never emit values in plans, logs, outputs, or receipts.
- Separate credential issuance from resource apply.
- Read back metadata or binding presence, never the secret.
- Revoke disposable credentials after lifecycle proof.

Removing a secret declaration may leave the old binding on the deployed Worker.
Check the active version's binding names and types; a no-change plan does not
prove removal. Prefer a supported native Alchemy deletion operation. If the
installed provider has none, record the residue and request an exact one-off
ownership exception before a provider write. Do not introduce a dependency
patch, custom resource or placeholder secret to conceal the gap. Keep shared
token revocation separate from binding removal. See the
[hosted telemetry cutover](../effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Observability

Cloudflare platform observability and application telemetry are separate sources.

For Cloudflare-native logs or destinations:

- identify Worker/service/environment/stage;
- define retention and sampling;
- read back the destination/binding;
- query the downstream provider.

For Effect OTLP export:

- keep endpoint/token in a redacted binding;
- decode the binding at application ingress;
- attach one exporter Layer to the runtime;
- preserve `waitUntil` or the host completion mechanism;
- test transport wiring;
- query Axiom independently before claiming ingestion.

## State

If Cloudflare backs Alchemy state, document bootstrap and recovery. Do not create a circular dependency between the state backend and the graph it stores. Use a separate bootstrap stack or a tested provider-supported mechanism where necessary.

Start with the installed native `Cloudflare.state()` setup and maintenance
behaviour. In the qualified beta.80 source, `--yes` permits automatic creation
and upgrades; pending setup can also be recovered. An existing-only rule is a
separate project choice. Check it before building a custom state client. Native
Website `domain.redirects` likewise has shared-list and failure semantics that
must be understood before promising stronger preservation. See
[native migrations](../operations/native-migrations.md#start-with-the-standard-behaviour)
and its pinned sources.

## Readback checklist

After apply, query the Cloudflare API for:

- account and zone identity;
- Worker/script/service name;
- deployment/version identifier where available;
- routes/domains;
- bindings and safe resource IDs;
- compatibility settings;
- observability configuration;
- storage resource presence.

Then run the public route/asset journey. Report any unavailable readback as a non-claim.

### Website loader transport

For a separate TanStack Website/native API, use shared Effect RPC declarations
for Website data reads. The server supplies Alchemy's public
`fromCloudflareFetcher`/`toHttpClient` private same-stage binding transport;
the browser supplies credential-free FetchHttpClient at its checked public API
`/rpc`. Keep native NDJSON on both ends. Local `createIsomorphicFn` branches
choose the existing server runner or existing browser Atom runtime. Remove
TanStack server functions and Website `/rpc` forwarding routes for these reads.
Website cookies and checked public settings are local setup, not backend RPC.

The official [full-stack example](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/frontend/full-stack-tanstack-rpc-drizzle/)
uses a Website proxy and AtomRpc.Service. Those are example choices, not required
RPC architecture. Do not copy them over an existing root Atom runtime or a
public read-only API. Follow the [repository architecture](https://github.com/crcorbett/commonplace-plugins/blob/main/plugins/development-workflows/skills/repo-structure/references/tanstack-effect.md)
and [React ownership](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/applications/react-and-tanstack.md)
for the qualified direct-browser variation. Public HTTP and MCP APIs, publishing
and analytics retain their existing owners. Verify private SSR, browser CORS,
complete initial HTML, interrupted reads and exact stage bindings separately.

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.

Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
satisfy the generated repository's local references.

## Split folders and files by durable ownership

Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file

## Keep render pure

React components should be total render functions over props, decoded loader/query state, and declared hooks. Do not:

- run Effect during render;
- construct live Layers during render;
- access server Config/secrets;
- call raw provider clients;
- mutate global state;
- create unmanaged Promise side effects.

JSX and pure view transformations may remain plain TypeScript.

## Server and client runtimes

Keep separate composition:

- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.

Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.

Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.

For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
Effect fibre without another runtime.

Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Loaders and actions

Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:

1. decode params/search/body/session;
2. call a named Effect service operation;
3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
4. encode hydration-safe data;
5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.

Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.

## TanStack Query

Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.

Define intentionally:

- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
- invalidation after mutation;
- server prefetch/hydration encoding.

Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.

## TanStack Router/Start

Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.

For serialisable loader data:

- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
- prove all error variants are handled.

Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
transport, including an error response status.

### Router preloading and freshness

Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
page can render immediately while a return starts another API RPC
request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.

For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.

Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
separate owners. An API reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.

Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.

## Initial JavaScript and fonts

Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.

Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.

For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.

Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.

## React lifecycle

For subscriptions/streams:

- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
- scope to mount/route lifetime;
- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
- encode backpressure/sampling;
- update view state through a controlled adapter.

Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.

When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
An optional registration/subscription pattern is
`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
not required for purely synchronous local UI state.

Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
state or cleanup has a real owner.

Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.

Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.

## State

Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.

Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.

## Errors

Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:

- not found;
- unauthorised;
- validation fields;
- unavailable/retry;
- conflict;
- unexpected defect boundary.

Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.

## Tests

Test:

- domain service independently;
- loader/action decoding and encoding;
- runtime bridge and cancellation;
- hydration round-trip;
- retry ownership;
- subscription cleanup;
- no server dependency in client bundle;
- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
  a stalled unrelated service;
- exhaustive UI error states.

## Direct RPC loaders for a separate Website and API

```text
first request -> Website server loader -> one server runner
              -> shared RPC client -> private BACKEND -> API RPC -> domain
later navigation/preload -> same loader's client branch
              -> one root Atom registry/runtime -> public API /rpc -> domain
local setup -> server cookie + checked bindings -> encoded root data
            -> retained browser config/appearance atoms (no settings RPC)
```

Use the same RPC declarations, domain Schemas and named failures in both
branches. `createIsomorphicFn().server(serverCallback).client(clientCallback)`
selects local code; it does not create an endpoint. Do not use `createServerFn`,
an alternate HTTP API data client, a Website RPC proxy, or `AtomRpc.Service`
when an existing Atom runtime owns browser work. Native `AtomRpc.Service`
constructs a runtime; its convenience does not justify a second one.

The router starts before React. Create one browser registry in the router's
client branch and pass that local registry through ordinary typed router
context. This is not an Effect Context and must never enter loader data.
React uses that exact registry through native `RegistryContext.Provider`.
SSR uses an isolated native RegistryProvider; there is no module-global mutable
registry. Close the browser registry at final root unmount. The starter uses
Atom React's cancellable scheduler so development mount/cleanup replay can
cancel pending disposal. Qualify replay, final unmount and outstanding requests.

Seed checked root setup once with `useAtomInitialValues`. Seeded configuration
atoms must be kept alive: otherwise Atom may remove an unread value before a
later loader starts and silently restore its empty default. Keep local
appearance/progress independent of remote-client acquisition. Browser root
reloads read live local appearance and stored checked configuration; do not
ask the API to read a Website cookie.

A scoped resource atom builds the static semantic RPC client Layer using
`Layer.build`, a checked stage address, native `RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp`
and the same serialisation as the API. A named request atom runs each loader
operation using those services. One named browser host bridge waits with
`AtomRegistry.getResult` and `Effect.runPromise(..., { signal })`; it starts
no ManagedRuntime. Cancellation removes that subscription and releases the
request atom. The server combines the incoming request and router signals
and uses its existing runner. Keep per-request atoms separate from the retained
shared client so cancellation does not close another caller's transport.

Await server page data before constructing headings, canonical metadata and
status. Encode complete success/error loader results with their owner Schema;
restore them on the browser side where types such as Option/errors differ.
Never stringify Cause or infer a selected response variant from the request.
Use the domain's checked format operation, including its default complete data.

Qualification must cover all declared error variants with their fields, exact
successful result types, actual native RPC round trips, malformed JSON/schema
replies versus unavailable transport, format mismatches, total-read deadlines,
cancellation and unrelated defects. In Effect 4.0.2, invalid native exit-schema
decoding may surface as a defect. Mark only that native reply-decoder failure
and translate that private marker; never catch every SchemaError defect as an
invalid reply. Keep native NDJSON and exit codecs, not handwritten RPC frames.

Use actual Oxlint fixtures for aliases and re-exports. Enable the portable
`website-rpc-boundary` on Website source and `module-ownership` for alternate
HTTP data clients and server implementations. It admits only `runtime` at the
exact server owner and `browserRuntime` at the exact client owner. TypeScript
prevents a second declaration of those names. It rejects server-function
imports/re-exports, RPC proxy routes, ad hoc generated clients and unguarded
runtime calls; it deliberately permits legitimate native HTTP work. Dynamic
module ownership and source-package bans remain separate checks. Neither lint
nor a local build proves hosted CORS, native binding startup, first HTML,
navigation/preload freshness, restoration or deployed stage pairing.
