# Common Practice foundation review

Use Common Practice's application structure and ordinary development workflow.
Prioritise the Cloudflare Website and API, remove every Alchemy patch, and remove
TaxKit's separate receipt and approval machinery. Keep Bun as a supported,
secondary host over the same calculation packages.

```text
Website server/browser -> checked RPC operations -> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP -----------------------------> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Local SDK ----------------------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core

Native API declaration -> Website declaration
                    API address + private binding -> Website
Reverse Website address dependency: decision still open below
Git commit/PR -> ordinary checks -> native Alchemy -> deployed Website/API
                               Doppler supplies stage-specific secrets
```

The comparison uses TaxKit commit `f899c963f463d2283517e908febcfa3ebb1dd442`,
Common Practice commit `54a62a5d64892ee2304260f51ef683fb299deea7`, and Commonplace
`development-workflows` 0.6.11, checked against its published release on
10 October 2026. This document and its [plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
replace the large, uncommitted audit packet created during this review.

This remains the agreed research and design stage. Application code, dependency
This records the design choice; the package code has not yet changed.

The Layer change also covers public `TakeHomeScenarioLiveFromInput` and
`AnnualTaxScenarioLiveFromInput`, used by calculator composition and package
consumers. Keep their checked scenario inputs and tax behaviour, but migrate
callable Layer helper signatures through normal package/versioning work. Do not
claim every helper signature can stay unchanged while enforcing no factories.

## Lint that enforces the design

The current published portable Effect asset contains thirteen rules. TaxKit's
executable `.agents` copy and Common Practice's vendor copy contain an older
eleven-rule set. The current asset adds `static-layers` and `module-ownership`,
and strengthens alias/scope handling. Common Practice separately enforces some
of these in its own rules. Copying both collections would leave overlap and old
product-specific assumptions.

Use one unchanged copy of the current portable asset under
`tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect`, with a short source/version note. Keep only
useful TaxKit extensions and adapt Common Practice's ownership checks to actual
TaxKit paths. Do not edit installed plugin caches or add a digest/receipt system.
TaxKit's newer Oxlint 1.86.0, Ultracite 7.12.2 and Effect tooling 0.48.0 do not
need downgrading to Common Practice's versions to adopt its approach.

| Check | Adoption and limit |
| --- | --- |
| Static Layers and runtime calls | Enable current portable rules across owned apps, packages, tools, tests and root configuration. Keep exact server/browser/SDK runtime paths. The SDK's private Promise runtime remains its public library adapter. |
| Host and private module ownership | Configure `module-ownership` for Alchemy, Cloudflare bindings, private SDKs and authored/generated content. Include re-exports, type imports and dynamic imports. Current TaxKit host checks miss Alchemy and `cloudflare:workers`. Source checks do not establish bundle contents. |
| Promise and HTTP adapters | Exact file/operation permissions only. Use native Alchemy binding conversion first; retain custom handling only for the actual trusted-call/reply policy it cannot supply. Keep TaxKit's checked error mapping for necessary `tryPromise`. No exemption for every Layer file or test. Extend raw-fetch restrictions across owned source. |
| Decoding and transport restoration | Retain TaxKit's lexical boundary rules and their effective two-pass suppression protection. They cover useful cases beyond the portable rules. A comment labelled `SAFETY` does not authorise a type assertion. |
| State and collections | Keep portable restrictions plus TaxKit's stronger alias/Object/Reflect write checks. Managed state uses Effect Ref/collections; a pure immutable fold does not need a Ref. Native Alchemy `Output.map` and `Namespace.push` already have targeted handling; no broad exception is needed. |
| Package imports and exports | Derive ownership from real nested workspace manifests, using the longest matching package root. Check exported subpaths and frontend-to-backend direction. The scaffold's one-level package scan would merge `packages/api/http` and `packages/api/rpc` incorrectly. Preserve source/types/default export conditions and SDK packed-consumer checks. |
| Named operations and Schema ownership | Adapt to actual TaxKit service owners. Common Practice's old instrumentation rule names obsolete services, so copying it does not enforce TaxKit methods. Type checks and focused review still establish Schema-derived contracts; a regex cannot establish this by itself. |
| Config and absence | Use owning `Config.schema` declarations for constrained settings. Native `Config.Boolean` is valid for a plain flag. Fix old template scans that miss current spellings and nested packages. Handle Option explicitly; native protocol/compiler nulls may stay inside their adapters. |
| Actual Effect diagnostics | Replace the single compatibility example with strict diagnostics over the real app/package/tool projects and root Alchemy entry. Elevate meaningful diagnostics such as floating Effects and missing service dependencies, following Common Practice. Keep ordinary TypeScript checking. |

# Strict Effect TypeScript

Treat Effect as the application language for every fallible, asynchronous, stateful, concurrent, resourceful, configuration-dependent, or boundary-crossing workflow. Allow plain TypeScript only for total, deterministic leaf computation and unavoidable host adapters.

Use this skill with repository-local instructions, `$repo-structure`, `$package-structure`, and `$effect-client-wrapper` where applicable. Use `$alchemy-iac` for infrastructure ownership, provider proof, and deployment lifecycle.

## Strictness level

This skill is intentionally stricter than ordinary Effect guidance.

In owned code, do not introduce:

- `async` or raw `Promise` orchestration;
- thrown domain or expected operational errors;
- raw `fetch` or an exposed SDK client;
- direct `process.env`, `Bun.env`, `import.meta.env`, or platform binding reads below a host adapter;
- unchecked `JSON.parse`, type assertions, `any`, or manual `unknown` narrowing;
- nullable domain models after ingress;
- `Date.now`, `new Date()` as a clock, `Math.random`, unmanaged timers, or sleeps;
- `console.*` for application telemetry;
- mutable local or global collections, loops, reassignment, raw `Map`/`Set`, or detached background work;
- repeated decoding of already checked domain values or JSON keys for an internal cache;
- copied primitive refinements or handwritten data types that compete with an owning Schema;
- generic callback escape hatches such as `request<T>(fn)`, `run<T>(callback)`, or `withClient(fn)`;
- package-owned runtimes or repeated `Effect.runPromise`;
- provider objects, wire DTOs, or primitive configuration crossing service boundaries.

A narrow host callback may be synchronous or Promise-shaped only when a framework requires it. Adapt it immediately to an Effect program, provide one application-owned runtime, and execute only at that boundary. Document any other exception beside the code with its host constraint, containment, and test.

## Allowed plain TypeScript

Keep plain TypeScript for:

- total pure functions over already-decoded values;
- type declarations and static constants;
- JSX and framework declarations that do not perform effects;
- immutable transformations using Effect Array, Record, HashMap and HashSet functions;
- the smallest adapter signature required by a host framework;
- performance-sensitive native data structures proven by measurement and encapsulated behind an Effect service.

Plain does not mean unchecked. Boundary data still requires Schema, failure still requires a typed error channel, and effects still require the application runtime.

Read [policy and exceptions](references/architecture/policy-and-exceptions.md).

## Mandatory workflow

### 1. Inspect the exact codebase

Before editing:

1. Read repository and package instructions.
2. Inspect the receiving repository's installed Effect version and exports. Research the cloned v4 source when available, record its revision, then check every chosen API against installed source/types and behaviour. The canonical template snapshot qualifies 4.0.2; it does not choose an upgrade for another repository.
3. Find existing schemas, errors, services, Layers, runtimes, test Layers, and observability.
4. Identify the current package boundary and intended public API.
5. Search the change surface for strictness violations.
6. Preserve unrelated dirty worktree changes.

When documentation and installed types disagree, follow the installed package, then record any compatibility decision.

### 2. Classify every operation

For each operation, identify:

- value success type;
- expected error union;
- service requirements;
- external inputs that need decoding;
- resource lifetime;
- concurrency and interruption behaviour;
- retry and timeout policy;
- logging, span, and metric semantics;
- runtime owner.

Use this translation:

| Vanilla TypeScript         | Required Effect model                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `async` / `Promise`        | `Effect`, `Effect.gen`, `Effect.fn`; `tryPromise` only at ingress                               |
| `throw`                    | typed `Effect.fail`; defect only for impossible invariant failure                               |
| `T \| null \| undefined`   | decode once, then `Option<T>` where absence is semantic                                         |
| environment strings        | `Config` plus `Schema` refinement                                                               |
| JSON / `unknown`           | Schema decode and encode                                                                        |
| `fetch`                    | Effect Platform `HttpClient` or a private typed adapter                                         |
| provider SDK               | private `live.layer.ts`; decode every output                                                    |
| filesystem / child process | Effect Platform services in a private Layer                                                     |
| time / retry               | `Clock`, `Duration`, `Schedule`, timeout                                                        |
| randomness / identifiers   | Effect Random or an injected service                                                            |
| mutable state              | `Ref`, `SynchronizedRef`, `SubscriptionRef`; `TxRef` inside `Effect.tx` for coordinated updates |
| `Map` / `Set` domain state | `HashMap`, `HashSet`, `Chunk`, `ReadonlyArray`                                                  |
| event callback             | `Queue`, `PubSub`, `Deferred`, `Stream`                                                         |
| cleanup                    | `Scope`, acquire/use/release                                                                    |
| `console`                  | structured Effect logging                                                                       |
| test sleep / network       | `TestClock`, deterministic test Layer                                                           |

### 3. Model boundaries first

Create or update, in order:

1. `schemas.ts` for external and domain codecs, brands, and redaction policy.
2. `errors.ts` for the closed expected error vocabulary.
3. `service.ts` for named semantic operations.
4. `live.layer.ts` for SDK, transport, storage, and configuration wiring.
5. `memory.layer.ts` or a domain-specific test Layer with the identical contract.
6. operation modules only when they own substantial reusable policy.
7. an application runtime at the host root.

Do not create ceremonial files. A small service may colocate a coherent contract; split when ownership is stable. Read [file and package conventions](references/architecture/files-and-packages.md).

### 4. Make public operations closed

Declare owned Layers as static values. Their Requirements type channel names
the dependencies that callers must supply. Use native `Layer.succeed` at
composition sites and `Layer.mock` or replacement Layers in tests. Keep native
composition callbacks, but do not wrap a Layer in an owned factory function.
Enable the portable `strict-effect/static-layers` rule with the other Effect
checks; it has no factory exceptions or automatic fix.

A public service operation should normally have:

```ts
Effect.Effect<Success, DomainError, never>;
```

Build dependencies into the service Layer. Do not make each caller provide transport, configuration, clock, SDK, or persistence requirements unless the dependency is intentionally part of the public composition contract.

For fixed host settings, yield checked Config in the owning Layer; Config is
already yieldable. Use `Layer.unwrap` to configure existing Layers and
`Layer.effect` to construct a real service. Follow the
[configuration decision procedure](references/services/config-and-secrets.md)
before adding a Context service or options wrapper for a setting.

Expose named operations such as `createRedirectUri`, `queryDataset`, or `loadAccount`. Do not expose raw clients, arbitrary request methods, or generic callbacks.

Read [services and Layers](references/services/services-and-layers.md) and [provider adapters](references/services/provider-adapters.md).

### 5. Decode at ingress and encode at egress

- Decode environment, HTTP, queue, database, filesystem, provider, and state payloads immediately.
- Brand identifiers and constrained strings.
- Use exact object schemas where unknown keys would hide drift.
- Redact secrets at acquisition and in error/log encoders.
- Encode owned outbound payloads and durable receipts.
- Never cast a provider response into the domain type.
- Infer domain, service and wire data types from one owning Schema. Reuse its fields, brands and whole-record checks in transport and persistence codecs. Spreading fields does not copy a record-level check.
- Keep already decoded values typed through internal calls. Construct new constrained values with the owning fallible constructor and map its validation issue to a named error. Construct unchanged records directly from checked fields.
- Convert optional/null source fields into Option. When historical bytes distinguish missing keys from null, preserve that distinction in the codec and prove the original encoding and hashes.
- Use readonly structured cache keys with the installed equality/hash contract. Do not encode and decode internal keys as JSON.

Read [schemas and brands](references/modeling/schemas-and-brands.md), [errors and Causes](references/modeling/errors-and-causes.md), and [Config and secrets](references/services/config-and-secrets.md).

For Alchemy saved props and attributes, read
[checked stored values](references/modeling/alchemy-stored-values.md). Keep
optional fields encoded at their owner, preserve protected keys separately and
test historical readers against the actual selected state store and diff code.

### 6. Preserve structured effects

Keep Effect programs flat and sequential. Extract a helper only when it is independently reusable, represents stable policy, owns I/O, or owns resource lifetime.

Use structured concurrency. Every child fibre must be joined, scoped, supervised, or deliberately daemonised at an application boundary with an explicit lifecycle. Encode backpressure. Make interruption and finalisation part of the design.

Read [fibres, queues, and streams](references/concurrency/fibres-queues-and-streams.md) and [scope, time, retry, and interruption](references/concurrency/scope-time-retry-and-interruption.md).

### 7. Instrument semantic work

- Public service methods use named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`.
- Short private pipelines stay plain functions. Dependent private generators
  use `Effect.fnUntraced` when they do not own a separate span. A private external
  operation may still deserve named `Effect.fn`. Do not add a generator only to
  wrap a direct pipeline.
- Log structured, bounded, secret-negative fields.
- Create spans around semantic operations and external calls, not Layer construction.
- Classify expected failure without dumping arbitrary Causes.
- Use low-cardinality metric labels.
- Add application/resource identity: service, version/revision, environment, stage, repository, and branch/ref where useful.
- Keep application telemetry separate from platform telemetry.
- Treat exporter success as transport evidence only; query the backend for ingestion proof.

Read [logging, tracing, and metrics](references/observability/logging-tracing-and-metrics.md).

### 8. Test the contract and its real boundary

Test:

- Schema boundary success and failure;
- each tagged error branch;
- Layer construction;
- live adapter translation using controlled transport or SDK fixtures;
- the same service contract through a memory/test Layer;
- timeout, retry, interruption, and cleanup using deterministic time;
- concurrency ordering and backpressure;
- observability field safety;
- serialisation round-trips.

Never make ordinary unit tests depend on the live network or wall-clock sleeps. Read [deterministic testing](references/testing/deterministic-testing.md).

### 9. Enforce the policy

Run narrow searches for forbidden constructs on changed owned TypeScript. Classify each match as:

- host-required adapter;
- generated/vendor code;
- measured encapsulated exception;
- violation.

Use lint restrictions, architecture tests, package exports, and code review to stop recurrence. Read [lint, review, and migration](references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md).

## Final review

Do not call the change strict Effect code unless all relevant statements are true:

- External data is decoded and outbound data is encoded.
- Expected failures are a closed tagged error union.
- Services expose named domain operations.
- Live dependencies are private to Layers.
- Public operations have no accidental requirements.
- Runtime execution occurs only at an application boundary.
- Time, randomness, retry, concurrency, state, and cleanup are Effect-managed.
- Nullable values do not leak past ingress.
- No raw client, generic callback, assertion, or Promise escape hatch was added.
- Logs, spans, metrics, and receipts are secret-negative and low-cardinality.
- Tests use deterministic Layers and prove failure/interruption paths.
- Pure work uses immutable Effect collection operations; changing shared state uses an owned Ref or transactional primitive with pure updates.
- Domain alternatives use exhaustive Match; Option and Result use their own matching APIs.
- Schemas and brands have one owner, typed internal calls do not decode again, and cache keys do not use JSON.
- Historical source formats, missing/null distinctions and byte hashes have explicit compatibility tests when changed.
- Any exception is narrow, documented, and enforced against expansion.

Use Common Practice's application structure and ordinary development workflow.
Prioritise the Cloudflare Website and API, remove every Alchemy patch, and remove
TaxKit's separate receipt and approval machinery. Keep Bun as a supported,
secondary host over the same calculation packages.

```text
Website server/browser -> checked RPC operations -> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Machine HTTP/RPC/MCP -----------------------------> API -> calculations -> rules/core
Local SDK ----------------------------------------------> calculations -> rules/core

Native API declaration -> Website declaration
                    API address + private binding -> Website
Reverse Website address dependency: decision still open below
Git commit/PR -> ordinary checks -> native Alchemy -> deployed Website/API
                               Doppler supplies stage-specific secrets
```

10 October 2026. This document and its [plan](../exec-plans/active/common-practice-foundation-review.md)
replace the large, uncommitted audit packet created during this review.

Use one unchanged copy of the current portable asset under
`tools/oxlint/vendor/strict-effect`, with a short source/version note. Keep only
useful TaxKit extensions and adapt Common Practice's ownership checks to actual
TaxKit paths. Do not edit installed plugin caches or add a digest/receipt system.
TaxKit's newer Oxlint 1.86.0, Ultracite 7.12.2 and Effect tooling 0.48.0 do not

| Check | Adoption and limit |

No exemption for every Layer file or test. Extend raw-fetch restrictions across owned source. |

Native Alchemy `Output.map` and `Namespace.push` already have targeted handling; no broad exception is needed. |

The scaffold's one-level package scan would merge `packages/api/http` and `packages/api/rpc` incorrectly. Preserve source/types/default export conditions and SDK packed-consumer checks. |

# Documentation Maintainer

Keep documentation aligned with repository behavior by updating the earliest
durable semantic owner and only the pointers that must lead to it.

## Establish the local contract

1. Read applicable `AGENTS.md`, inspect the worktree, and identify the exact
   change, repository, environment, and write authority. Do not infer authority
   to mutate providers, publish, release, or push from permission to edit docs.
2. Read the repository-local `docs-maintainer` profile completely when one is
   present at `references/repository-profile.md`. It owns repository paths,
   commands, generated-document boundaries, mirrors, exceptions, and archive
   policy. The global skill supplies method, never local truth.
3. If no local profile exists, derive a temporary impact map from the root
   `README*`, `docs/README*`, applicable package/app READMEs, active SPEC/tasks,
   configuration, and changed implementation. Record missing ownership as a
   gap; do not invent canonical paths or command names.
4. Select an execution mode:
   - **attached change:** when the user authorized implementation and repository
     edits, edit affected documentation and task artifacts in the same slice;
   - **audit or curator:** for scheduled/background freshness work, or when
     mutation authority is absent, produce an isolated report-only candidate
     with provenance and a proposed patch. Publication requires a separately
     named responsible owner and publisher identity.

Never let a curator publish its own uncorroborated findings or treat its prior
output as independent feedback. Pin any published context projection to an
immutable repository revision; refresh it only at a recorded phase boundary.

Keep these truth layers distinct and apply the strongest applicable precedence:
external system for current external state; shared store for shared source
material; immutable context projection for a recorded phase; repository code,
config, and Schemas for desired state; durable docs for explanation and routing;
dated evidence for observations; active SPEC/tasks for current intent and
execution. Link across layers instead of copying claims between them.

For a repository-wide documentation audit, substantial PRD, or cross-cutting
harness change, read
[repository-harness-contract.md](references/repository-harness-contract.md).
It routes to the complete local method and requires no external source lookup.
Load the applicable structured modules directly:

- [contract map](references/harness/contract-map.md) for mode and lifecycle;
- [invariant register](references/harness/invariant-register.md) for stable IDs;
- [context and ownership](references/harness/context-and-ownership.md) for truth
  layers, phased retrieval, and publication boundaries;
- [proof and evaluation](references/harness/proof-and-evaluation.md) for
  journeys, delivery, receipts, terminal states, and proportional evaluation;
- [operations and authority](references/harness/operations-and-authority.md)
  when runbooks, providers, controls, releases, or automation are in scope; and
- [repository variation](references/harness/repository-variation.md) when
  creating or changing the local profile.

Use the Schemas and templates under `assets/harness/` for repository profiles,
critical journeys, bounded receipts, authority envelopes, and feedback or
automation controls. Do not replace those fixed field contracts with free-form
prose.
For an ordinary localized documentation change, do not load that broader
contract unless an ownership, delivery, dependency, or proof question requires
it. This skill owns the documentation track; use the sibling `repo-structure`
skill for a complete repository audit.

## Load context in phases

Use just enough context to decide and then prove the change:

1. **Ground:** read the change, directly affected docs/READMEs, the docs router,
   the owning architecture or standard, and active task context.
2. **Investigate:** inspect code, config, generated owners, history, provider
   readback, or upstream material only to resolve an identified question.
3. **Land:** inventory all affected docs, READMEs, skills, runbooks, references,
   generated artifacts, indexes, and active/archive pointers. Reconcile every
   contradiction on an affected route before closeout.

Do not preload the whole repository for an ordinary localized change. A
repository-wide documentation audit or PRD review may require a full
`docs/**` and `README*` accounting under its owning skill.

For a repository-wide audit, return documentation findings in the stable
finding format owned by the repository-audit procedure: consequence,
evidence, semantic owner, root correction, duplicated guidance to retire,
affected surfaces, proof, authority, limitations, and non-claims. Separate
important corrections from optional improvements.

## Build the impact ledger

Read [document-classes.md](references/document-classes.md) to select semantic
owners and [change-impact.md](references/change-impact.md) for the trigger
matrix. For each surface, record `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A`, with:

- changed behavior or claim;
- semantic owner and required pointers;
- exact affected path or narrowly bounded path set;
- lifecycle transition, if any;
- generated source and regeneration command, if applicable;
- verification and observable postcondition;
- proof location and explicit non-claims.

Cover docs, root/package/app READMEs, architecture/ADRs, standards, API and
generated references, runbooks, critical journeys, proof/evidence, skills and
agent instructions, lint/config/CI docs, migration/release notes, and active
SPEC/tasks. Never accept a generic “update docs” item.

## Edit the correct owner

- Put durable design, invariants, and boundaries in architecture or standards.
- Put exact repeatable operations in target-owned runbooks, including
  preconditions, authority, sequential steps, receipts, rollback, and
  escalation. Skills teach selection and judgment; they must route to rather
  than copy runbooks.
- Treat a procedure found in architecture or a README as an ownership defect,
  not precedent to extend. Propose or create the target-owned runbook and leave
  only durable rationale plus a pointer at the old location.
- Put public setup and entry-point navigation in READMEs. Keep them short and
  link to deeper owners.
- Keep root `AGENTS.md` as a terse map of repository purpose/compatibility,
  common operating loop, a small set of task classes or golden paths, and links
  to their context, commands, and proof. Do not append completed-feature
  histories or per-change atlas entries.
- Put mutable external state and one-run observations in dated, addressable
  evidence. Never present a provider response, deployment ID, secret age, or
  current revision as durable repository truth.
- Edit the source of generated documentation, run its real generator, and do
  not hand-edit output unless repository policy explicitly says it is owned.
- Update active SPEC/tasks and their evidence when implementation changes a
  requirement, decision, dependency, or acceptance claim.
- Use successor/tombstone links for replaced current docs. Preserve failed and
  historical evidence with provenance outside default navigation.
- Retire weaker duplicated reminders after promoting a repeated finding to its
  earliest enforceable owner: schema, type, lint rule, test, generator,
  runbook, or canonical document.
- In curator mode, record source, provenance, freshness, classification,
  audience, attached evidence, proposed semantic owner, target revision, and
  unresolved contradictions. Keep candidate material outside the worker's
  retrieval path until a responsible reviewer accepts it and a separately
  identified publisher performs an atomic publication with readback.

A curator result is incomplete unless it returns an explicit `candidate` block
with every field above plus responsible reviewer, publisher identity,

# TaxKit documentation profile

Read this profile after `AGENTS.md` and `docs/README.md`. Paths and commands
below are repository-local; resolve the checkout with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.

## Owner map

| Change class                                        | Earliest owner and required pointers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Maintainer lifecycle, truth layers, archive routing | `docs/README.md`; architecture, standards, audit and active intent only when affected                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Calculator rules, facts and schemas                 | owning `packages/calculators` or `packages/rules/**` source/README; relevant `docs/architecture/**`, SDK/API/public docs only when consumers change                                                                                                                                                                             |
| SDK exports and examples                            | `packages/sdk/typescript` source/export map and README; packed-consumer/downstream proof; `docs/architecture/api-and-sdk.md`                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| HTTP/OpenAPI                                        | `packages/api/http/src/**` schemas and `src/openapi.ts`; generated snapshot `packages/api/http/__snapshots__/openapi.json` through `test:openapi`; `packages/api/http/README.md`, `apps/api/README.md`, and API/SDK architecture only when their contracts change                                                               |
| Public MDX/navigation/lifecycle                     | `packages/docs-content/content/**`, `packages/docs-content/navigation.json`, and `tools/documentation/owner-policy.json`; `published` requires one exact `public.statusDecision.acceptanceRecords` binding to a strict addressable record, with the durable lifecycle decision routed from `docs/documentation-audit/hgi-207/public-mdx-lifecycle.json` |
| Public docs runtime/generated Fumadocs              | `apps/web/README.md` and its accepted catalogue/private API presentation; `apps/docs/README.md` is a retirement tombstone routing verified original source and separately approved historical recovery; `packages/docs-content/source.config.ts`, `packages/docs-content/.source`, and `packages/docs-fumadocs`; regenerate/check through the owning commands and never hand-edit generated output                                                                                                               |

| Commands, CI, versioning and release readiness      | `package.json`, workflow/command owner, `docs/standards/versioning.md`, `docs/runbooks/README.md`, testing-quality architecture and proof owner                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Public `published` needs an exact accepted record and one-to-one binding in

record and binding.
Generated source is authoritative over checked output. Repository evidence is
not provider, registry, deployment, public-site or consumer proof.

## Commands and boundaries

- Baseline documentation/path/skill checks: `bun run
check:docs`, `bun run check:runbooks`, `bun run check:repository-paths`.
- Harness foundation checks: `bun run check:harness-governance:types`, `bun run

- Current accepted content/runtime: `bun run docs:catalogue`, `bun run

For each check, state its observable postcondition and what it does not prove.
Keep background freshness reports as candidates until an attached implementation

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain, RPC, and HTTP API packages, copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied

# React and TanStack

## Contents

- [Keep render pure](#keep-render-pure)
- [Server and client runtimes](#server-and-client-runtimes)
- [Loaders and actions](#loaders-and-actions)
- [TanStack Query](#tanstack-query)
- [TanStack Router Start](#tanstack-routerstart)
- [Initial JavaScript and fonts](#initial-javascript-and-fonts)
- [React lifecycle](#react-lifecycle)
- [State](#state)
- [Errors](#errors)
- [Tests](#tests)

## Keep render pure

React components should be total render functions over props, decoded loader/query state, and declared hooks. Do not:

- run Effect during render;
- construct live Layers during render;
- access server Config/secrets;
- call raw provider clients;
- mutate global state;
- create unmanaged Promise side effects.

JSX and pure view transformations may remain plain TypeScript.

## Server and client runtimes

Keep separate composition:

- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.

Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.

Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.

For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
Effect fibre without another runtime.

Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Loaders and actions

Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:

1. decode params/search/body/session;
2. call a named Effect service operation;
3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
4. encode hydration-safe data;
5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.

Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.

## TanStack Query

Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.

Define intentionally:

- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
- invalidation after mutation;
- server prefetch/hydration encoding.

Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.

## TanStack Router/Start

Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.

For serialisable loader data:

- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
- prove all error variants are handled.

Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
transport, including an error response status.

### Router preloading and freshness

Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
page can render immediately while a return starts another API RPC
request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.

For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.

Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
separate owners. An API reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.

Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.

## Initial JavaScript and fonts

Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.

Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.

For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.

Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.

## React lifecycle

For subscriptions/streams:

- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
- scope to mount/route lifetime;
- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
- encode backpressure/sampling;
- update view state through a controlled adapter.

Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.

When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
An optional registration/subscription pattern is
`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
not required for purely synchronous local UI state.

Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
state or cleanup has a real owner.

Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.

Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.

## State

Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.

Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.

## Errors

Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:

- not found;
- unauthorised;
- validation fields;
- unavailable/retry;
- conflict;
- unexpected defect boundary.

Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.

## Tests

Test:

- domain service independently;
- loader/action decoding and encoding;
- runtime bridge and cancellation;
- hydration round-trip;
- retry ownership;
- subscription cleanup;
- no server dependency in client bundle;
- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
  a stalled unrelated service;
- exhaustive UI error states.

## Direct RPC loaders for a separate Website and API

```text
first request -> Website server loader -> one server runner
              -> shared RPC client -> private BACKEND -> API RPC -> domain
later navigation/preload -> same loader's client branch
              -> one root Atom registry/runtime -> public API /rpc -> domain
local setup -> server cookie + checked bindings -> encoded root data
            -> retained browser config/appearance atoms (no settings RPC)
```

Use the same RPC declarations, domain Schemas and named failures in both
branches. `createIsomorphicFn().server(serverCallback).client(clientCallback)`
selects local code; it does not create an endpoint. Do not use `createServerFn`,
an alternate HTTP API data client, a Website RPC proxy, or `AtomRpc.Service`
when an existing Atom runtime owns browser work. Native `AtomRpc.Service`
constructs a runtime; its convenience does not justify a second one.

The router starts before React. Create one browser registry in the router's
client branch and pass that local registry through ordinary typed router
context. This is not an Effect Context and must never enter loader data.
React uses that exact registry through native `RegistryContext.Provider`.
SSR uses an isolated native RegistryProvider; there is no module-global mutable
registry. Close the browser registry at final root unmount. The starter uses
Atom React's cancellable scheduler so development mount/cleanup replay can
cancel pending disposal. Qualify replay, final unmount and outstanding requests.

Seed checked root setup once with `useAtomInitialValues`. Seeded configuration
atoms must be kept alive: otherwise Atom may remove an unread value before a
later loader starts and silently restore its empty default. Keep local
appearance/progress independent of remote-client acquisition. Browser root
reloads read live local appearance and stored checked configuration; do not
ask the API to read a Website cookie.

A scoped resource atom builds the static semantic RPC client Layer using
`Layer.build`, a checked stage address, native `RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp`
and the same serialisation as the API. A named request atom runs each loader
operation using those services. One named browser host bridge waits with
`AtomRegistry.getResult` and `Effect.runPromise(..., { signal })`; it starts
no ManagedRuntime. Cancellation removes that subscription and releases the
request atom. The server combines the incoming request and router signals
and uses its existing runner. Keep per-request atoms separate from the retained
shared client so cancellation does not close another caller's transport.

Await server page data before constructing headings, canonical metadata and
status. Encode complete success/error loader results with their owner Schema;
restore them on the browser side where types such as Option/errors differ.
Never stringify Cause or infer a selected response variant from the request.
Use the domain's checked format operation, including its default complete data.

Qualification must cover all declared error variants with their fields, exact
successful result types, actual native RPC round trips, malformed JSON/schema
replies versus unavailable transport, format mismatches, total-read deadlines,
cancellation and unrelated defects. In Effect 4.0.2, invalid native exit-schema
decoding may surface as a defect. Mark only that native reply-decoder failure
and translate that private marker; never catch every SchemaError defect as an
invalid reply. Keep native NDJSON and exit codecs, not handwritten RPC frames.

Use actual Oxlint fixtures for aliases and re-exports. Enable the portable
`website-rpc-boundary` on Website source and `module-ownership` for alternate
HTTP data clients and server implementations. It admits only `runtime` at the
exact server owner and `browserRuntime` at the exact client owner. TypeScript
prevents a second declaration of those names. It rejects server-function
imports/re-exports, RPC proxy routes, ad hoc generated clients and unguarded
runtime calls; it deliberately permits legitimate native HTTP work. Dynamic
module ownership and source-package bans remain separate checks. Neither lint
nor a local build proves hosted CORS, native binding startup, first HTML,
navigation/preload freshness, restoration or deployed stage pairing.

## Contents

- [Keep render pure](#keep-render-pure)
- [Server and client runtimes](#server-and-client-runtimes)

- [Errors](#errors)

## Keep render pure

React components should be total render functions over props, decoded loader/query state, and declared hooks. Do not:

- run Effect during render;
- construct live Layers during render;
- access server Config/secrets;
- call raw provider clients;
- mutate global state;
- create unmanaged Promise side effects.

JSX and pure view transformations may remain plain TypeScript.

## Server and client runtimes

Keep separate composition:

- server runtime: filesystem/database/provider/secrets;
- client runtime: browser transport, client cache, browser-safe telemetry.

Never serialise a service, Layer, Cause, Redacted value, or SDK object into hydration data.

Use TanStack's matching server/client environment functions for runtime imports
as well as the `*.server.ts` and `*.client.ts` filenames. Keep browser globals
out of module initialisation and inspect the built browser dependency graph.

For an Alchemy-hosted Website/API pair, keep TanStack as the frontend. All
Website server entry points use one runner whose Layers contain typed API
clients, not live backend implementations. A private Cloudflare service-binding
adapter supplies its same-stage API; browser clients use a checked public URL.
The native API owns HTTP/RPC/MCP handlers and executes them in its incoming
Effect fibre without another runtime.

Do not carry Effect Context through TanStack, merge event services into its
runtime, borrow tracer hooks or add a custom backend Worker around Start.
Preserve cancellation and body streams at the narrow host adapter. Native API
telemetry and any qualified frontend host-span adapter have separate owners;
see [hosted telemetry](../../../alchemy-iac/references/effect/hosted-web-telemetry.md).

## Loaders and actions

Framework loaders/actions are host adapters:

1. decode params/search/body/session;
2. call a named Effect service operation;
3. map tagged errors to redirect/not-found/protocol result;
4. encode hydration-safe data;
5. bridge to Promise only at the required callback.

Keep retries, provider calls, and business policy inside Effect services.

## TanStack Query

Wrap query/mutation functions through one runtime bridge. The query key must use stable encoded domain identity.

Define intentionally:

- which layer owns retry: Query or Effect Schedule, not both accidentally;
- cancellation: Query AbortSignal interrupts the Effect;
- error shape: encoded domain/protocol error, not Cause;
- cache staleness versus Effect Cache;
- invalidation after mutation;
- server prefetch/hydration encoding.

Avoid returning `Effect.runPromise(program)` ad hoc from every component.

## TanStack Router/Start

Keep route definitions declarative. Route loaders decode and bridge to the server/client runtime appropriate to the execution environment.

For serialisable loader data:

- Schema encode before crossing server/client;
- Schema decode on the receiving side if trust boundary requires;
- represent expected recoverable states explicitly;
- prove all error variants are handled.

Do not depend on class prototype identity after hydration. Return a
Schema-encoded success/error result for expected backend failures and decode it
on the receiving side. Prove tags and useful fields survive the actual TanStack
transport, including an error response status.

### Router preloading and freshness

Set link preloading and loader freshness in `createRouter`, not the Vite plugin.
Check the receiving installation's defaults: TanStack retains unused loader
data for five minutes by default, but ordinary `staleTime` is zero. A cached
page can render immediately while a return starts another API RPC
request. Retention does not promise a period without requests.

For public page data that can be reused briefly, the repository starter uses
`defaultPreload: "intent"`, `defaultStaleTime: 60_000` and
`defaultPreloadStaleTime: 60_000`. Intent preloads on link hover, focus or touch;
the one-minute freshness window applies to both loaded and preloaded data.
Choose route-specific freshness and invalidation for changing or personal data.
Encoded error envelopes are also loader data; account for their retry and
recovery behaviour rather than treating them as successful content.

Router memory, browser HTTP caching, Cloudflare caching and Effect Cache are
separate owners. An API reply marked `no-store` can still be held by
the router. A full reload starts a new router cache. Prefetching moves the first
request before the click; freshness controls repeat reads. Analytics requests
and a route's first JavaScript download are separate from page-data refreshes.

Prove the behaviour in a real browser: hover before opening a page, return to a
visited page within its freshness window, then return after expiry. Inspect the
page-data requests separately from assets and analytics. A build does not prove
these interactions. See TanStack's official [data loading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/data-loading)
and [preloading](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/preloading) guides;
reconcile their current descriptions with installed source and types.

## Initial JavaScript and fonts

Inspect the production build before changing how code loads. TanStack Start's
plugin already separates non-critical route components in the qualified
installation. Router-only applications need their matching bundler's automatic
splitting setting. Keep optional implementations out of the root route and
other modules imported by every page. A separate file or lazy service acquisition
does not remove a static import from the initial download. Use the framework's
normal splitting and keep necessary matching and loader code readily available.

Import important font assets through Vite's `?url` handling and declare ordinary
font preload links in the owning route's `head` result. Render `HeadContent` so
the browser sees those links in the initial HTML. For WOFF2 use `rel: "preload"`,
`as: "font"`, `type: "font/woff2"` and `crossOrigin: "anonymous"`. The preload and
stylesheet must resolve to the same asset. Preload only the styles and character
sets used by visible opening content; every extra preload competes with it.
Keep the chosen `font-display` policy explicit.

For owned conditional head data, prefer a checked Schema constructor with fixed
tags, `Option` and `Array.fromOption`, and immutable `Array` or `Struct` operations.
Do not spread a ternary array of repeated font objects into every route.
Trusted Vite asset URLs need no runtime environment reader or browser global.

Measure compressed transfer bytes separately from expanded JavaScript size,
fonts and styles. Record Lighthouse's network, CPU and cache settings, and retain
repeated results when scores vary. A smaller download alone does not prove that
visible content appears sooner. Prove the emitted HTML, browser font requests
and route navigation separately from local checks. See the official
[code splitting](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/code-splitting),
[head management](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/guide/document-head-management)
and [Vite asset](https://vite.dev/guide/assets) guides, then check installed behaviour.

## React lifecycle

For subscriptions/streams:

- acquire in an effect/hook adapter;
- scope to mount/route lifetime;
- interrupt on unmount/navigation;
- avoid duplicate subscriptions under development lifecycle;
- encode backpressure/sampling;
- update view state through a controlled adapter.

Do not launch a daemon fibre from a component without cleanup.

When Effect Atom already owns browser work, use its runtime and root registry.
An optional registration/subscription pattern is
`Atom.runtime(browserLayers).atom(scopedOperation)`, mounted with `useAtomMount`
under one `RegistryProvider`. Unmounting must release the operation's Scope and
interrupt outstanding work. A browser-only registration has an inert server
counterpart selected through TanStack's environment function. Do not create an
extra ManagedRuntime or an unmanaged Promise workflow in a component. Atom is
not required for purely synchronous local UI state.

Separate browser work when its dependencies or lifetime differ. Appearance,
local progress, analytics and browser-tool registration can share one runtime
and root registry while using independent resource or action Atoms. Mounting
tools must not acquire an unrelated analytics SDK; using analytics must not
register tools. Share checked root configuration through a data Atom rather
than making local features wait for remote service acquisition. A service does
not automatically need its own Atom: split where independent acquisition,
state or cleanup has a real owner.

Declare service Layers as static values and supply their checked requirements
at composition. In a resource Atom, native `Layer.build` can build the selected
Layer in the Atom's Scope. Pass its resulting Context only to dependent Effect
operations inside that runtime. An `Effect.provide(layer)` around a short
registration operation can release its private Layer scope as soon as that
operation returns; it does not by itself retain the registered service for the
mounted lifetime. Keep a shared resource Atom alive only when consumers need
one instance until the root registry closes. Registration usually belongs to
its mount, while a reused analytics client can belong to the root lifetime.
Check the receiving Effect Atom version's scope behaviour.

Independent acquisition does not imply delayed loading. An immediate page-view
action still requests analytics immediately. Any later startup policy must
name its trigger and event-loss trade-off, with Effect owning cancellation and
cleanup. Do not add arbitrary timers, detached imports or another runtime.

## State

Keep domain state in Effect services when it is shared, concurrent, or effectful. Keep local ephemeral UI state in React when it is truly view-local and synchronous.

Do not move every `useState` into Effect. Do move provider/cache/concurrent workflows out of component-local mutable logic.

## Errors

Translate domain errors to a closed UI state:

- not found;
- unauthorised;
- validation fields;
- unavailable/retry;
- conflict;
- unexpected defect boundary.

Never render raw provider messages, stack traces, or Causes.

## Tests

Test:

- domain service independently;
- loader/action decoding and encoding;
- runtime bridge and cancellation;
- hydration round-trip;
- retry ownership;
- subscription cleanup;
- no server dependency in client bundle;
- independent optional service acquisition and root/mount cleanup, including
  a stalled unrelated service;
- exhaustive UI error states.

## Direct RPC loaders for a separate Website and API

```text
first request -> Website server loader -> one server runner
              -> shared RPC client -> private BACKEND -> API RPC -> domain
later navigation/preload -> same loader's client branch
              -> one root Atom registry/runtime -> public API /rpc -> domain
local setup -> server cookie + checked bindings -> encoded root data
            -> retained browser config/appearance atoms (no settings RPC)
```

Use the same RPC declarations, domain Schemas and named failures in both
branches. `createIsomorphicFn().server(serverCallback).client(clientCallback)`
selects local code; it does not create an endpoint. Do not use `createServerFn`,
an alternate HTTP API data client, a Website RPC proxy, or `AtomRpc.Service`
when an existing Atom runtime owns browser work. Native `AtomRpc.Service`
constructs a runtime; its convenience does not justify a second one.

The router starts before React. Create one browser registry in the router's
client branch and pass that local registry through ordinary typed router
context. This is not an Effect Context and must never enter loader data.
React uses that exact registry through native `RegistryContext.Provider`.
SSR uses an isolated native RegistryProvider; there is no module-global mutable
registry. Close the browser registry at final root unmount. The starter uses
Atom React's cancellable scheduler so development mount/cleanup replay can
cancel pending disposal. Qualify replay, final unmount and outstanding requests.

Seed checked root setup once with `useAtomInitialValues`. Seeded configuration
atoms must be kept alive: otherwise Atom may remove an unread value before a
later loader starts and silently restore its empty default. Keep local
appearance/progress independent of remote-client acquisition. Browser root
reloads read live local appearance and stored checked configuration; do not
ask the API to read a Website cookie.

A scoped resource atom builds the static semantic RPC client Layer using
`Layer.build`, a checked stage address, native `RpcClient.layerProtocolHttp`
and the same serialisation as the API. A named request atom runs each loader
operation using those services. One named browser host bridge waits with
`AtomRegistry.getResult` and `Effect.runPromise(..., { signal })`; it starts
no ManagedRuntime. Cancellation removes that subscription and releases the
request atom. The server combines the incoming request and router signals
and uses its existing runner. Keep per-request atoms separate from the retained
shared client so cancellation does not close another caller's transport.

Await server page data before constructing headings, canonical metadata and
status. Encode complete success/error loader results with their owner Schema;
restore them on the browser side where types such as Option/errors differ.
Never stringify Cause or infer a selected response variant from the request.
Use the domain's checked format operation, including its default complete data.

Qualification must cover all declared error variants with their fields, exact
successful result types, actual native RPC round trips, malformed JSON/schema
replies versus unavailable transport, format mismatches, total-read deadlines,
cancellation and unrelated defects. In Effect 4.0.2, invalid native exit-schema
decoding may surface as a defect. Mark only that native reply-decoder failure
and translate that private marker; never catch every SchemaError defect as an
invalid reply. Keep native NDJSON and exit codecs, not handwritten RPC frames.

Use actual Oxlint fixtures for aliases and re-exports. Enable the portable
`website-rpc-boundary` on Website source and `module-ownership` for alternate
HTTP data clients and server implementations. It admits only `runtime` at the
exact server owner and `browserRuntime` at the exact client owner. TypeScript
prevents a second declaration of those names. It rejects server-function
imports/re-exports, RPC proxy routes, ad hoc generated clients and unguarded
runtime calls; it deliberately permits legitimate native HTTP work. Dynamic
module ownership and source-package bans remain separate checks. Neither lint
nor a local build proves hosted CORS, native binding startup, first HTML,
navigation/preload freshness, restoration or deployed stage pairing.

Q6 — Should TaxKit copy Common Practice’s API access and page-link policy? Common Practice lets browsers call its public API without cookies, and uses fixed Production addresses for canonical links, sitemap and other discovery documents—even in Preview. TaxKit currently restricts browser access to its Website and uses each stage’s Website address in those links. I recommend the Common Practice approach to simplify the patch-free Alchemy setup; this would change those two behaviours.

The proposed [Common Practice foundation review](./common-practice-foundation-review.md)
owns the 10 October source comparison and proposed migration to Common
Practice's ordinary workflow: Cloudflare first, patch-free Alchemy and retirement
of extra receipt tooling. It remains design work; implementation must update
the older clean-slate plan rather than preserve its retired ceremony.

The [Clean slate foundation](./clean-slate-foundation.md) implements the accepted
website/API rebuild in dependency order; provider apply remains separately gated.

The wider clean-slate plan remains active; adad consumer qualification and enablement are separate work.

The completed [Entire session history setup](../completed/entire-session-history.md)
retains recording, import and hosted publication proof.

Live implementation plans belong here while work is in progress. Maintainer
lifecycle is owned by [`../../README.md`](../../README.md).

and its [completed plan](../completed/alchemy-doppler-modernisation.md)
retain the one-resource owner, Alchemy/Effect upgrade, Doppler contract,
Production update and separate hosted proof. The original failed deploy run,
untested rollback and other proof limits remain dated history.

current generic and Effect anti-slop policy, structural finding fixes, local
verification, hosted Quality and merged-main proof. Package publication and
deployment remain explicit non-claims.

The implemented
[Doppler configuration governance](../../product-specs/doppler-configuration-governance.md)

non-claims rather than active repository work.
