repository-wide documentation audit or PRD review may require a full
`docs/**` and `README*` accounting under its owning skill.

For a repository-wide audit, return documentation findings in the stable
finding format owned by the repository-audit procedure: consequence,
evidence, semantic owner, root correction, duplicated guidance to retire,
affected surfaces, proof, authority, limitations, and non-claims. Separate
important corrections from optional improvements.

## Build the impact ledger

Read [document-classes.md](references/document-classes.md) to select semantic
owners and [change-impact.md](references/change-impact.md) for the trigger
matrix. For each surface, record `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A`, with:

- changed behavior or claim;
- semantic owner and required pointers;
- exact affected path or narrowly bounded path set;
- lifecycle transition, if any;
- generated source and regeneration command, if applicable;
- verification and observable postcondition;
- proof location and explicit non-claims.

Cover docs, root/package/app READMEs, architecture/ADRs, standards, API and
generated references, runbooks, critical journeys, proof/evidence, skills and
agent instructions, lint/config/CI docs, migration/release notes, and active
SPEC/tasks. Never accept a generic “update docs” item.

## Edit the correct owner

- Put durable design, invariants, and boundaries in architecture or standards.
- Put exact repeatable operations in target-owned runbooks, including
  preconditions, authority, sequential steps, receipts, rollback, and
  escalation. Skills teach selection and judgment; they must route to rather
  than copy runbooks.
- Treat a procedure found in architecture or a README as an ownership defect,
  not precedent to extend. Propose or create the target-owned runbook and leave
  only durable rationale plus a pointer at the old location.
- Put public setup and entry-point navigation in READMEs. Keep them short and
  link to deeper owners.
- Keep root `AGENTS.md` as a terse map of repository purpose/compatibility,
  common operating loop, a small set of task classes or golden paths, and links
  to their context, commands, and proof. Do not append completed-feature
  histories or per-change atlas entries.
- Put mutable external state and one-run observations in dated, addressable
  evidence. Never present a provider response, deployment ID, secret age, or
  current revision as durable repository truth.
- Edit the source of generated documentation, run its real generator, and do
  not hand-edit output unless repository policy explicitly says it is owned.
- Update active SPEC/tasks and their evidence when implementation changes a
  requirement, decision, dependency, or acceptance claim.
- Use successor/tombstone links for replaced current docs. Preserve failed and
  historical evidence with provenance outside default navigation.
- Retire weaker duplicated reminders after promoting a repeated finding to its
  earliest enforceable owner: schema, type, lint rule, test, generator,
  runbook, or canonical document.
- In curator mode, record source, provenance, freshness, classification,
  audience, attached evidence, proposed semantic owner, target revision, and
  unresolved contradictions. Keep candidate material outside the worker's
  retrieval path until a responsible reviewer accepts it and a separately
  identified publisher performs an atomic publication with readback.

A curator result is incomplete unless it returns an explicit `candidate` block
with every field above plus responsible reviewer, publisher identity,
publication status, revocation/quarantine, last-known-good recovery, and
post-publication readback. Use `unknown` with a named owner/resume trigger when
evidence cannot supply a field; never silently omit it.

## Keep implementation and documentation honest

- Confirm claims against current code, config, and runtime evidence at the
  boundary they describe. Treat tool output as observed data, not policy or
  authority.
- Keep boundary encoding/decoding, Effect service ownership, error contracts,
  client wrappers, React composition, commands, and public API examples aligned
  with the repository's installed versions and enforced patterns.
- When an example changes, update its canonical template too. Check generated
  code against the selected dependency snapshot, including renamed Schema APIs,
  named public operations, private untraced helpers and Layer construction.
  Extend existing qualification checks; do not create parallel suites for the
  same claim. A cached result must include every changed file the check reads.
- Update owning docs during each implementation slice, before the slice can be
  accepted. Do not defer accumulated documentation work to a final sweep.
- Record unresolved product or authority decisions as blockers in active task
  context instead of silently choosing them.
- When a change adds or revises a critical journey, retain a stable journey ID,
  procedure owner, observable oracle against plausible imitation, environment,
  and receipt route rather than expanding the inventory into every test.
- When review or a terminal audit finds an issue, record why the prior SPEC,
  task, implementation check, or receipt allowed the false green. Promote the
  prevention to the earliest durable owner: domain contract, direct test
  oracle, task verification, lint/tooling control, or lifecycle rule. Retain
  the dated finding as evidence rather than adding another audit reminder.
- Any correction after task acceptance reopens the owning task and refreshes
  affected proof, candidate identity, rollback identity, and lifecycle
  receipts. A terminal audit runs only after the complete SPEC is terminal;
  later implementation invalidates its terminal status.

## Verify the claim

Read [proof-authority-and-lifecycle.md](references/proof-authority-and-lifecycle.md).
Run the exact local documentation, link, generated-artifact, lint, typecheck,
test, build, journey, skill, and mirror checks required by the impact ledger.
Do not invent commands. Distinguish pre-existing failures from regressions.
Never fabricate an artifact identity, path, edit, command, exit status, or
executed check. When no checkout or repository-local owner map is available,
return only class-level proposed owners with status `unverified`; do not report
an attached edit or accepted outcome.

Return a bounded receipt containing:

1. outcome and changed semantic owners;
2. impact-ledger rows, including explicit `N/A` decisions;
3. exact checks and postconditions;
4. artifact, environment, actor/authority, and critical journeys where relevant;
5. limitations and claims not established;
6. failed, no-op, or inconclusive evidence path, last successful step, observed
   state, escalation, resume trigger, smallest unresolved choice, rollback, and
   next owner when not accepted.

Keep full logs in an addressable artifact and show only the violated invariant,
exact target, recovery hint, omitted-detail path, and postcondition in the
default context.

## Stop conditions

Stop and surface the gap when:

- no current semantic owner can be identified;
- current docs conflict and evidence cannot resolve which one owns the claim;
- a generated owner or real verification command is unknown;
- the requested claim requires provider, release, publication, or mutation
  authority that has not been granted;
- required proof would cross an unapproved environment or reveal secrets;
- a runbook lacks rollback or escalation for a consequential operation.

# Repository Structure

Create a small repository whose boundaries are executable, documented, and
updateable. Resolve current versions first; render only from a recorded snapshot.

## Audit before scaffolding

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, all repository-owned readable `docs/**` and `README*`,
   manifests, workspace/lock/runtime config, lint/format/test/CI config, skills,
   and representative apps/packages. Exclude generated, dependency, build, and
   vendored trees explicitly.
2. Inspect worktree state. For an existing repository, patch only authorized
   paths and preserve unrelated work.
3. For an existing-repository audit, read the
   [repository audit router](references/repository-audit.md), then load its
   [workflow](references/audit/workflow.md),
   [corpus and journeys](references/audit/corpus-and-journeys.md),
   [lenses](references/audit/lenses.md),
   [findings and acceptance](references/audit/findings-and-acceptance.md), and
   [variation and stopping](references/audit/variation-and-stopping.md).
   Then read the
   [repository contract](references/repository-contract.md),
   [TanStack and Effect architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md), and
   [tooling and docs](references/tooling-and-docs.md).
4. Load the canonical sibling
   [`package-structure`](../package-structure/SKILL.md) and
   [`docs-maintainer`](../docs-maintainer/SKILL.md) skills. Resolve them
   relative to this installed skill collection, or pass the skill collection
   explicitly to the renderer. Stop before rendering if either is unavailable;
   do not invent package/document contracts or assume a user's home directory.

## Audit an existing repository

Default to report-first. Define the target revision, claimed jobs, accepted
outcomes, proof boundaries, authority, exclusions, and stop conditions. Account
for the repository corpus, then follow a small set of representative jobs from
request through ownership, implementation, proof, delivery, and acceptance.
Use prior collaboration evidence when available and authorized; treat it as
trajectory evidence rather than repository policy.

For a whole-repository audit, create the structured scope and finding artifacts
from `assets/audit/`; do not use free-form prose as the sole audit record.
Validate them with `scripts/validate_audit_artifacts.py`. Return a
consequence-ordered Markdown view with stable IDs, separate important
corrections from optional improvements, identify the earliest owning
correction, and name duplicated machinery to retire. Stop for acceptance before
implementation unless the original request authorizes both. Record accepted
finding IDs in the crosswalk, hand them to `prd-writer`, then use `prd-review`
and `prd-implementer`.

For most repositories, stop after the structural and trajectory audit,
accepted important corrections, normal repository checks, and one fresh
independent review. Do not create a comparative harness evaluation unless the
claim is that a particular intervention changes future worker behavior.

## Resolve or select versions

Rendering is offline and deterministic. The checked-in snapshot is a known-good
fallback, not permission to call it current. To research a refresh, use primary
registries/official sources and DeepWiki only for upstream packages—not the
local codebase:

```bash
python3 scripts/resolve_versions.py --output /tmp/provisional-versions.json
```

Effect ecosystem packages share the qualified exact stable v4 version, currently
`4.0.2`. Resolve that exact version; registry `latest`/`beta` tags do not
select the qualified native Alchemy combination. TanStack Start and Router
resolve independently. Never emit `latest`.
Alchemy beta and the preview-only Cloudflare scaffold require an explicit
qualified/rejected decision; never infer compatibility from a registry tag.
Read [version policy](references/version-policy.md); a snapshot is adopted only
after full compatibility rendering and verification.

## Render safely

The target must be an absolute, new path. There is no overwrite mode:

```bash
python3 scripts/render_repository.py \
  --target /absolute/new/repository \
  --name example \
  --scope @example \
  --source-condition @example/source \
  --versions assets/version-snapshot.json
```

The renderer stages root/app/docs/tooling assets, invokes the canonical package
renderer for domain and HTTP API packages (RPC is an optional package variant), copies every complete current
repository-skill folder, adds only the declared repository-local profiles,
creates `.claude/skills/**` links to `.agents/skills/**`, validates the copied
trees against their canonical sources, then atomically renames. It never
templates lockfiles, generated route trees, output, caches, or dependency trees.

Every scaffold includes the minimum repository-owned harness:

- fixed invariant and audit guidance inside the copied local skills;
- a repository harness profile as the sole local variation surface;
- one docs router and documentation owner map;
- structured audit scope, finding, and accepted-finding templates plus schemas;
- critical journeys, proof and bounded-receipt contracts;
- authority, feedback/control, automation, epoch, effectiveness, evidence, and
  runbook owners;
- deterministic governance and audit validation; and
- an active bootstrap-harness task that qualifies the rendered defaults before
  they become current repository truth.

The render receipt records official sources, selected versions, compatibility
decisions, config digests, limitations, and an explicitly absent lockfile. After
the first `bun install`, run `scripts/finalize_repository_receipt.py` to bind the
receipt to `bun.lock`; do not claim a bootstrapped fixture before that phase.

Use `--skills-root /absolute/skill-collection` only when the sibling skills are
installed outside the default collection. Generated repository-local skills
must remain useful without that global collection after rendering. Each copied
skill is the complete canonical folder. The docs-maintainer and
package-structure skills receive explicit generated repository profiles; those
profiles are the only permitted tree differences. Claude compatibility
surfaces are links, never independently maintained copies.

Include the complete `linear` skill because PRD Implementer loads it for
projects with Linear tracking. The generated receipt and local validator must
cover that folder and its Claude link too; a global installed copy does not
satisfy the generated repository's local references.

## Split folders and files by durable ownership

Choose paths from the call graph and semantic owner. A repository/package
boundary is justified by an independent contract; an app-internal subfolder is
justified by a durable capability, domain, adapter, authority, runtime, or
independently tested policy. File count alone is not a boundary, and a one-file
capability should stay a file when a folder would add no meaning.

- Start with actual callers, exports, tests, untrusted ingress, runtime
  composition, and provider/authority edges before moving a file.
- Name folders after capabilities/domains (`observability`, `cloudflare`, or
  `metrics-token-qualification`) and files after owned roles (`schemas.ts`,
  `errors.ts`, `service.ts`, `plan.ts`, `authority.ts`, `website.ts`, or
  `manifest.main.ts`).
- Do not scaffold every conventional file. Add `service.ts`, `live.layer.ts`,
  `test.layer.ts`, or `config.ts` only when a real service, resource Layer,
  deterministic test Layer, or durable configuration boundary exists.
- Keep tests beside app-internal owners or in the package's contract/test
  location; keep reusable fixtures in the package-approved testing owner.
  Reject `common/`, `shared/`, `helpers/`, and `utils/` dumping grounds.
- After a split, update imports, tests, architecture/README pointers, exports,
  and lifecycle/proof owners in the same slice. Preserve one canonical Schema,
  error, service, plan, and configuration owner.

## Enforce the separate Website/API architecture

Read the [TanStack, Effect and Alchemy architecture](references/tanstack-effect.md)
before composing apps. The scaffold uses the separate frontend/backend design:

- The domain package owns Schemas, failures, operations, source validation and
  live/test Layers. HTTP, RPC and optional MCP reuse that owner.
- apps/api composes the live domain and native handler Layers in Alchemy's
  instance Scope. Incoming work keeps the native request fibre and cleanup.
  It has no ManagedRuntime or extra Promise runner.
- apps/web remains a standard TanStack Website. Native HttpApiClient reads use
  the private same-stage binding for SSR; native AtomHttpApi.Service calls the
  checked public API directly in the browser. Share one runtime factory and
  router/React registry. TanStack owns loader data/freshness, so no pageLoaderAtom,
  copied client service, success/error envelope or Website server-function proxy.
  Component-owned reactive reads use native query atoms. Optional RPC is a
  deliberate transport choice, not the root scaffold's public-read default.

- Keep one frontend server runner and one React-mounted browser Atom graph.
  No Effect Context, request-service merge or tracer-hook workaround goes
  through TanStack. Use matching server/client environment functions for imports.
- Native generated clients own encoding/decoding. Add adapters only for real
  feature policy or host conversion, not replica domain service contracts.
  Bound the complete native read with Effect.timeout where a feature needs a
  deadline; preserve cancellation, native errors and response cleanup.

- One native Alchemy stack deploys both apps with a matching API per stage.
  Preview never connects to Production. Bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` for each
  host's own origin; use native resource Outputs for another host's address.
  Never hard-code or construct a deployed website address. Keep Schema checks
  where resolved bindings enter application code. A chosen custom domain is
  valid infrastructure input, not a second application origin setting. Follow
  the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md).
- Every cross-workspace import uses explicit exports, including infrastructure.
- Routes and feature owners load data and choose error/workflow behaviour.
  Presentation components receive readonly values and action callbacks.
- Decode external input and encode outward values with their owning Schemas.
  Extract only demonstrated reuse, substantial work or a resource lifetime.

Check actual Worker startup after initialisation returns, response consumption
and cancellation, native-client errors and deadlines, real browser CORS and
bundle contents. Run negative Oxlint fixtures under the moved package paths;
a green typecheck or server call alone does not prove those connections.

## Add product analytics when required

For browser and backend PostHog analytics, read the
[application ownership and relay guide](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md). It
routes to the Alchemy lifecycle and Effect browser adapter owners. Keep analytics
optional: the base scaffold does not provision projects or start collection.

## Verify and maintain

Run in this order:

```bash
bun install
bun run format:check
bun run lint
bun run test:lint-rules
bun run check-types
bun run test
bun run build
python3 scripts/validate_repository.py /absolute/repository
```

Inspect export consumers and generated docs in addition to command status. Read
[maintenance](references/maintenance.md) before changing versions, assets,
profiles, rules, or skill baselines. Report exact commands, exit codes, and any
blocked upstream incompatibility; do not waive a failing compatibility fixture.
Use the generated docs-maintainer owner map and lifecycle/skill checks for
documentation impact, and retain a bounded impact receipt with explicit
non-claims.

## Immutable Effect and Schema ownership

Apply the canonical strict-effect-ts policy to all owned TypeScript, including
tests, tools, configuration and infrastructure. Use immutable Effect Array,
Record, HashMap and HashSet operations and exhaustive Match. For pure work use
folds/unfolds; for effectful work use a bounded sequential traversal or owned
Stream. Ref belongs to real changing state with a pure immutable update.

Every meaningful identifier/value and data record has one owning Schema with
inferred types. Reuse fields, brands and whole-record checks across codecs;
decode actual external input/replies once, construct new constrained values
with checked constructors and named errors, and trust typed internal contracts.
Domain absence is Option. Preserve historical source formats, missing/null
distinctions and hashes when changing a codec. Internal caches use full readonly
address records, tested with installed equality/hash and cancellation rules.

Enable the portable no-imperative-collections rule alongside the existing
rules; prove it through actual negative and valid Oxlint fixtures in app,
package, tests, tools and config paths. Document precise host operation/property
allowances, never a whole-file or wildcard mutation waiver. Keep the native API
request execution and cleanup and the one exact TanStack server runner. Templates
are examples qualified at their snapshot; research a v4 clone and reconcile with
installed source/types before applying them to another Effect version.

The generated Oxlint configuration enables native loader/client/cache ownership
and public API proxy checks. Its real-command fixtures prove forbidden wrappers
fail while native HTML loaders and Alchemy cache declarations pass. Configure a
checked-response rule only when the project has an actual format-checking helper;
the starter does not invent one. Follow the shared
[native request ownership policy](../strict-effect-ts/references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
when extending its API paths or loader owners.

  the private same-stage binding for SSR; native AtomHttpApi.Service calls the
  checked public API directly in the browser. Share one runtime factory and
  router/React registry. TanStack owns loader data/freshness, so no pageLoaderAtom,
  copied client service, success/error envelope or Website server-function proxy.
  Component-owned reactive reads use native query atoms. Optional RPC is a
  deliberate transport choice, not the root scaffold's public-read default.

- Keep one frontend server runner and one React-mounted browser Atom graph.
  No Effect Context, request-service merge or tracer-hook workaround goes
  through TanStack. Use matching server/client environment functions for imports.
- Native generated clients own encoding/decoding. Add adapters only for real
  feature policy or host conversion, not replica domain service contracts.
  Bound the complete native read with Effect.timeout where a feature needs a
  deadline; preserve cancellation, native errors and response cleanup.

- One native Alchemy stack deploys both apps with a matching API per stage.
  Preview never connects to Production. Bind `Cloudflare.Worker.URL` for each
  host's own origin; use native resource Outputs for another host's address.
  Never hard-code or construct a deployed website address. Keep Schema checks
  where resolved bindings enter application code. A chosen custom domain is
  valid infrastructure input, not a second application origin setting. Follow
  the website origin rules in [Cloudflare](../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md).
- Every cross-workspace import uses explicit exports, including infrastructure.
- Routes and feature owners load data and choose error/workflow behaviour.
  Presentation components receive readonly values and action callbacks.
- Decode external input and encode outward values with their owning Schemas.
  Extract only demonstrated reuse, substantial work or a resource lifetime.

Check actual Worker startup after initialisation returns, response consumption
and cancellation, native-client errors and deadlines, real browser CORS and
bundle contents. Run negative Oxlint fixtures under the moved package paths;
a green typecheck or server call alone does not prove those connections.

## Add product analytics when required

For browser and backend PostHog analytics, read the
[application ownership and relay guide](../alchemy-iac/references/effect/posthog-analytics.md). It
routes to the Alchemy lifecycle and Effect browser adapter owners. Keep analytics
optional: the base scaffold does not provision projects or start collection.

## Verify and maintain

Run in this order:

```bash
bun install
bun run format:check
bun run lint
bun run test:lint-rules
bun run check-types
bun run test
bun run build
python3 scripts/validate_repository.py /absolute/repository
```

Inspect export consumers and generated docs in addition to command status. Read
[maintenance](references/maintenance.md) before changing versions, assets,
profiles, rules, or skill baselines. Report exact commands, exit codes, and any
blocked upstream incompatibility; do not waive a failing compatibility fixture.
Use the generated docs-maintainer owner map and lifecycle/skill checks for
documentation impact, and retain a bounded impact receipt with explicit
non-claims.

## Immutable Effect and Schema ownership

Apply the canonical strict-effect-ts policy to all owned TypeScript, including
tests, tools, configuration and infrastructure. Use immutable Effect Array,
Record, HashMap and HashSet operations and exhaustive Match. For pure work use
folds/unfolds; for effectful work use a bounded sequential traversal or owned
Stream. Ref belongs to real changing state with a pure immutable update.

Every meaningful identifier/value and data record has one owning Schema with
inferred types. Reuse fields, brands and whole-record checks across codecs;
decode actual external input/replies once, construct new constrained values
with checked constructors and named errors, and trust typed internal contracts.
Domain absence is Option. Preserve historical source formats, missing/null
distinctions and hashes when changing a codec. Internal caches use full readonly
address records, tested with installed equality/hash and cancellation rules.

Enable the portable no-imperative-collections rule alongside the existing
rules; prove it through actual negative and valid Oxlint fixtures in app,
package, tests, tools and config paths. Document precise host operation/property
allowances, never a whole-file or wildcard mutation waiver. Keep the native API
request execution and cleanup and the one exact TanStack server runner. Templates
are examples qualified at their snapshot; research a v4 clone and reconcile with
installed source/types before applying them to another Effect version.

The generated Oxlint configuration enables native loader/client/cache ownership
and public API proxy checks. Its real-command fixtures prove forbidden wrappers
fail while native HTML loaders and Alchemy cache declarations pass. Configure a
checked-response rule only when the project has an actual format-checking helper;
the starter does not invent one. Follow the shared
[native request ownership policy](../strict-effect-ts/references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
when extending its API paths or loader owners.

name: docs-maintainer
description: Audit and edit repository documentation so material code, configuration, API, infrastructure, CI, operational, skill, and SPEC changes update the correct semantic owners in the same implementation slice. Use for documentation maintenance, docs audits, stale or contradictory READMEs, documentation-impact assessment during implementation, and PRD writing/review/closeout. Preserve just-in-time context, distinguish skills from runbooks and durable docs from dated proof, and provide claim-matched verification. Do not use for public copywriting alone or to copy mutable provider state into repository docs.
---

# Documentation Maintainer

Keep documentation aligned with repository behavior by updating the earliest
durable semantic owner and only the pointers that must lead to it.

## Establish the local contract

1. Read applicable `AGENTS.md`, inspect the worktree, and identify the exact
   change, repository, environment, and write authority. Do not infer authority
   to mutate providers, publish, release, or push from permission to edit docs.
2. Read the repository-local `docs-maintainer` profile completely when one is
   present at `references/repository-profile.md`. It owns repository paths,
   commands, generated-document boundaries, mirrors, exceptions, and archive
   policy. The global skill supplies method, never local truth.
3. If no local profile exists, derive a temporary impact map from the root
   `README*`, `docs/README*`, applicable package/app READMEs, active SPEC/tasks,
   configuration, and changed implementation. Record missing ownership as a
   gap; do not invent canonical paths or command names.
4. Select an execution mode:
   - **attached change:** when the user authorized implementation and repository
     edits, edit affected documentation and task artifacts in the same slice;
   - **audit or curator:** for scheduled/background freshness work, or when
     mutation authority is absent, produce an isolated report-only candidate
     with provenance and a proposed patch. Publication requires a separately
     named responsible owner and publisher identity.

Never let a curator publish its own uncorroborated findings or treat its prior
output as independent feedback. Pin any published context projection to an
immutable repository revision; refresh it only at a recorded phase boundary.

Keep these truth layers distinct and apply the strongest applicable precedence:
external system for current external state; shared store for shared source
material; immutable context projection for a recorded phase; repository code,
config, and Schemas for desired state; durable docs for explanation and routing;
dated evidence for observations; active SPEC/tasks for current intent and
execution. Link across layers instead of copying claims between them.

For a repository-wide documentation audit, substantial PRD, or cross-cutting
harness change, read
[repository-harness-contract.md](references/repository-harness-contract.md).
It routes to the complete local method and requires no external source lookup.
Load the applicable structured modules directly:

- [contract map](references/harness/contract-map.md) for mode and lifecycle;
- [invariant register](references/harness/invariant-register.md) for stable IDs;
- [context and ownership](references/harness/context-and-ownership.md) for truth
  layers, phased retrieval, and publication boundaries;
- [proof and evaluation](references/harness/proof-and-evaluation.md) for
  journeys, delivery, receipts, terminal states, and proportional evaluation;
- [operations and authority](references/harness/operations-and-authority.md)
  when runbooks, providers, controls, releases, or automation are in scope; and
- [repository variation](references/harness/repository-variation.md) when
  creating or changing the local profile.

Use the Schemas and templates under `assets/harness/` for repository profiles,
critical journeys, bounded receipts, authority envelopes, and feedback or
automation controls. Do not replace those fixed field contracts with free-form
prose.
For an ordinary localized documentation change, do not load that broader
contract unless an ownership, delivery, dependency, or proof question requires
it. This skill owns the documentation track; use the sibling `repo-structure`
skill for a complete repository audit.

## Load context in phases

Use just enough context to decide and then prove the change:

1. **Ground:** read the change, directly affected docs/READMEs, the docs router,
   the owning architecture or standard, and active task context.
2. **Investigate:** inspect code, config, generated owners, history, provider
   readback, or upstream material only to resolve an identified question.
3. **Land:** inventory all affected docs, READMEs, skills, runbooks, references,
   generated artifacts, indexes, and active/archive pointers. Reconcile every
   contradiction on an affected route before closeout.

Do not preload the whole repository for an ordinary localized change. A
repository-wide documentation audit or PRD review may require a full
`docs/**` and `README*` accounting under its owning skill.

For a repository-wide audit, return documentation findings in the stable
finding format owned by the repository-audit procedure: consequence,
evidence, semantic owner, root correction, duplicated guidance to retire,
affected surfaces, proof, authority, limitations, and non-claims. Separate
important corrections from optional improvements.

## Build the impact ledger

Read [document-classes.md](references/document-classes.md) to select semantic
owners and [change-impact.md](references/change-impact.md) for the trigger
matrix. For each surface, record `Change required`, `Preserve`, or `N/A`, with:

- changed behavior or claim;
- semantic owner and required pointers;
- exact affected path or narrowly bounded path set;
- lifecycle transition, if any;
- generated source and regeneration command, if applicable;
- verification and observable postcondition;
- proof location and explicit non-claims.

Cover docs, root/package/app READMEs, architecture/ADRs, standards, API and
generated references, runbooks, critical journeys, proof/evidence, skills and
agent instructions, lint/config/CI docs, migration/release notes, and active
SPEC/tasks. Never accept a generic “update docs” item.

## Edit the correct owner

- Put durable design, invariants, and boundaries in architecture or standards.
- Put exact repeatable operations in target-owned runbooks, including
  preconditions, authority, sequential steps, receipts, rollback, and
  escalation. Skills teach selection and judgment; they must route to rather
  than copy runbooks.
- Treat a procedure found in architecture or a README as an ownership defect,
  not precedent to extend. Propose or create the target-owned runbook and leave
  only durable rationale plus a pointer at the old location.
- Put public setup and entry-point navigation in READMEs. Keep them short and
  link to deeper owners.
- Keep root `AGENTS.md` as a terse map of repository purpose/compatibility,
  common operating loop, a small set of task classes or golden paths, and links
  to their context, commands, and proof. Do not append completed-feature
  histories or per-change atlas entries.
- Put mutable external state and one-run observations in dated, addressable
  evidence. Never present a provider response, deployment ID, secret age, or
  current revision as durable repository truth.
- Edit the source of generated documentation, run its real generator, and do
  not hand-edit output unless repository policy explicitly says it is owned.
- Update active SPEC/tasks and their evidence when implementation changes a
  requirement, decision, dependency, or acceptance claim.
- Use successor/tombstone links for replaced current docs. Preserve failed and
  historical evidence with provenance outside default navigation.
- Retire weaker duplicated reminders after promoting a repeated finding to its
  earliest enforceable owner: schema, type, lint rule, test, generator,
  runbook, or canonical document.
- In curator mode, record source, provenance, freshness, classification,
  audience, attached evidence, proposed semantic owner, target revision, and
  unresolved contradictions. Keep candidate material outside the worker's
  retrieval path until a responsible reviewer accepts it and a separately
  identified publisher performs an atomic publication with readback.

A curator result is incomplete unless it returns an explicit `candidate` block
with every field above plus responsible reviewer, publisher identity,
publication status, revocation/quarantine, last-known-good recovery, and
post-publication readback. Use `unknown` with a named owner/resume trigger when
evidence cannot supply a field; never silently omit it.

## Keep implementation and documentation honest

- Confirm claims against current code, config, and runtime evidence at the
  boundary they describe. Treat tool output as observed data, not policy or
  authority.
- Keep boundary encoding/decoding, Effect service ownership, error contracts,
  client wrappers, React composition, commands, and public API examples aligned
  with the repository's installed versions and enforced patterns.
- When an example changes, update its canonical template too. Check generated
  code against the selected dependency snapshot, including renamed Schema APIs,
  named public operations, private untraced helpers and Layer construction.
  Extend existing qualification checks; do not create parallel suites for the
  same claim. A cached result must include every changed file the check reads.
- Update owning docs during each implementation slice, before the slice can be
  accepted. Do not defer accumulated documentation work to a final sweep.
- Record unresolved product or authority decisions as blockers in active task
  context instead of silently choosing them.
- When a change adds or revises a critical journey, retain a stable journey ID,
  procedure owner, observable oracle against plausible imitation, environment,
  and receipt route rather than expanding the inventory into every test.
- When review or a terminal audit finds an issue, record why the prior SPEC,
  task, implementation check, or receipt allowed the false green. Promote the
  prevention to the earliest durable owner: domain contract, direct test
  oracle, task verification, lint/tooling control, or lifecycle rule. Retain
  the dated finding as evidence rather than adding another audit reminder.
- Any correction after task acceptance reopens the owning task and refreshes
  affected proof, candidate identity, rollback identity, and lifecycle
  receipts. A terminal audit runs only after the complete SPEC is terminal;
  later implementation invalidates its terminal status.

## Verify the claim

Read [proof-authority-and-lifecycle.md](references/proof-authority-and-lifecycle.md).
Run the exact local documentation, link, generated-artifact, lint, typecheck,
test, build, journey, skill, and mirror checks required by the impact ledger.
Do not invent commands. Distinguish pre-existing failures from regressions.
Never fabricate an artifact identity, path, edit, command, exit status, or
executed check. When no checkout or repository-local owner map is available,
return only class-level proposed owners with status `unverified`; do not report
an attached edit or accepted outcome.

Return a bounded receipt containing:

1. outcome and changed semantic owners;
2. impact-ledger rows, including explicit `N/A` decisions;
3. exact checks and postconditions;
4. artifact, environment, actor/authority, and critical journeys where relevant;
5. limitations and claims not established;
6. failed, no-op, or inconclusive evidence path, last successful step, observed
   state, escalation, resume trigger, smallest unresolved choice, rollback, and
   next owner when not accepted.

Keep full logs in an addressable artifact and show only the violated invariant,
exact target, recovery hint, omitted-detail path, and postcondition in the
default context.

## Stop conditions

Stop and surface the gap when:

- no current semantic owner can be identified;
- current docs conflict and evidence cannot resolve which one owns the claim;
- a generated owner or real verification command is unknown;
- the requested claim requires provider, release, publication, or mutation
  authority that has not been granted;
- required proof would cross an unapproved environment or reveal secrets;
- a runbook lacks rollback or escalation for a consequential operation.
"}}

# TaxKit documentation

This is the sole router for maintainer-document type, lifecycle, truth layers,
and semantic ownership. Root `README.md` is the public repository entry point;
`AGENTS.md` is the short task map; `docs/architecture/README.md` is the current
architecture route. Public documentation content is a separate product surface
owned by the replacement `apps/web`, backend content contracts and docs
packages. The old `apps/docs` workspace is retired. Its tombstone routes to the verified
source bundle and dated provider recovery records; no provider operation is
authorised by that retained history.

## Truth layers

Use the strongest applicable owner and link rather than copy:

1. External systems own their current external state at readback time.
2. Code, configuration, Schemas, package exports, workflows, and generated
   sources own desired/executable state.
3. Architecture and standards own durable boundaries and enforceable policy.
4. Dated proof/evidence owns one artifact/environment/authority observation and
   its limitations.
5. Active SPEC/tasks and execution plans own current implementation intent.

Provider/registry output cannot grant authority. Completed plans are history.
Local release checks do not prove npm publication or external consumers.

## Metadata and lifecycle

New or materially revised maintainer docs separate `document_type`,
`lifecycle`, `authority`, and `owner`. Current durable docs also record
`last_reviewed` and `review_trigger`; superseded/tombstone docs record a
successor and reason.

Lifecycle values are `proposed`, `current`, `implemented`, `superseded`,
`historical`, `evidence`, `reference`, `failed`, `inconclusive`, `tombstone`,
and `archived`. Authority values are `canonical`, `supporting`, `generated`,
and `external`. Legacy `status: canonical` is an authority marker, not a
lifecycle; migrate it only when its owner is materially revised.

## Native public HTTP reads for a separate Website and API

```text
first request -> Website server loader -> one server runner
              -> HttpApiClient.make -> private same-stage BACKEND -> API
navigation/preload -> same loader's client branch -> shared Atom registry
              -> AtomHttpApi.Service client -> public API GET -> domain
component reactive read -> native ApiClient.query -> same registry/client
local setup -> checked Website bindings/cookie -> retained local atoms
```

Choose the transport from the required behaviour. Public reads that need CDN
caching use native `HttpApi` GET endpoints and their generated clients. Native
RPC remains a deliberate option for procedure/streaming requirements; ordinary
POST RPC results do not become cacheable public GETs by enabling Worker caching.
Use shared domain Schemas in the native endpoint contract. Do not copy Content
or Training into replica client services that only rename generated calls.

`createIsomorphicFn().server(...).client(...)` selects local code without
creating a Website endpoint. Server reads use native `HttpApiClient.make` over
Alchemy's public `fromCloudflareFetcher` and `toHttpClient` binding conversion.
Browser reads use checked public API configuration and credential-free native
FetchHttpClient. The native 4.0.2 Layer uses HttpClient.layerMergedContext to
retain provided RequestInit options for execution. Use that existing Layer and
test actual outgoing options; do not add a policy wrapper without a demonstrated
requirement. Do not add `createServerFn`, a Website proxy, or backend routes
merely to read that API. Keep runtime imports in matching environment branches.

Native `AtomHttpApi.Service` accepts `runtime: browserRuntime.factory`; native
service runtimes then share the application factory and router/React registry.
The default factory is not a reason to forbid the native Service. Do not start
another application runner, registry or copied client lifecycle. Create one
browser registry before loaders run, provide that exact registry to React, and
close it at final unmount. The portable ownership rule allows AtomRegistry.make
only inside createLoaderRegistry at the configured browser owner. Isolated test
registries require exact registryTests paths ending in .test/.spec.ts or .tsx;
glob paths, another test file and production files do not gain permission.
Aliases and exported constructor references remain checked. Preserve development replay and pending-request
cleanup tests. SSR registries are isolated; no mutable module-global registry.

Use `baseUrl` when the checked API origin is fixed during construction. When
root configuration is retained in an Atom, use the native `httpClient(get)`
composition callback and native request mapping to read it. This callback is a
native configuration hook, not an owned Layer factory. Keep configuration atoms
alive for the registry lifetime and check configuration before client acquisition
when its named error must remain distinct. Local appearance/progress must not
wait on remote clients or an unrelated optional service.

TanStack owns route loading, preloading, freshness and serialisation. Loader-only
reads call the generated client directly; the sole browser Promise bridge runs
that request Effect using the same registry. Do not create a `pageLoaderAtom`
or another query cache for every route. Components owning reactive remote state
use native `ApiClient.query`; tools and loaders that need typed operational
errors can call the native client directly. In Effect 4.0.2 native query helpers
turn Schema/HttpClient failures into defects; test the actual path rather than
claiming every helper keeps those errors in its typed channel.

Keep failures typed inside Effect and translate once at the framework boundary
to native TanStack not-found/error handling. Plain successful values use native
TanStack serialisation. Convert only values requiring an explicit checked view;
do not add success/error envelopes, reply codecs or repeated Schema decoding
solely to serialise a plain successful result. A format-selected response still
needs one semantic variant check before promising a narrower type; its callers
must reuse that narrowing. Reuse API-owned finished downloads through a single
native binding request instead of refetching data and rebuilding the response.

Wrap the complete native call in `Effect.timeout` when the product needs a
request deadline. The operation includes body reading and Schema decoding.
In the qualified HttpClient, `transformResponse` surrounds response acquisition
(headers); in HttpApiClient/AtomHttpApi it surrounds body decoding after headers
have arrived. Timing either stage alone misses part of the complete request.
Choose the duration for the feature; ten or forty seconds are examples, not
framework requirements. Preserve earlier caller interruption, response cleanup,
native tagged errors and unrelated defects. Test late headers then a stalled
body with TestClock, invalid JSON/schema replies and final registry disposal.

Review every owned helper with the deletion test: would deleting it remove
complexity, or force meaningful policy into several callers? Delete pass-through
Layers/services/hooks, generic request factories, duplicated error conversions
and wrappers around native defaults. Keep checked host adapters, real feature
policy and one required runner. Local lint/build proof does not establish hosted
CORS, direct browser GETs, private binding startup or cache hits.

See the Alchemy [native public caching guide](../../../alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md#native-public-response-caching)
for response eligibility, version isolation and hosted cache evidence.

Use the portable [native request ownership checks](../enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
to reject recognised loader request state, generated-client replica services,
duplicate checked replies and Website data proxies. Configure real import and
owner paths and prove both valid native patterns and forbidden replacements
with the actual Oxlint command. Their local syntax coverage does not replace
review of opaque imports or runtime behaviour.

alchemy-iac/references/providers/cloudflare.md
## Native public response caching

First inspect the matching Alchemy repo, installed types and official
[Workers Cache guide](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/cache/). In the
qualified beta.81, use `yield* Cloudflare.cache({ crossVersionCache: false })`
in native Worker construction **before** a plan-only return, and
`cache: { enabled: true, crossVersionCache: false }` on `Website.Vite`.
These declare native version-scoped storage. They do not choose which application
responses are public or their freshness. Do not build an owned Cache API runtime,
cache-key framework, purge service or Alchemy provider patch.

Enable the portable [native Cloudflare cache rule](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
in the owned Cloudflare application paths to prevent a second global Cache API
runtime. Prove native declarations and backend Effect caches still pass. The
rule checks code ownership; hosted requests must separately prove reuse.

Choose response policy explicitly. For example, Common Practice uses seven-day
CDN freshness with browser `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` and
`Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-if-error=0`.
Seven days is that project's product decision; qualify the target's own duration.
Cloudflare owns [CDN header precedence](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cdn-cache-control/);
Alchemy's local Cache API shim is a different path and does not prove that edge
behaviour. Preserve the headers and qualify actual hosted reuse separately.
TanStack loader freshness is another choice (the starter uses one minute),
separate from browser HTTP reuse and native Worker cache freshness. Freshness
allows reuse; it does not guarantee retention for seven days or a HIT on every
request. Eviction, regions, new versions, request variants and private responses
can cause misses. Cache hits may skip Worker execution and its request analytics.

Cache only eligible public GET/HEAD responses. Preserve stricter Cache-Control,
CDN-Cache-Control and Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control instructions; private/no-store,
failures and Set-Cookie responses remain uncacheable. Preserve native status,
headers, cookies, body/stream and cancellation when adapting responses. Use a
small app-owned eligibility/header decision when needed; do not create an
independent caching library or parse durations that native storage already owns.

GET selection fields belong in the path/query, not a request body. Native clients
encode endpoint query fields and the URL distinguishes `format=data`, Markdown,
HTML and images. `Vary` supplies additional response variants: preserve API CORS
`Vary: Origin` and negotiated HTML `Vary: Accept`. Public HTML that changes with
a saved appearance can vary on Cookie only when the entire response remains
public; qualify the actual cached Light/Dark/Device first paint. Reject malformed
saved values with private responses. Unrelated cookies can reduce sharing; never
assume a Cookie variant makes user-specific content public.

With cross-version sharing disabled, a new Worker version starts a separate
cache. Include authored content in both API and Website native build/memo inputs,
and deploy them together so a content-only change refreshes JSON and HTML.
The stack coordinates deployment but activation is not atomic. Prove this with a
controlled Preview content change, both new version IDs and changed JSON/HTML;
restore the fixture before Production. Do not claim deployment invalidation from
a successful plan or one Worker's new version alone.

Hosted qualification consumes the first response and repeats the exact ordinary
URL/headers to observe `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` and Age. A first request after a
version change may be MISS. Inspect request `Cache-Control`/browser reload headers
and repeat them rather than assuming `no-cache` always bypasses native storage.
Do not add cache-busting queries or sleeps to force a passing test. Warm format,
Accept, Origin and Cookie variants in both orders; verify private/error/cookie
responses remain private and HEAD follows native semantics. Read back cache
options on both Workers and their current versions. A local image/render cache,
HTTP headers alone, or an internal service-binding call is not public edge-cache
proof. Keep local, deployment, provider, public URL and browser evidence separate.

## Native request ownership

Use these checks when the Website reads a separate public API. They live in the
same portable policy asset, not another plugin or custom request runtime.

| Rule                       | What it rejects                                                                                                                                                            | What stays valid                                                                                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-loader-request-state`  | Native request Atom/result-cache construction inside recognised TanStack loaders or exact loader owners; loader reads of locally inspectable configured-client query Atoms | Component query Atoms, local appearance/progress state, direct native client calls, configuration/service Atom reads |

## Native public response caching

First inspect the matching Alchemy repo, installed types and official
[Workers Cache guide](https://alchemy.run/cloudflare/compute/cache/). In the
qualified beta.81, use `yield* Cloudflare.cache({ crossVersionCache: false })`
in native Worker construction **before** a plan-only return, and
`cache: { enabled: true, crossVersionCache: false }` on `Website.Vite`.
These declare native version-scoped storage. They do not choose which application
responses are public or their freshness. Do not build an owned Cache API runtime,
cache-key framework, purge service or Alchemy provider patch.

Enable the portable [native Cloudflare cache rule](../../../strict-effect-ts/references/enforcement/lint-review-and-migration.md#native-request-ownership)
in the owned Cloudflare application paths to prevent a second global Cache API
runtime. Prove native declarations and backend Effect caches still pass. The
rule checks code ownership; hosted requests must separately prove reuse.

Choose response policy explicitly. For example, Common Practice uses seven-day
CDN freshness with browser `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` and
`Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800, stale-if-error=0`.
Seven days is that project's product decision; qualify the target's own duration.
Cloudflare owns [CDN header precedence](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cdn-cache-control/);
Alchemy's local Cache API shim is a different path and does not prove that edge
behaviour. Preserve the headers and qualify actual hosted reuse separately.
TanStack loader freshness is another choice (the starter uses one minute),
separate from browser HTTP reuse and native Worker cache freshness. Freshness
allows reuse; it does not guarantee retention for seven days or a HIT on every
request. Eviction, regions, new versions, request variants and private responses
can cause misses. Cache hits may skip Worker execution and its request analytics.

Cache only eligible public GET/HEAD responses. Preserve stricter Cache-Control,
CDN-Cache-Control and Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control instructions; private/no-store,
failures and Set-Cookie responses remain uncacheable. Preserve native status,
headers, cookies, body/stream and cancellation when adapting responses. Use a
small app-owned eligibility/header decision when needed; do not create an
independent caching library or parse durations that native storage already owns.

GET selection fields belong in the path/query, not a request body. Native clients
encode endpoint query fields and the URL distinguishes `format=data`, Markdown,
HTML and images. `Vary` supplies additional response variants: preserve API CORS
`Vary: Origin` and negotiated HTML `Vary: Accept`. Public HTML that changes with
a saved appearance can vary on Cookie only when the entire response remains
public; qualify the actual cached Light/Dark/Device first paint. Reject malformed
saved values with private responses. Unrelated cookies can reduce sharing; never
assume a Cookie variant makes user-specific content public.

With cross-version sharing disabled, a new Worker version starts a separate
cache. Include authored content in both API and Website native build/memo inputs,
and deploy them together so a content-only change refreshes JSON and HTML.
The stack coordinates deployment but activation is not atomic. Prove this with a
controlled Preview content change, both new version IDs and changed JSON/HTML;
restore the fixture before Production. Do not claim deployment invalidation from
a successful plan or one Worker's new version alone.

URL/headers to observe `CF-Cache-Status: HIT` and Age. A first request after a
version change may be MISS. Inspect request `Cache-Control`/browser reload headers

options on both Workers and their current versions. A local image/render cache,
HTTP headers alone, or an internal service-binding call is not public edge-cache
proof. Keep local, deployment, provider, public URL and browser evidence separate.

A service is the checked list of operations a caller can use. A Layer is a
recipe that supplies an implementation and its dependencies. Declaring a Layer
does not start it; the app builds it for the lifetime it needs.
Schema checks a value's shape and meaning; Config reads settings; Scope owns
when resources must be released. An Alchemy Output is a resource value that
Alchemy resolves during deployment or local development.

| Owner | Required design |
| --- | --- |
| Domain contracts and representations | Calculator/content owners keep the Schemas, branded identities and named expected errors. Decode external values once. Reuse whole-record checks as well as fields; encode when values leave the process or enter storage. Preserve meaningful missing/undefined distinctions with the existing Option codecs. Pure tax arithmetic and immutable mappings remain plain functions. |
| Public service methods | Named `Effect.fn("Service.operation")`, including test implementations. Acquire transport and fixed settings when building the service, so normal public operations need no extra service requirements. Short private pipelines stay plain functions; dependent private generators use `fnUntraced`. No generator or extra file just to wrap one step. |
| Static Layers | Replace `TaxKitRpcClientLive(origin)`, `DocsRpcClientLive(origin)`, `WebsiteServerLive(binding)` and the HTTP Layer factories with static Layer values. Caller-supplied checked inputs become named requirements supplied with native `Layer.succeed`; fixed host settings are read through checked Config in their owning Layer. Use native Layer replacement in tests. Do not introduce one address-only service per environment key, factory exceptions or another runtime. |
| Checked transport clients | Native generated clients stay private. HTTP and RPC expose the same semantic operations for matching capabilities. Keep distinct owners for content catalogue, discovery and Markdown operations: their current method lists differ. Do not merge unrelated capabilities merely to produce a matching table. |
| Native API host | Build shared services once in the Worker instance, keep each request's Scope and cancellation native, and keep streams in the consumer's Scope. Do not capture a request, event tracer or request Scope in an app-wide service. No ManagedRuntime around the native Worker. |
| Website host | Keep the existing one server runner and one browser Atom graph. Move raw Cloudflare reads into a separate live ingress Effect; select only Website-owned keys and use native `reifyBoundConfigProvider`. Do not feed the whole environment into Config or inspect Alchemy's protected markers manually. Keep the original private binding object and its existing checked capability contract. |
| Frontend calls | Routes restore checked transport values; containers own commands and cancellation; leaves render checked values. Server/browser runtimes are imported inside the corresponding TanStack environment function. Preserve root Atom registrations and initial values. Check the actual browser bundle when changing ownership; a filename or import rule alone does not prove its contents. |
| Failure handling | Expected failures use the named error channel. Unexpected bugs and caller cancellation retain their identity until the host handles them. Do not convert every Cause into an unavailable result. Native HTTP mapping still owns missing-route, abort and server-failure responses. |

Two current reply adapters need correction. The private RPC buffer in
`apps/api/src/worker.application.ts` catches every Cause and returns 503; the MCP
buffer in `apps/api/src/mcp-response.boundary.ts` preserves interruption but
hides other unexpected defects. Recover only the named body-read, size and
deadline failures those adapters own. Pass cancellation and unexpected defects
to native handling with a safe reporter.

That does not mean removing every `catchCause`. Website host loaders and the
in-process HTTP adapter deliberately use native `HttpServerError.causeResponse`
to map the host response. Keep that narrow use. The current RPC client also
correctly marks only failure inside the native reply decoder and translates
that marker into its invalid-response error; unrelated Schema defects stay
unchanged. Recheck that native codec behaviour when upgrading Effect.

At the API boundary, provide the checked `ErrorReporter.CurrentErrorReporters`
to the outer native `safeHttpEffect` mapper. A reporter supplied only inside a
route does not prevent the host's raw-Cause fallback. Capture only that reporter
set, preserve the incoming request Scope, and keep its required synchronous
callback to fixed safe fields with an empty Cause. No extra runner, ambient
clock, raw error dump or request-wide Layer wrapper. This is part of safe host
composition, even while exported logs and traces remain off.

The existing ten-second complete-reply limit, 2 MiB response cap, request limit,
manual retry and per-operation RPC acquisition remain. A static service Layer
does not require an app-wide RPC receive loop. Keep that loop inside each call's
closing Scope; the shared capacity pool belongs to the app instead.

Read fixed API settings while building the runtime application after the native
`ALCHEMY_PHASE === "plan"` check. Alchemy supplies resolved bindings and builds
that application on the first real event, before its handler, then reuses a
successful build. Put address-dependent provided Layers after that check too;
a check inside an Effect already wrapped in `Effect.provide` is too late for
those Layers. Preserve binding/RPC/telemetry/secret registration during the
planning phase, with explicit native env declarations where reads are skipped.
Use the native bundled runtime guard for deployment-only settings; no copied
host is needed. Keep invalid-setting failures typed and preserve the intended
safe client response at the host.

TaxKit's current cached Config reads once on first use. It does not reread and
decode settings on every request, and that extra delay is not required by the
native host. Moving it into application acquisition is a composition change,
not a reason to remove startup checks or guess planning addresses.

For calculator access, keep the existing narrow `PublicCalculatorService`
contract used by the local SDK. Define a domain-owned `CalculatorAccess`
contract from that existing operation map, reusing each request/result type and
adding the owning access-error family to each operation's local errors. Move
the shared access-error Schemas to calculators, retaining legacy encoded RPC
tags and re-exports. Reduced revision-four replies cannot recover detail that
the backend deliberately omitted.

A static alias Layer at the calculator owner publishes the final checked local
service object under `CalculatorAccess`. Compose it only after admission,
capacity and analytics in the API app. Publishing it from the base live Layer
could let access callers bypass those policies. HTTP and RPC publish their own
checked implementation under the access tag; an old compatible tag can point
to that same object. Native `Layer.effectContext` and `Context.add` are present
in both installed 4.0.0 and matching 4.0.2. No forwarding methods, second runtime
or duplicated nine-operation declaration is needed. The SDK still uses its
narrow local contract.

Name the underlying public calculator and engine operations, not only their
bounded wrappers. The local SDK currently misses the canonical operation names.
Named operations do not authorise exporting their arguments, reports or
calculation traces.

Correct CORS independently of exported tracing. The current Website RPC clients
disable native tracing at execution and acquisition, and the README calls this
CORS containment. The current Alchemy skill expressly rejects disabling tracing
to avoid preflight. Remove that workaround, retain named operations, and admit
the actual native `b3` and `traceparent` headers alongside TaxKit's content and
collection-policy headers. Keep the selected checked Origin policy and test
the real outgoing request/preflight. Header propagation enables no exporter;
exported trace and platform trace channels stay off. Native HTTP spans can carry
URLs and, in older versions, headers even without explicit annotations, so the
safe-field policy still applies to any future collection.

The public HTTP helper replacement is now agreed. Current exports include
`createTaxKitApiClient`, `withTaxKitHttpApiClient`,
`createTaxKitApiClientLayer` and their old aliases, and public examples use them.
The strict skill rejects raw clients, generic callbacks and Layer factories;
its static-Layer rule has no factory exception. On 10 October 2026 Cooper chose
to replace those helpers with checked named operations and fixed Layers, update
examples in the same package change and record it in a Changeset. Existing callers must
update; there is no temporary raw-client or Layer-factory compatibility path.
This records the design choice; the package code has not yet changed.

The Layer change also covers public `TakeHomeScenarioLiveFromInput` and
`AnnualTaxScenarioLiveFromInput`, used by calculator composition and package
consumers. Keep their checked scenario inputs and tax behaviour, but migrate
callable Layer helper signatures through normal package/versioning work. Do not
claim every helper signature can stay unchanged while enforcing no factories.

## Lint that enforces the design
exports or supported dependencies. Keep local emulator tests separate from
provider-mutating integration tests; Common Practice's live integration tests
are opt-in. Do not run the whole native suite after every wording change, nor
turn a failed meaningful runtime check into a passing result by dropping its
assertion or increasing its timeout without understanding the failure.

Normal Changesets still describe public package contract changes. The existing
fixed version group is a packaging choice, not a deployment approval system;
this change does not need to redesign it. Drop per-run versioning authority
receipts and requirements to version private infrastructure for ordinary app
work. No package contract changes in this document-only edit need a Changeset.

Earlier local checks passed 162 focused tax cases and the SDK packed/downstream
checks. Full verification did not establish a clean result: native emulator
startup/cancellation/development cases timed out. A subsequent run was
interrupted without a confirmed final result. The current document review
passes docs and runbook checks; its full repository check stops in
`tools/quality-workflow/release-boundary.test.ts`, where thirteen temporary
fixture installs fail with a temp-directory permission error under the available
Bun 1.4.0. That run does not reach or establish application qualification.
These results are recorded here, without new receipt files or a successful
deployment claim. Meaningful native emulator failures still need investigation
during the application change.

## Remaining corrections and sequence

| Priority | Change and owning paths |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Replace Cloudflare deployment/secret/command ceremony with the native workflow above. Update the actual instructions and current docs in the same change, including the older active clean-slate plan. |
| 2 | Settle the native-address/preserved-behaviour choice above, redesign `packages/infrastructure/src/apps-stack.ts`, replace shared `www` rules with Website handling, and check the unpatched native graph. Remove all Alchemy patch references. |
| 3 | Apply the strict Effect corrections above: static Layers, final shared access contract, selected-key native Config, request-owned RPC lifetime, native CORS headers and safe outer error reporting. Replace the old public HTTP helpers and update examples, as agreed. Migrate Website loaders/root registry through the focused owner map above; preserve wire compatibility or settle a normal RPC contract change explicitly. |
| 4 | Move Cloudflare header interpretation from `packages/api/rpc/src/rate-identity.boundary.ts` into the API/Website host ingress. Keep the checked host-neutral identity contract. |
| 5 | Adopt the current portable lint asset under `tools/oxlint`, useful TaxKit extensions and real-project strict Effect diagnostics. Adapt manifest-aware imports for nested packages and retain actual-CLI fixtures. |
| 6 | Fix Bun's shared service lifetime at application composition, preserving its HTTP API and the host-independent packages. |
| Later | Add safe operational records through the existing native Axiom/Cloudflare declarations. Keep unsafe native channels off; Cloudflare's native metrics are distinct from exported logs/traces. |

No new generic utilities, second docs renderer, duplicated service facade or
permanent audit system is needed. Preserve tax rules/facts, encoded public
errors and HTTP statuses, RPC revision, MCP sessions, package names/subpaths and
SDK behaviour, subject only to the explicit compatibility choices below.

Public HTTP helper replacement is the agreed compatibility change;
they must not be confused with unchanged tax inputs/results. The native-address
alternative also needs a stated discovery/MCP contract decision before it can
claim to preserve those interfaces.

Matching upstream clones: Effect tag `effect@4.0.2`, commit
`269a7c864351231d42e6e95b7fa8f32050df3691`; Alchemy tag `v2.0.0-beta.81`, commit
`e73c66857553a5abe045e1a66b5512cf7d39ef2e`. Consulted owners include Effect

The deeper comparison also reads Effect `Layer.ts`, `Context.ts`, `Config.ts`,
`http/HttpClient.ts`, `http/HttpServerError.ts`, `rpc/RpcClient.ts` and
`ai/McpServer.ts`; Alchemy `Runtime.ts`, `Platform.ts`, `RuntimeContext.ts`,
`Output.ts`, `Apply.ts`, `Http.ts`, `Cloudflare/Workers/Fetch.ts` and

No dependency, publishing, privacy or browser-access change follows merely from

# Common Practice foundation review plan

The [proposal](../../product-specs/common-practice-foundation-review.md) records
the source comparison and Cooper's direction: Common Practice's app/client and
ordinary operational approach, Cloudflare first, patch-free Alchemy, supported
Bun host, and safe operational details only. This remains design work; no runtime
or provider change has been made.

Completed research covers the full Website/HTTP/RPC/MCP/SDK call paths, current
Common Practice workflows and native secrets, upstream Effect/Alchemy support,
package/export differences, and the tools that enforce TaxKit's extra ceremony.
The deeper strict Effect review adds static Layer ownership, a shared checked
access contract after all calculation policies, selected-key native Config,
request cancellation/defect handling, safe native reporting, actual CORS headers
and current portable lint rules. The 11 October comparison adds Common Practice's
implemented Website RPC loading and merged canonical guidance at
`cf8269dc983f5fbb4683a019f92f8b3995f7ff36`. Published 0.6.11 remains the confirmed
release; locally generated 0.7.0 is not a published-version claim.
The new audit packet has been removed and its useful findings folded into the
proposal. No implementation acceptance crosswalk or new receipt is required.

## Implementation order

| Order | Work | Meaningful check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Replace receipt/approval/custody/epoch tooling and instructions with normal commits, checks, native Alchemy and Doppler. Wire current Cloudflare preview/production workflows. | Commands select the intended stage; forks receive no secrets; preview deploy/cleanup cannot overlap; ordinary checks run without old receipt files. |
| 2 | Settle the Website-address choice; redesign the native graph and replace shared redirect rules with native aliases and Website handling. Remove all Alchemy patch entries/files and align the chosen published dependency graph. Keep local state isolated. | Frozen unpatched install; native create/update/no-op planning, local addresses and Website/API calls; selected Origin/trusted key policy; redirect behaviour including static files and unchanged unrelated zone rules. |
| 3 | Adopt static Layers, the shared checked access contract and native selected-key Config. Keep RPC acquisition scoped to each operation. Replace old public HTTP helpers with named checked operations/static Layers and update examples, as agreed. Move Cloudflare headers to host ingress; correct CORS and native safe reporting. | No access path bypasses calculation policies; complete reply deadline/byte cap, cancellation and defects, repeated requests, no-JavaScript form, real browser headers, safe errors/logs and supported package contracts. |
| 3a | Follow the proposal's Website loader owner map: local server/browser branches, private same-stage server RPC, direct public browser RPC, local root settings and retained catalogue/configuration atoms. Move the existing browser runtime to its canonical owner; create its registry before loaders and share it with React. Remove generated page/settings/search wrappers and their ingress headers/allowlist. | Full first HTML and metadata; hydration and navigation/preload behaviour; idle settings retention; request interruption without closing another caller's services; development replay/final cleanup; existing form, Markdown/discovery and machine-client compatibility. |
| 4 | Adopt current portable lint at its code owner, including the merged Website RPC rule, useful TaxKit extensions and strict Effect diagnostics over real projects. Make import rules aware of nested manifests; remove duplicated checks and copied executable skill assets. | Actual lint rejects server-function aliases/re-exports, alternate data clients, proxies and extra runtimes; accepts intended HTTP work, adapters/exports and nested package paths; real app/tool/root Effect diagnostics run. |
| 5 | Fix Bun application-wide calculation pool using the same host-neutral services. Keep current HTTP coverage. | Overlapping requests share eight places; five-second work limit and existing HTTP behaviour remain. |
| Later | Introduce fixed safe operational fields through native Axiom/Cloudflare resources using the agreed existing datasets. | No salaries/facts/results/traces, raw URLs/bodies/errors or unsafe native channel exports. |

Keep each code change coherent and reversible with Git. Use focused tests for
its actual behaviour and one ordinary verification command. Public package
contract changes use normal Changesets and actual packed/downstream checks.
The previous native emulator timeout failures remain unresolved; do not declare
the new graph working until meaningful runtime checks pass.

Cooper agreed on 10 October 2026 to replace public raw-client/Layer-factory HTTP
helpers, with callers/examples updated together and no temporary compatibility
path. The Website-address choice remains open: preserve current behaviour with
a stated exception, or remove that reverse dependency. Common Practice uses
public Origin policies and fixed Production canonical discovery links; moving
discovery construction to Website is a separate TaxKit alternative. Common
Practice's API catalogue endpoints still use each stage's API address. No address
exception, Effect MCP patch or discovery-policy change is assumed while that
answer is pending.

The Website RPC loading pattern can be designed without choosing that access
policy. Keep one server `runtime`, one client `browserRuntime` and the same
browser registry for router loaders and React. Root configuration stays local;
catalogue/page/search remain remote checked operations. Add neither a Website
RPC proxy nor another Atom runtime. Reconcile native NDJSON guidance with
TaxKit's existing JSON framing and machine clients before changing the public
wire contract. Keep current router freshness explicit rather than silently
adopting Common Practice's 60-second policy.

Static Layers also change exported scenario helper signatures. Use normal
Changesets and update callers together, preserving the checked tax inputs and
results. There is no silent factory allowance in the new shared rule.

Update current architecture, runbooks, root instructions, skill profiles and the
older clean-slate plan as their implementation changes. History stops being an
executable prerequisite. Do not create a replacement receipt system under a
new name. Redeploy a previous working revision for operational rollback through
the same native workflow.

unchanged. Recheck that native codec behaviour when upgrading Effect.

At the API boundary, provide the checked `ErrorReporter.CurrentErrorReporters`
to the outer native `safeHttpEffect` mapper. A reporter supplied only inside a
route does not prevent the host's raw-Cause fallback. Capture only that reporter
set, preserve the incoming request Scope, and keep its required synchronous
callback to fixed safe fields with an empty Cause. No extra runner, ambient
clock, raw error dump or request-wide Layer wrapper. This is part of safe host
composition, even while exported logs and traces remain off.

The existing ten-second complete-reply limit, 2 MiB response cap, request limit,
manual retry and per-operation RPC acquisition remain. A static service Layer
does not require an app-wide RPC receive loop. Keep that loop inside each call's
closing Scope; the shared capacity pool belongs to the app instead.

Read fixed API settings while building the runtime application after the native
`ALCHEMY_PHASE === "plan"` check. Alchemy supplies resolved bindings and builds
that application on the first real event, before its handler, then reuses a
successful build. Put address-dependent provided Layers after that check too;
a check inside an Effect already wrapped in `Effect.provide` is too late for
those Layers. Preserve binding/RPC/telemetry/secret registration during the
planning phase, with explicit native env declarations where reads are skipped.
Use the native bundled runtime guard for deployment-only settings; no copied
host is needed. Keep invalid-setting failures typed and preserve the intended
safe client response at the host.

TaxKit's current cached Config reads once on first use. It does not reread and
decode settings on every request, and that extra delay is not required by the
native host. Moving it into application acquisition is a composition change,
not a reason to remove startup checks or guess planning addresses.

For calculator access, keep the existing narrow `PublicCalculatorService`
contract used by the local SDK. Define a domain-owned `CalculatorAccess`
